contenido: This Group consists of Concepts which relate to, the extraction and/or excavation of natural resources, the processing, fabrication and/or manufacturing of items, the devices and structures used in agriculture, utilities and their networks to include electric power, communications of any kind and waste management and all associated industries and services Concepts.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which relate to the extraction of raw materials and the excavation of soil.

objetos.definicion: An excavation drilled into the ground for purposes other than the extraction of potable water, oil, gas or brine.
objetos.descripcion: For example, drilled to support the underground testing of munitions, for coring or sampling of bedrock or ice for scientific purposes, or drilled for the injection of waste material.

objetos.definicion: A location of entrance and/or exit.
objetos.descripcion: For example, a cave mouth or a doorway.

objetos.definicion: A mechanical device for removing materials from the ground.
objetos.descripcion: For example, a dredger, a powershovel, and a dragline.

objetos.definicion: An excavation made in the terrain for the purpose of extracting and/or exploiting natural resources.
An area where the presence of recoverable petroleum, oil, and/or natural gas has been identified.
objetos.descripcion: The field can exist regardless of current exploitation activities.

objetos.definicion: A man-made heap of material(s) of unspecified nature.

A structure over a vertical mine shaft containing machinery (for example: a winding head or hoist) used to transport minerals, equipment, and/or workers between the surface and various levels within the mine.
objetos.descripcion: It is usually the most prominent structure at a shaft mining facility.
objetos.aliases: Mine Shaft Headframe, Mine Shaft Headgear, Pit-head Frame

objetos.definicion: An area, place, site or deposit, of which little may be known, except that specific minerals or rocks, that are considered to be valuable or that are of scientific or technical interest, have been identified and recorded.
objetos.descripcion: The minerals may be solid, liquid or gaseous.

objetos.definicion: A man-made heap of mining or quarrying products that does not contain waste materials.
objetos.descripcion: For example, a pile of coal or quarried stones.

objetos.definicion: An artificial structure that is located offshore.
objetos.descripcion: It usually has a surface that is raised above the sea and may be used as a working stage for conducting offshore operations (for example: drilling for petroleum and/or natural gas, loading and/or unloading vessels, or navigation support).

objetos.definicion: An open-air excavation created by removal of stone by blasting or cutting.
A superstructure fitted for drilling or lifting operations for extraction and/or exploitation of natural resources.
The wall of the excavation within a quarry or extraction mine.
A large storage structure used for storing loose materials.
An excavation where gravel, sand, and/or clay are removed for use elsewhere.
objetos.descripcion: For example, a gravel pit or a sandpit.

objetos.definicion: An underground geological formation that is used to store materials, especially liquids and/or gases.
objetos.descripcion: The formation may be either natural (for example: a depleted oil reservoir), man-made for other purposes (for example: an abandoned mine), or intentionally engineered for the purpose of storage (for example: a hard rock cavern). Packaged (for example: in drums or on pallets) or bulk (for example: coal or grain) materials may also be stored.

objetos.definicion: A region undermined through mining activities that has already partly subsided or that is in the process of subsiding.
A wheel, one portion of which is immersed in water, that consists of vanes or cells and rotates on a supporting framework.
objetos.descripcion: It is used either to convert the energy of flowing water to the rotation of its shaft in order to power equipment (for example: a grindstone) or to use energy from an outside power source in order to transport water from a lower level to a higher level (for example: from an irrigation canal to an irrigation ditch).

objetos.definicion: An excavation drilled or dug into the ground (for example: the sea bed) for the extraction of liquids and/or gases.
Equipment used to maintain control of a well.
objetos.descripcion: For example, casing heads, lowermost and intermediate tubing heads, Christmas tree equipment with valves and fittings, and casing and tubing hangers. Included are oil, gas, water, and/or brine wells.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which relate to the production and/or processing of materials.

objetos.definicion: A basin, usually artificial, in which air is mixed with partially treated wastewater.
objetos.descripcion: The water is treated with microorganisms to consume organic materials and convert suspended solids to settleable solids that are later collected by a settling pond and removed as sludge.

objetos.definicion: A site and associated buildings used for the purpose of combining manufactured parts to make a completed product.
A smelting furnace in which a blast of air is used, especially one for iron-smelting using a compressed hot air blast.
Utilities or pipeline network that is located underground or below a waterbody.
objetos.descripcion: For example, cables transmitting electrical power and/or communication signals and pipes carrying liquids, slurries, or gases.

objetos.definicion: A device in which the separation of petroleum is carried out in the presence of a catalyst.
A tall tower for cooling hot water from an industrial process before reuse.

An open area that is open to the sky and surrounded by walls or buildings forming the precincts of a larger facility (for example: an extended house, a castle, or a homestead), often in the form of an area that is enclosed by a single building.
objetos.descripcion: Historically, these areas in inns and public buildings were often the primary meeting places for some purposes, leading to the other meanings of the term 'court'.

objetos.definicion: A structure over which brine trickles and is concentrated through increased evaporation.
A facility involved in the production or distribution of petroleum, oil and/or natural gas products.

A structure used in material processing that employs heating to harden (for example: to fire brick or ceramic), pyrolyse (for example: convert coal to coke, or limestone to lime), burn (for example: to incinerate waste), or dry (for example: lumber).
objetos.descripcion: May assume many forms, for example a domed 'beehive' kiln or a long linear coke oven battery.

objetos.definicion: An industrial facility consisting of buildings and related structures that are tenanted by multiple manufacturing (for example: industrial equipment manufacture or materials processing) and/or service businesses (for example: auto repair or residential contractors) requiring significant equipment and/or materials, and sharing common access to adjacent transport facilities.
objetos.descripcion: Heavy industrial parks have tenants that are involved in industries where a significant tonnage of raw materials and/or finished products are shipped and more than one transport mode (for example: road, railway, aerodrome, canal, or navigable river) is available. Light industrial parks have tenants that may be involved in manufacturing and/or services; for example: small electrical appliance manufacture or repair.

objetos.definicion: The structures, grounds, and equipment of a manufacturing facility.
objetos.descripcion: Includes, for example, structures in engineering such as docks and bridges.

objetos.definicion: A man-made heap of material(s) of unspecified nature.
A facility including one or more buildings used for processing materials.
objetos.descripcion: For example, a treatment plant.

objetos.definicion: A small reservoir where solid matter is precipitated from a liquid by evaporating or settling.
An operational area with buildings and other facilities for the purification of wastewater.
A large enclosed area adjoining the sea or a major river, including facilities in which ships are built or repaired.
A large storage structure used for storing loose materials.
A tract for the treatment of water that consists of a bed of material where water is aerated or filtered.
An establishment for storing, purifying, and supplying an area or town with water.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which are associated with agriculture.
subcategorias.descripcion: Describes concepts that relate to the function of agriculture such associated buildings and equipment as opposed to Subgroup 06.01, which describes the land use itself.

objetos.definicion: A tract of land set aside for agricultural settlement.
A global land-use zone based on a predominant form and type of plant cultivation.
objetos.descripcion: Agricultural zones extend across areas of similar latitude and often reflect climatic zones.

objetos.definicion: A facility involved in the culturing or farming (including harvesting) of aquatic organisms (for example: fish, mollusks, crustaceans, plants, crocodiles, alligators or amphibians) using techniques designed to increase the production of the organisms in question beyond the natural capacity of the environment (for example: regular stocking, feeding and protection from predators).
objetos.descripcion: Culturing or farming refers to the rearing of individuals up to their juvenile and/or adult phase under captive conditions. In addition, it also encompasses individual, corporate or state ownership of the individual organisms throughout the rearing or culture stage, up to and including harvesting.

objetos.definicion: A roofed farm building designed for sheltering harvested crops (for example: hay), livestock (for example: cattle), and/or farm machinery (for example: tractors and plows).
A small artificial pond used for immersing cattle in chemically treated water for disease control.
An elevated irrigation system revolving around a central pivot point.
An artificial waterway with no flow, or a controlled flow, usually unlined, used for draining or irrigating land.
A man-made open container holding water for animals to drink.
An unenclosed road or trail, due to the regular movement of animal herds.
objetos.descripcion: Chiefly for cattle and/or sheep.

objetos.definicion: A tract of land, including buildings and structures, whose primary use is the production of food (for example: crops or livestock).
objetos.descripcion: A farm can be a holding of any size from a few dozen to many thousands of acres, and may be specialized to particular forms of food production, for example: a truck farm where primarily vegetables are grown, an orchard where tree fruit and/or nuts are grown, a vineyard where grapes are grown, and a ranch where livestock are raised on the range. A large farm or estate operating on the plantation economy model is termed an 'industrial farm' or 'plantation'.

objetos.definicion: A man-made barrier of relatively light structure used as an enclosure or boundary.
objetos.descripcion: Similar structures that are constructed of heavy materials (for example: stone, rock or masonry) are classified as walls.

objetos.definicion: A facility involved in the breeding (hatching and associated activities) and cultivation (raising for release or harvesting) of fish in tanks or landlocked enclosures.
objetos.descripcion: Fish species raised on fish farms include, for example, salmon, catfish, tilapia, cod, carp, and trout.

objetos.definicion: A tall structure, equipped for loading, unloading, processing, and/or storing grain.
An enclosed container, used for storing grain or fodder.

A structure, sometimes recognized as a building, constructed primarily of transparent material (for example: glass or plastic), in which temperature and humidity can be controlled for the cultivation and/or protection of plants.
objetos.descripcion: Greenhouses can range in size from very large conservatories such as the Palm House at Kew Gardens in England to row covers. Many of the large public greenhouse conservatories are used for growing tender and rare plants. Commercial greenhouses are often state-of-the-art production facilities for vegetables or flowers. Row covers and similar structures are usually made of a lightweight transparent material placed directly above rows of crops on a supporting framework to form a low tunnel. The transparent materials on these structures may be temporary being removed once the crop is well-established. At times, the entire structure may be removed.

objetos.definicion: An enclosed tract on which livestock are temporarily kept.
objetos.descripcion: For example, a sheepfold, a holding paddock, a livestock pen, a feedlot, and/or a stock yard. The enclosure may be by, for example, a fence or a wall.

objetos.definicion: An area used for the cultivation of vegetables, fruits and/or flowers as well as for the raising of cultivated plants.

An estate or large farm operating on the plantation economy model in which the farm operates as a single economic unit whose operations are based on agricultural mass production of a few staple crops (for example: cotton, tobacco, sugar cane, bananas, and/or rubber) that are typically not indigenous to the region.
objetos.descripcion: Plantation economies are often dependent on distant (for example: export) markets as the crops are harvested in large quantities. Historically, industrial farms were often found in former European colonies and termed 'plantations'.

objetos.definicion: A system for supplying land with water, usually by a network of channels or pipes.
objetos.descripcion: In addition to a source of water (for example: a stream or a well), the network may include pumps, reservoirs, controls (for example: gates or valves), timing devices, and drains.

objetos.definicion: A tract of vegetation that is being exploited for lumber resources.

A site where marine organisms are cultivated for food and other products in either the open ocean, in an enclosed section of the ocean, or in tanks, ponds or raceways that are filled with seawater (for example: the farming of marine fish, prawns, or oysters in saltwater ponds).
A man-made heap of material(s) of unspecified nature.
A tract of land, including buildings and structures, whose primary use is the grazing of livestock on large, mostly unimproved, lands that are otherwise unsuitable for farming (for example: arid).
objetos.descripcion: The natural vegetation of the grazing area is usually dominated by native grasses, grass-like plants, forbs, and shrubs, but may include native or adapted introduced species that are managed like native vegetation. Ranches may be of nearly any size and if the ranch includes arable or irrigated land, the ranch may also engage in raising crops, especially hay and feed grains.

objetos.definicion: A small building, generally of light construction, that usually has one or more open sides.
objetos.descripcion: Typically used for storage.

objetos.definicion: A large storage structure used for storing loose materials.
An area within which the upper soil horizons have become enriched in salts to a sufficient degree to result in loss in agricultural productivity.
objetos.descripcion: The enrichment may be due to either natural processes and/or human activity.

objetos.definicion: A building similar to a barn and adapted for the shelter and feeding of domestic animals, being divided into individual stalls.
objetos.descripcion: Although commonly used to house horses, it may be used to house other animals (for example: prize cattle, sheep or goats) and often includes a storage loft (for example: for hay).

objetos.definicion: An excavation drilled or dug into the ground (for example: the sea bed) for the extraction of liquids and/or gases.
A tower and associated equipment that generates electrical power from wind.
A system of vanes attached to a tower and driven by wind (excluding wind turbines).

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which relate to the production, transportation and distribution of energy, whereas energy is mostly electricity.
subcategorias.descripcion: Mechanical energy production, for example, does not fit in this Subgroup.

objetos.definicion: A modeling entity collecting information regarding the electrical power available at an aerodrome.
Utilities or pipeline network that is located underground or below a waterbody.
objetos.descripcion: For example, cables transmitting electrical power and/or communication signals and pipes carrying liquids, slurries, or gases.

objetos.definicion: A territorial region within which electric power production, consumption and/or distribution is managed.
A facility including one or more buildings and equipment used for electric power generation.
objetos.descripcion: An electric power station consists of one or more power generating units, each consisting of the full set of equipment required to generate power and capable of independent operation. The power generating units are located on one or more contiguous or adjacent properties, are under the common control of the same entity and supply power through a common connection to the electric grid. Electric power stations most commonly are used to generate electricity for long distance transmission.

objetos.definicion: A modeling entity collecting information about aircraft ground power equipment at an aerodrome.
objetos.descripcion: This equipment is either located on a trailer and towed or is self-propelled and driven to the aircraft. Ground power equipment does not include aircraft electrical and air start (a power source is used to provide the initial rotation to start an engine).

objetos.definicion: A facility for the generation of thermal energy for heating purposes.
A man-made heap of material(s) of unspecified nature.
An apparatus or structure in which fissile material can be made to undergo a controlled, self-sustaining nuclear reaction with the consequent release of energy.
objetos.descripcion: The nuclear reactor may be contained within a power plant.

objetos.definicion: A building-like structure intended to create a barrier against the release of radioactivity generated during nuclear power operations.
objetos.descripcion: The structure is usually heavily reinforced. It houses equipment used to manage a self-sustaining nuclear reaction of fissile material. The consequent release of energy may be used to generate electricity, as in a power plant.

objetos.definicion: A full set of equipment, capable of independent operation, used to generate power at a power station.
objetos.descripcion: In the case of electric power generation it includes all equipment up to the high-voltage terminal of the generator step-up transformer (IEEE 762). In the case of a steam electric power generating unit, it consists of individual boilers, any installed emission control equipment, and any steam turbine/generators dedicated to generating electricity. All combustion units/boilers/combined cycle turbines that produce steam for use in a single steam turbine/generator unit are part of the same electric power generating unit.

objetos.definicion: A cable that transmits or distributes electrical power.
objetos.descripcion: Long distance power transmission lines are typically operated at high voltages (for example, 500 kilovolts) whereas local power distribution lines are typically operated at much lower voltages (usually less than one kilovolt).

objetos.definicion: A pylon that supports one or more power lines.
objetos.descripcion: May occasionally also support communication lines, but usually only in the case of low voltage power distribution (typically less than one kilovolt).

objetos.definicion: A facility, along a power transmission line, in which electric current is switched, transformed, and/or converted.
An extensive collection of solar panels that are collocated and serve a common purpose (for example: the generation of electricity or the generation of heating steam and/or water).
objetos.descripcion: The collection is often organized as an array covering many hundreds of square metres in area and it may be controlled so as to track the direction of the sun throughout the day.

objetos.definicion: A panel designed to absorb the sun's rays for the purpose of generating electricity or heat.
A structure that uses a water wheel or turbine to drive a mechanical process (for example: grinding grain into flour, cutting timber into lumber, or stripping bark from trees for use in tanning).
objetos.descripcion: A water mill that only generates electricity is more usually termed a 'hydroelectric plant'.

objetos.definicion: A collection of windmotors that are collocated and are organized as a single power generation unit.
A tower and associated equipment that generates electrical power from wind.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which relate to any kind of communication.

objetos.definicion: A device that is used for emitting and/or sensing electromagnetic energy.
objetos.descripcion: For example, used to transmit and/or receive electronic signals as on a radio tower or to capture electromagnetic energy as in radio astronomy.

objetos.definicion: A collection of aerials that are collocated and serve a common purpose.
objetos.descripcion: They may be organized either to function as a single larger virtual device (for example: a phased array) or function relatively independently of each other (for example: pointed in different directions and operating at different frequencies as at a satellite communication ground station).

objetos.definicion: Utilities or pipeline network that is located underground or below a waterbody.
objetos.descripcion: For example, cables transmitting electrical power and/or communication signals and pipes carrying liquids, slurries, or gases.

objetos.definicion: A single continuous rope-like bundle consisting of multiple strands.
objetos.descripcion: The strands may be individually insulated and/or protected and the cable as a whole sheathed. Cables may be used for load bearing (for example, supporting or suspending equipment and/or structures), transmitting electrical power, and/or communicating signals (for example, by electrical or optical means).

objetos.definicion: A cable that transmits communication signals.
objetos.descripcion: For example, a telephone line, a telegraph line, or a fibreoptic cable.

objetos.definicion: A pylon that supports one or more communication lines.
objetos.descripcion: Often multi-purpose, supporting communication lines of different types (for example: telephone and television). May occasionally also support power lines, but usually only in the case of low voltage power distribution (typically less than one kilovolt). For example, a telephone pole.

objetos.definicion: A facility in which communication signals are processed and/or controlled.
objetos.descripcion: For example, a telephone switching station, a microwave repeater station, a satellite ground station, cellular telephone equipment, and a land-line telephone repeater station.

objetos.definicion: A tower used to support an aerial for transmitting and/or receiving electronic communication signals.
A concave-shaped aerial that is used for emitting and/or sensing electromagnetic energy.
objetos.descripcion: For example, used to transmit and/or receive electronic signals as at a satellite station or to capture electromagnetic energy as in radio astronomy.

objetos.definicion: A territorial region within which telecommunications (for example: provisioning of services, assignment of telephone numbers) are managed.
objetos.descripcion: Traditionally these regions are established in accordance with landline-based principles.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which support Concepts stored in the other industrial and services Group (01).

objetos.definicion: A basin, usually artificial, in which air is mixed with partially treated wastewater.
objetos.descripcion: The water is treated with microorganisms to consume organic materials and convert suspended solids to settleable solids that are later collected by a settling pond and removed as sludge.

objetos.definicion: A pylon supporting an aerial cable.
objetos.descripcion: For example, a ski lift pylon.

objetos.definicion: Utilities or pipeline network that is located underground or below a waterbody.
objetos.descripcion: For example, cables transmitting electrical power and/or communication signals and pipes carrying liquids, slurries, or gases.

objetos.definicion: A single continuous rope-like bundle consisting of multiple strands.
objetos.descripcion: The strands may be individually insulated and/or protected and the cable as a whole sheathed. Cables may be used for load bearing (for example, supporting or suspending equipment and/or structures), transmitting electrical power, and/or communicating signals (for example, by electrical or optical means).

objetos.definicion: A suspended transportation system consisting of one or more load cables, supporting pylons, carrier units (for example: cars or buckets intended to transport people, material, and/or equipment) and usually stations.
objetos.descripcion: A cableway consists of carrier units attached to load cables which are strung between pylons and/or stations. For example, a ski-lift.

objetos.definicion: A device in which the separation of petroleum is carried out in the presence of a catalyst.
A small artificial pond used for immersing cattle in chemically treated water for disease control.
A device for conveying articles or materials from one location to another during manufacture or processing using a continuously moving mechanism.
objetos.descripcion: Usually long, thin, and rectangular, and located above ground surface. It can be situated horizontally, vertically, at a slope between flat and upright, or in a combination of these postures. In general, conveyor systems consist of the bucket, screw (auger), apron, or flight conveyors to load silos or bunkers. Other systems use a series of rollers to move a range of products from relatively lightweight luggage and cargo packages at transportation terminals, up to heavyweight plate steel and ingots in industrial mills. The most common system is the belt conveyor. Some systems use a combination of these designs such as shallow buckets (or flat plates) attached to a belt conveyor. Conveyors can be used for long distance transportation (ifor example, kilometres) of materials. Long distance conveyor systems are usually constructed in segments to accommodate changes in direction where needed.

objetos.definicion: A facility for the removal of thermal energy (for example: by generating and circulating chilled water) for cooling purposes.
A tall tower for cooling hot water from an industrial process before reuse.
Equipment for lifting, shifting, and lowering objects or materials by means of a swinging boom or with the lifting apparatus supported on an overhead track.
A prepared or reserved site on land for the collection and/or deposition of waste, refuse or discarded material.
objetos.aliases: Refuse Tip, Slag Heap, Waste Pile

objetos.definicion: A facility including one or more buildings and equipment used for electric power generation.
objetos.descripcion: An electric power station consists of one or more power generating units, each consisting of the full set of equipment required to generate power and capable of independent operation. The power generating units are located on one or more contiguous or adjacent properties, are under the common control of the same entity and supply power through a common connection to the electric grid. Electric power stations most commonly are used to generate electricity for long distance transmission.

objetos.definicion: A structure wherein aircraft or rocket engines are tested.
objetos.descripcion: The most common test cells are used for testing the performance characteristics of jet engines and are typically located at military aerodromes or aerospace research and development facilities. Test cells for liquid-fueled rocket booster engines are unique, massive structures (for example: the test cell located at Stennis Space Flight Center in the U.S.).

objetos.definicion: A mechanical device for removing materials from the ground.
objetos.descripcion: For example, a dredger, a powershovel, and a dragline.

objetos.definicion: An open-ended pipe at which waste gases are burned.
A permanent vertical structure normally used for the disposal of waste or by-products from petro-chemical production by burning.

A permanent raised structure used to support equipment (for example: cranes, signal lights, or signs) while spanning over or around an object (for example: over a road or railroad, or around a ship hull or rocket).
objetos.descripcion: A gantry may be moveable (for example: a rocket gantry may be repositioned away from the launch pad when pre-launch preparations are complete). A 'scaffold' is a structure that may be similar in appearance but is assembled only for temporary use (for example: during external repair of a building).

objetos.definicion: A top-loaded funnel-shaped structure for temporary holding of loose material which will be dispensed from its bottom.
A permanent structure used for the disposal of waste products by burning.
Equipment located at or below water level where liquids (for example: cooling water) are spread out.
A tall pole or other slender structure set upright for any purpose.
A building-like structure intended to create a barrier against the release of radioactivity generated during nuclear power operations.
objetos.descripcion: The structure is usually heavily reinforced. It houses equipment used to manage a self-sustaining nuclear reaction of fissile material. The consequent release of energy may be used to generate electricity, as in a power plant.

objetos.definicion: A connected set of pipes for conveying liquids, slurries, or gases.
objetos.descripcion: Usually for long distances and often located underground.

objetos.definicion: A facility, along a power transmission line, in which electric current is switched, transformed, and/or converted.
A facility to move solids, liquids or gases by means of pressure or suction.
A pylon or pole used to support one or more cables.
A site engaged in the wrecking, dismantling, storage, recycling, and/or disposal of discarded or scrap products.
objetos.descripcion: For example, a wrecking yard or a scrap yard.

objetos.definicion: A superstructure fitted for drilling or lifting operations for extraction and/or exploitation of natural resources.
A small reservoir where solid matter is precipitated from a liquid by evaporating or settling.
The wall of the excavation within a quarry or extraction mine.
A mechanical device consisting of three poles bolted together at their upper ends and extended below, carrying tackle for raising heavy weights or machinery.
A vertical structure containing a passage or flue for discharging smoke and gases of combustion.
A collector opening into a pipe or channel to allow the removal of excess runoff water or in some cases sewage.
objetos.descripcion: In civil engineering terms, a drop inlet.

objetos.definicion: A site for the testing of technical products and equipment.
A removable cover or plate which provides access to underground utility tunnels, distribution lines, or drainage systems.
objetos.descripcion: For example, a manhole cover.

objetos.definicion: A tower-like structure associated with a dam or water source and used for the intake of water.
An excavation drilled or dug into the ground (for example: the sea bed) for the extraction of liquids and/or gases.
Equipment used to maintain control of a well.
objetos.descripcion: For example, casing heads, lowermost and intermediate tubing heads, Christmas tree equipment with valves and fittings, and casing and tubing hangers. Included are oil, gas, water, and/or brine wells.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which are used to store, provide and to protect any kind of goods.

objetos.definicion: Utilities or pipeline network that is located underground or below a waterbody.
objetos.descripcion: For example, cables transmitting electrical power and/or communication signals and pipes carrying liquids, slurries, or gases.

objetos.definicion: A tall structure, equipped for loading, unloading, processing, and/or storing grain.
An enclosed container, used for storing grain or fodder.
A top-loaded funnel-shaped structure for temporary holding of loose material which will be dispensed from its bottom.
A man-made heap of material(s) of unspecified nature.
A man-made heap of mining or quarrying products that does not contain waste materials.
objetos.descripcion: For example, a pile of coal or quarried stones.

objetos.definicion: A shaft sunk into the ground to reach and tap a supply of liquids and/or gases other than water intended for use in agriculture or domestic consumption.
objetos.descripcion: Typically drilled to tap underground reservoirs of hydrocarbons (for example: petroleum or natural gas). May also, for example, yield geothermally heated liquids for use in power generation or heating, or brine for use in the extraction of salt.

objetos.definicion: A designated, multi-level, structure used for parking and/or storing vehicles.
objetos.descripcion: May be present as part of a building or as a separate structure.

objetos.definicion: A vertical shaft that provides access to an underground aqueduct and which is part of a qanat system.
objetos.descripcion: A qanat system consists a system of deep underground tunnels especially constructed to channel water from an uphill region to a dryer lower region for use (for example: a village, a garden, a crop land), and qanat shafts to provide access from the surface to the underground tunnels.

objetos.definicion: A substantial lake-like body of water impounded by a dam.
objetos.descripcion: May be used for flood control and/or as a source of water for irrigation, industrial processes, and/or human consumption.

objetos.definicion: A small building, generally of light construction, that usually has one or more open sides.
objetos.descripcion: Typically used for storage.

objetos.definicion: A moveable container used for the shipping of solid, liquid, or gaseous materials.
objetos.descripcion: The container may be either closed on all sides or open on the top or along a side. With minor modifications, if needed, shipping containers may be used for non-traditional purposes including, for example: emergency shelter, housing, retail activities, warehousing and secure space.

objetos.definicion: A large storage structure used for storing loose materials.
A mobile storage unit to hold material (for example: missiles).
objetos.descripcion: For example, a drum or a can.

objetos.definicion: A tract used for the storage of products and/or supplies.
A container used for the storage of liquids and/or gases that is not supported by a tower.
A surface structure that may be covered and/or surrounded with earth and is resistant to ordnance.
objetos.descripcion: Used, for example, for storage and/or aircraft protection.

objetos.definicion: A tract of land occupied by large-capacity tanks in which petroleum, natural gas, or liquid petrochemicals are stored.
objetos.descripcion: The tanks are usually round, constructed from metal plates, and separated from each other by berms intended to contain any leakage.

objetos.definicion: An open tract for the storage of wooden lumber and timbers.
A complex of buildings, associated facilities, roads, and adapted areas used for transshipment of freight between the same or different kinds of transport.
An underground geological formation that is used to store materials, especially liquids and/or gases.
objetos.descripcion: The formation may be either natural (for example: a depleted oil reservoir), man-made for other purposes (for example: an abandoned mine), or intentionally engineered for the purpose of storage (for example: a hard rock cavern). Packaged (for example: in drums or on pallets) or bulk (for example: coal or grain) materials may also be stored.

objetos.definicion: A tract used for storing and/or parking vehicles (for example: recreational vehicles) and/or vessels.
objetos.aliases: Vehicle Storage Area, Parking Area, Car Park, Boat Park

objetos.definicion: A tower supporting an elevated storage tank of water.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which relate to the collection, storage, processing or recycling of waste.

objetos.definicion: An excavation drilled into the ground for purposes other than the extraction of potable water, oil, gas or brine.
objetos.descripcion: For example, drilled to support the underground testing of munitions, for coring or sampling of bedrock or ice for scientific purposes, or drilled for the injection of waste material.

objetos.definicion: Utilities or pipeline network that is located underground or below a waterbody.
objetos.descripcion: For example, cables transmitting electrical power and/or communication signals and pipes carrying liquids, slurries, or gases.

objetos.definicion: An area within which refuse has been dumped on land or sunk (legally or illegally) in the sea and has resulted in environmental endangerment.
A prepared or reserved site on land for the collection and/or deposition of waste, refuse or discarded material.
objetos.aliases: Refuse Tip, Slag Heap, Waste Pile

objetos.definicion: A sea area where dredged material or other potentially more harmful material (for example: explosives or chemical waste) is deliberately deposited.
An open-ended pipe at which waste gases are burned.
A permanent vertical structure normally used for the disposal of waste or by-products from petro-chemical production by burning.
A permanent structure used for the disposal of waste products by burning.
A man-made heap of material(s) of unspecified nature.
The location where there occurs a regulated discharge of pollutants (for example: from a pipe or a man-made ditch) into ground or surface waters.
objetos.descripcion: Pollutants include dredged spoil, solid waste, incinerator residue, sewage, garbage, sewage sludge, munitions, chemical wastes, biological materials, radioactive materials, heat, wrecked or discarded equipment, rock, sand, cellar dirt and industrial, municipal, and agricultural waste discharged into water. In the United States, permits for pollutant discharge are issued by the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), and such discharges are monitored and legal limits enforced.

objetos.definicion: A site engaged in the wrecking, dismantling, storage, recycling, and/or disposal of discarded or scrap products.
objetos.descripcion: For example, a wrecking yard or a scrap yard.

objetos.definicion: A small reservoir where solid matter is precipitated from a liquid by evaporating or settling.
A large storage structure used for storing loose materials.
An area where heaped material (for example: waste or spoil) is deposited.
objetos.descripcion: Waste heaps may be located at disposal sites or in unsanctioned and unprepared locations where illegal dumping takes place. Illegal dumping sites are usually composed of materials produced in the immediately surrounding area; for example, in a residential neighborhood their content would principally be household trash. Illegal dumping sites have no associated structures or facilities.

objetos.definicion: A facility where waste is processed through chemical, physical, biological, and/or thermal procedures.
A tract for the treatment of water that consists of a bed of material where water is aerated or filtered.

contenido: This Group consists of Concepts which relate in the broadest sense to the habitation of people and aspects of population.
descripcion: To this Group belong the domains of administration, trade, leisure, education and science.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which relate to settlements and buildings.

objetos.definicion: A site where remains of past civilizations or human activity have been discovered.
A large outdoor board for advertisements.
objetos.descripcion: May be attached to another structure or self-supporting. Usually elevated so as to be seen for a significant distance.

objetos.definicion: A free-standing self-supporting construction that is roofed, usually walled, and is intended for human occupancy (for example: a place of work or recreation) and/or habitation.
objetos.descripcion: For example, a dormitory, a bank, and a restaurant.

objetos.definicion: A canopy or ledge attached to the front of a building and protruding beyond the perimeter wall.
A supplemental portion of a building which rises from the roof but is not considered to be a portion of the roof.
A tract containing a concentration of buildings and/or other structures.
An encampment where tents and/or other easily moveable structures (for example: yurts) serve as full-time, temporary, or seasonal residences.
A prepared site, typically including facilities, used for holiday accommodations where caravans and/or motor homes are parked.
objetos.descripcion: Caravans are travel trailers towed behind vehicles while motor homes are self-contained vehicles used for both travel and accommodations. Facilities may include utility connections (for example: water, power, or gas), convenience store(s), showers, laundry facilities, and swimming pools.

objetos.definicion: A single large fortified building that has thick walls, battlements, and often the presence of a moat, and is commonly of some historical significance.
objetos.descripcion: Historically castles were designed and constructed as defensive structures situated so as to dominate the surrounding countryside. With advancing technology, especially artillery, they have become obsolete for military defensive purposes and are now valued primarily for their historical significance. In more recent times elaborate country houses were built incorporating many design elements of a castle but which were not fully capable of being used as defensive structures. Examples of castles of both types include Doue-la-Fontaine and Neuschwanstein.

objetos.definicion: A dwelling built in the recesses of cliffs.
A camp providing shelter for Internally Displaced Persons (IDP), refugees and evacuees (DPRE).
objetos.descripcion: IDPs, refugees and evacuees are defined separately in AAP-6(2007).

objetos.definicion: A relatively permanent structure, roofed and usually walled and designed for some particular use.
A farm, especially a country house with out-buildings attached, that is closed to the street by a gate or by a vertical building with a gate in it.
A site containing one or more historical and/or culturally significant buildings and/or other structures.
An area within which an infectious disease is endemic.
A site maintained for the public and declared to be of national or provincial historical significance and/or interest.
A large and imposing house with many rooms, and often of architectural significance, which is located on a large rural estate.
objetos.descripcion: The term 'Manor House' covers a range of buildings from relatively modest rectories up to the largest and grandest country houses termed 'stately homes'. Titular names of manor houses frequently carry a suffix such as 'House', 'Manor(s)', 'Tower(s)', 'Hall', 'Park', 'Grange', 'Court', or 'Palace'. Historically, manor houses were residences for the landed gentry or the very wealthy. Although this still applicable today, many are used for different functions such as museums, hotels, amusement, hospitals, religious activities, and schools. A lack of fortification features distinguishes a manor house from a castle. The estate surrounding a manor house is typically at least several square kilometres in extent, often with a garden in the immediate vicinity of the house and a larger park beyond for aesthetic, recreational, and/or agricultural purposes.

objetos.definicion: A site for the semi-permanent parking of manufactured homes used as dwellings and designed without a permanent foundation.
objetos.descripcion: Manufactured homes are prefabricated homes built in factories, rather than on-site, and then taken to the place where they will be occupied. They are usually transported by tractor-trailers over public roads to sites which are often in rural areas or high-density developments. While these houses are usually placed in one location and left there permanently, they do retain the ability to be moved as this is a requirement in many areas. Behind the cosmetic work fitted at installation to hide the base, there are strong trailer frames, axles, wheels and tow-hitches.

objetos.definicion: A named area where people live and/or work.
objetos.descripcion: For example, a city, a town, and a village.

objetos.definicion: The deteriorated remains of an unspecified structure.
A continuously occupied concentration of tents or lightweight fixed structures (for example: huts) serving as residences.
objetos.descripcion: May also include supporting non-residential (for example: commercial) structures.

objetos.definicion: A boundary or limit beyond which human settlement is either not possible or not appropriate for climatic or topographic reasons.
objetos.descripcion: This limit separates the ecumene (land where people have made their permanent home, and all work areas that are considered occupied and used for agricultural or any other economic purposes) from the uninhabited world.

objetos.definicion: A section of a built-up area consisting chiefly of densely packed shacks and having few, if any, streets and no public facilities.
objetos.descripcion: Usually located on the outskirts of the built-up area. The shacks are generally crude, improvised, and made from salvaged materials.

objetos.definicion: A concentration of simple dwellings, which are generally huts, that are usually not of substantial construction.
Underground living quarters.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which are associated with settlements or related to an urban area.

objetos.definicion: A covered pedestrian route composed of arches and pillars, usually open along one or both sides.
A location that is marked or designated as a meeting or an assembly point for a specific purpose (for example: evacuation) for specific individuals.
An outdoor band-stand in the form of a large concave shell with special acoustical properties.
objetos.descripcion: It typically has a concave, nearly hemispherical back serving as a sounding board. A band-stand is a platform or other structure for the use of a band of musicians.

objetos.definicion: A roofed farm building designed for sheltering harvested crops (for example: hay), livestock (for example: cattle), and/or farm machinery (for example: tractors and plows).
A long hard seat for two or more persons.
objetos.descripcion: May be backless and attached to, or adjacent to, a picnic table.

objetos.definicion: A large outdoor board for advertisements.
objetos.descripcion: May be attached to another structure or self-supporting. Usually elevated so as to be seen for a significant distance.

objetos.definicion: A structure, mounted on a pedestal, composed of an upright member with a shorter horizontal member centered at approximately two-thirds of the height of the upright member.
An area containing military quarters.
objetos.descripcion: Typically consisting of the residential sections of a military installation, where tactical training may be limited due to other activities that would endanger and disrupt personnel and their dependents.

objetos.definicion: A fortified complex of buildings and related structures that consists principally of a central keep with surrounding thick walls, battlements, and often the presence of a moat, and is commonly of some historical significance.
objetos.descripcion: A castle complex may be quite extensive, including multiple distinct buildings of diverse function. Historically castle complexes were designed and constructed as defensive structures situated so as to dominate the surrounding countryside. With advancing technology, especially artillery, they have become obsolete for military defensive purposes and are now valued primarily for their historical significance. Examples of castle complexes include Prague and Windsor Castles.

objetos.definicion: A site and associated structures devoted to the burial of the dead.
A tower used to support an aerial for transmitting and/or receiving electronic communication signals.

An open area that is open to the sky and surrounded by walls or buildings forming the precincts of a larger facility (for example: an extended house, a castle, or a homestead), often in the form of an area that is enclosed by a single building.
objetos.descripcion: Historically, these areas in inns and public buildings were often the primary meeting places for some purposes, leading to the other meanings of the term 'court'.

objetos.definicion: An area that is protected (for example: designated as World Heritage Site) because of its cultural (for example: historical) importance.
objetos.descripcion: For example, the Dresden Elbe Valley.

objetos.definicion: A tube or passageway associated with a culvert which carries a watercourse (for example: a stream, a sewer, or a drain) under a route (for example: a road, a railway, or an embankment).
objetos.descripcion: Usually the construction of the route is unaffected.

objetos.definicion: A border of concrete, asphalt or stone forming part of a gutter along the edge of a street or road.
An upright panel or similar structure used to convey visual information.
A location of entrance and/or exit.
objetos.descripcion: For example, a cave mouth or a doorway.

objetos.definicion: A man-made barrier of relatively light structure used as an enclosure or boundary.
objetos.descripcion: Similar structures that are constructed of heavy materials (for example: stone, rock or masonry) are classified as walls.

objetos.definicion: An apparatus for drawing water directly from a main, especially alongside a street or road, consisting of a pipe with one or more nozzles or spouts, to which a hose of a fire-engine may be attached.
A staff or pole on which a flag is raised.
A building that is specifically designed or reinforced to provide for defense from armed attack.
A monumental and/or ornamental structure containing moving water, often including jets, falls, or other decorative features.
objetos.descripcion: The structure is often of a civic nature; the water is typically recirculated.

objetos.definicion: A site where a human corpse is buried.
objetos.descripcion: It normally contains a single human corpse, however in some cultures servants and/or animals are buried with the deceased. The site is usually marked.

objetos.definicion: A marker indicating an individual grave site.
objetos.descripcion: Often located at a cemetery.

objetos.definicion: A structure intended for short term occupancy to protect personnel from injury.
objetos.descripcion: For example, a slit trench or other excavation either open or covered by sandbags, fill, or other material and supported by logs or other framing. May be more elaborate with many of the characteristics of an underground bunker.

objetos.definicion: A small, simple free-standing (detached) self-contained residence usually having only a single multi-function room.
objetos.descripcion: May be intended only as temporary (for example: by displaced persons) or seasonal (for example: during seasonal livestock movement) residence. May be crude (for example: quickly built from locally-available natural materials) or relatively modern in construction and austerely furnished (for example: a Norwegian 'hytte').

objetos.definicion: A structure serving as a support for one or more lights.
objetos.descripcion: For example, a light standard or a lamp post.

objetos.definicion: A distinctive structure on or off a coast exhibiting a major light designed to serve as an aid to navigation.
A large and imposing house with many rooms, and often of architectural significance, which is located on a large rural estate.
objetos.descripcion: The term 'Manor House' covers a range of buildings from relatively modest rectories up to the largest and grandest country houses termed 'stately homes'. Titular names of manor houses frequently carry a suffix such as 'House', 'Manor(s)', 'Tower(s)', 'Hall', 'Park', 'Grange', 'Court', or 'Palace'. Historically, manor houses were residences for the landed gentry or the very wealthy. Although this still applicable today, many are used for different functions such as museums, hotels, amusement, hospitals, religious activities, and schools. A lack of fortification features distinguishes a manor house from a castle. The estate surrounding a manor house is typically at least several square kilometres in extent, often with a garden in the immediate vicinity of the house and a larger park beyond for aesthetic, recreational, and/or agricultural purposes.

objetos.definicion: A grave containing multiple, usually unidentified, human corpses.
objetos.descripcion: Mass graves may be created after a large number of people die or are killed due to a natural disaster, disease, epidemic, warfare or criminal activity. Mass grave sites may not be marked, as in cases where they have been created to conceal genocide.

objetos.definicion: A marker erected and/or maintained as a memorial to a person and/or event.
A tower that is used for purposes other than communication.
objetos.descripcion: For example, for observation, support, and/or storage.

objetos.definicion: An elevated or suspended bridge-like structure providing pedestrian passage.
objetos.descripcion: For example, may be used to cross a strreet, a waterbody, or an interior floor space.

objetos.definicion: A designated, multi-level, structure used for parking and/or storing vehicles.
objetos.descripcion: May be present as part of a building or as a separate structure.

objetos.definicion: A table used for picnics.
objetos.descripcion: Often includes attached benches for seating.

objetos.definicion: A container for growing or displaying plants, usually decorative and permanent.
An open site that serves as a public meeting location in a built-up area.
A facility at which passengers may board and alight from trains and/or rail-transported freight may be loaded or unloaded.
A facility, building, structure or site that was designed and designated to be used for religious activities.
objetos.descripcion: In addition to worship (conducted in, for example: churches, mosques, temples, synagogues and other places of worship), religious activities include the preparation of individuals for religious service (in a religious community, for example: a convent or a monastery) as well as conducting funeral services and holding retreats.

objetos.definicion: A facility that is intended to be used for research and/or scientific purposes.
objetos.descripcion: For example, an astronomic observatory with facilities like dish aerials, buildings and infrastructure.

objetos.definicion: A small structure that stands alone, and is designated for the purpose of supplying a product (for example: souvenirs, magazines, snacks or refreshments) or service (for example: a shoe shine) to passers-by.
objetos.descripcion: It may be roofed (for example: a newspaper stand along the side of a city street or the attendant's booth in a parking lot or at a taxi cab stand), covered by an awning (for example: a cellular phone booth in the center of the promenade of a shopping mall or a hot dog stand on a city sidewalk), or unroofed. Although often semi-permanent in nature it may be wheeled and portable on a seasonal basis or more frequently as business conditions warrant.

objetos.definicion: A sign used to designate the name and/or identifying number of a road.
objetos.descripcion: The sign may also display an emblem used to designate the road type (for example: national, interstate, or local).

objetos.definicion: A large outdoor board for publicly displaying the score in an athletic event.
objetos.descripcion: Usually associated with a sports stadium or major playing field.

objetos.definicion: A small building, generally of light construction, that usually has one or more open sides.
objetos.descripcion: Typically used for storage.

objetos.definicion: A paved or improved pedestrian path, typically located adjacent and parallel to a street or road.
A series of fixed steps leading from one level to another, especially such a series leading from one floor level to another inside a structure.
objetos.descripcion: The steps may also be on the outside of the structure, for example, on a gasometer.

objetos.definicion: A geographic area characterized by statistically derived and/or aggregated properties (for example: population age profile, distribution of land uses, probability of types of events).
objetos.descripcion: These areas may be characterized by statistics in one or both of the following ways: (1) delineation of the area, wholly or partially, on a statistical basis (for example: a population threshold is applied, as for a Census Tract); (2) a statistical description of the area is developed (for example: age and gender statistics; economic statistics; or natural hazard occurrences within the area). Special constraints may be applied, such as: (a) the value of one or more statistical parameters is the same throughout the area, and different from adjacent areas; (b) the value of some statistical parameter(s) falls within a range that applies throughout the area.

objetos.definicion: An architectural support or base for a statue.
A structure, usually topped by a point, that may be erected on the roof of a building.
A lamp intended to illuminate a road.
objetos.descripcion: May also illuminate the ground adjacent to the road. Usually attached to a tall pole.

objetos.definicion: A sign placed along a road for the purpose of regulating the flow of traffic (for example: vehicles and/or pedestrians) and/or providing information.
A structure within which a corpse is entombed.
objetos.descripcion: It is often a building-like structure that may be partly or wholly underground (except for its entrance), but may be a simple enclosure cut into solid rock (for example: into a cliff face or inside of a cave). It may contain a single corpse or a related group (for example: a family) may be entombed together.

objetos.definicion: A relatively tall, narrow structure that may either stand alone or may form part of another structure.
objetos.descripcion: Usually of a square, circular, or rectangular cross-section.

objetos.definicion: A set of automatic lights (usually red, amber, and green) for controlling road traffic, especially at a road intersection.
objetos.descripcion: Usually attached to tall poles or suspended from overhead cables.

objetos.definicion: A solid man-made barrier of generally heavy material used as an enclosure, boundary, or for protection.
A tower supporting an elevated storage tank of water.
A shaft sunk into the ground to reach and tap a supply of water intended for uses other than power generation, heating or the extraction of minerals.
objetos.descripcion: May be, for example, drilled to tap deep underground reservoirs or dug to reach a shallow water table. Dug wells are typically circular, lined with masonry, have a stone border and a structure built above then for lowering and raising a bucket.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which relate to trade and/or economy.
subcategorias.descripcion: This varies from local shops to Concepts describing global economy issues.

objetos.definicion: A large outdoor board for advertisements.
objetos.descripcion: May be attached to another structure or self-supporting. Usually elevated so as to be seen for a significant distance.

objetos.definicion: An open area that is open to the sky and surrounded by walls or buildings forming the precincts of a larger facility (for example: an extended house, a castle, or a homestead), often in the form of an area that is enclosed by a single building.
objetos.descripcion: Historically, these areas in inns and public buildings were often the primary meeting places for some purposes, leading to the other meanings of the term 'court'.

objetos.definicion: An area that has been developed to perform a specific principal function, consisting of one or more vertical constructions (for example: structures or buildings), horizontal constructions (for example: pavements, roads, rail tracks, or bridges), and/or supporting utilities (for example: power lines, water supply, or sewerage), plus the underlying land.
objetos.descripcion: For example, an industrial plant consisting of building(s), shipping dock(s), storage area(s), power transformer(s), heating and/or cooling equipment, vehicle parking, roads, railroad tracks, and perimeter fences and gates.

objetos.definicion: An area on a water body bottom established to simulate a natural reef and intended to enhance fishery resources and commercial and/or recreational fishing opportunities.
objetos.descripcion: The haven (reef) is constructed by dumping (or emplacing) assorted scrap materials (or artificial structures) in areas which may be of very small extent or may stretch a considerable distance along a depth contour.

objetos.definicion: An industrial facility consisting of buildings and related structures that are tenanted by multiple manufacturing (for example: industrial equipment manufacture or materials processing) and/or service businesses (for example: auto repair or residential contractors) requiring significant equipment and/or materials, and sharing common access to adjacent transport facilities.
objetos.descripcion: Heavy industrial parks have tenants that are involved in industries where a significant tonnage of raw materials and/or finished products are shipped and more than one transport mode (for example: road, railway, aerodrome, canal, or navigable river) is available. Light industrial parks have tenants that may be involved in manufacturing and/or services; for example: small electrical appliance manufacture or repair.

objetos.definicion: A grouping of facilities, located in the same vicinity, which support particular functions.

A free-standing self-supporting construction (for example: a large piece of equipment) designed to support human activities (for example: agriculture, manufacturing, or mining) but not intended for human occupancy and/or habitation (for example: a house, a bank, an office, or a stadium).
objetos.descripcion: May have only limited protection from the weather (for example: a hayrick) and often composed of components specialized for a particular activity (for example: animal feeding, material storage, or traffic control) or process (for example: chemical reaction, heating, mixing, or physical shaping). For example, a cane press, a cement mill, a cotton gin, a distillation tower, and a rock crusher.

objetos.definicion: A commercial facility consisting of multiple office buildings tenanted by one or more non-retail businesses (for example: corporate management, consulting services, or research and development) and supportive businesses (for example: a restaurant serving mid-day meals or a post office) that share a common park-like setting consisting of landscaping (for example: lawns, ornamental plantings, or ponds), parking facilities, and common entrances from adjacent roads.
objetos.descripcion: May also include commercial tenants involved in light industry (for example: gem cutting or specialized electronics manufacture).

objetos.definicion: A small structure that stands alone, and is designated for the purpose of supplying a product (for example: souvenirs, magazines, snacks or refreshments) or service (for example: a shoe shine) to passers-by.
objetos.descripcion: It may be roofed (for example: a newspaper stand along the side of a city street or the attendant's booth in a parking lot or at a taxi cab stand), covered by an awning (for example: a cellular phone booth in the center of the promenade of a shopping mall or a hot dog stand on a city sidewalk), or unroofed. Although often semi-permanent in nature it may be wheeled and portable on a seasonal basis or more frequently as business conditions warrant.

objetos.definicion: A commercial facility tenanted by multiple retail stores (for example: household goods, clothing, or books), restaurants (for example: a food court), entertainment venues (for example: a movie theatre or electronic games arcade), and/or other businesses (for example: professional services), that is completely enclosed, climate controlled, has a common public arcade (for example: furnished with decorative plantings, benches, and/or fountains) and a common vehicle parking area (for example: a parking lot or parking garage).
objetos.descripcion: When the commercial entrances open onto the interior of the complex (public access being by means of central entries and broad corridors) it may consist of multiple levels connected by escalators and is often termed a 'shopping mall'. When the commercial entrances open towards the exterior of the complex and access to individual commercial entrances is directly from an adjacent vehicle parking area it consists of a single level and is often termed a 'shopping centre' or 'shopping plaza'.
objetos.aliases: Shopping Centre, Shopping Plaza, Shopping Mall

objetos.definicion: A geographic area characterized by statistically derived and/or aggregated properties (for example: population age profile, distribution of land uses, probability of types of events).
objetos.descripcion: These areas may be characterized by statistics in one or both of the following ways: (1) delineation of the area, wholly or partially, on a statistical basis (for example: a population threshold is applied, as for a Census Tract); (2) a statistical description of the area is developed (for example: age and gender statistics; economic statistics; or natural hazard occurrences within the area). Special constraints may be applied, such as: (a) the value of one or more statistical parameters is the same throughout the area, and different from adjacent areas; (b) the value of some statistical parameter(s) falls within a range that applies throughout the area.

objetos.definicion: A route that links two locations and is served by regularly scheduled transport.
objetos.descripcion: For example, air routes between aerodromes or sea routes between ports. The route is used for the transport of people and/or goods.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which relate to recreational activities of people.

objetos.definicion: A small tract of level ground serving as a stage that is surrounded by rising slopes (either naturally occurring or artificially constructed) supporting tiered seating (for example: benches).
objetos.descripcion: Generally oval or circular in overall shape and typically used for live theatrical presentations, concerts, opera or dance productions, cinema, and/or other stage productions.

objetos.definicion: A predominantly man-made facility equipped with recreational devices.
A large structure located in an amusement park.
A natural area set aside for the preservation and protection of wildlife.
A site where remains of past civilizations or human activity have been discovered.
A building enclosing a large open area, often circular or oval-shaped, surrounded on most or all sides by tiered seating for spectators.
objetos.descripcion: Generally designed to showcase theater, musical performances, or sporting events (for example: basketball, ice hockey, wrestling, or boxing).

objetos.definicion: An outdoor band-stand in the form of a large concave shell with special acoustical properties.
objetos.descripcion: It typically has a concave, nearly hemispherical back serving as a sounding board. A band-stand is a platform or other structure for the use of a band of musicians.

objetos.definicion: A long hard seat for two or more persons.
objetos.descripcion: May be backless and attached to, or adjacent to, a picnic table.

objetos.definicion: A culturally designated tract where plants are displayed.
A tract containing a concentration of buildings and/or other structures.
An encampment where tents and/or other easily moveable structures (for example: yurts) serve as full-time, temporary, or seasonal residences.
A designated place for recreational camping.
A prepared site, typically including facilities, used for holiday accommodations where caravans and/or motor homes are parked.
objetos.descripcion: Caravans are travel trailers towed behind vehicles while motor homes are self-contained vehicles used for both travel and accommodations. Facilities may include utility connections (for example: water, power, or gas), convenience store(s), showers, laundry facilities, and swimming pools.

objetos.definicion: A fortified complex of buildings and related structures that consists principally of a central keep with surrounding thick walls, battlements, and often the presence of a moat, and is commonly of some historical significance.
objetos.descripcion: A castle complex may be quite extensive, including multiple distinct buildings of diverse function. Historically castle complexes were designed and constructed as defensive structures situated so as to dominate the surrounding countryside. With advancing technology, especially artillery, they have become obsolete for military defensive purposes and are now valued primarily for their historical significance. Examples of castle complexes include Prague and Windsor Castles.

objetos.definicion: An area of land and/or sea especially dedicated to the protection and maintenance of biological diversity, and of natural and associated cultural resources, and managed through legal or other effective means.
objetos.descripcion: As determined, for example, by the International Union for Conservation of Nature and Natural Resources (IUCN).

objetos.definicion: A place where motion pictures are shown while viewers remain in their vehicles.
An area where permanent facilities exist to hold outdoor fairs, circuses or exhibitions.
A piece of ground (often enclosed) where fruits, flowers, herbs, or vegetables are cultivated.
objetos.descripcion: Often adjoining a house or other residential building.

objetos.definicion: A tract of land on which golf is played.
A parcel of land used for practicing golf shots.
A structure for special viewing of outdoor events, usually roofed, that has tiers of seats or standing room for spectators.
A maintained vegetated area, which may also contain pathways.
objetos.descripcion: Its primary intent is to improve the appearance of a built-up area but not to be a park.

objetos.definicion: A site containing one or more historical and/or culturally significant buildings and/or other structures.
A site maintained for the public and declared to be of national or provincial historical significance and/or interest.
A location, which is generally elevated, from which the surrounding area may be observed.
objetos.descripcion: For example, it is easily accessible by vehicle, is free of obscuring vegetation, and the local topography allows for unobstructed viewing of distant features.

objetos.definicion: A site for the semi-permanent parking of manufactured homes used as dwellings and designed without a permanent foundation.
objetos.descripcion: Manufactured homes are prefabricated homes built in factories, rather than on-site, and then taken to the place where they will be occupied. They are usually transported by tractor-trailers over public roads to sites which are often in rural areas or high-density developments. While these houses are usually placed in one location and left there permanently, they do retain the ability to be moved as this is a requirement in many areas. Behind the cosmetic work fitted at installation to hide the base, there are strong trailer frames, axles, wheels and tow-hitches.

objetos.definicion: A recognizable feature in the terrain that is subject to defined protective rules (for example: world cultural heritage).
objetos.descripcion: It may be of either artificial or natural origin, and may not be in its original pristine state (for example: overgrown, damaged or fragmentary).

objetos.definicion: A facility with a swimming pool and/or located on the bank of a water body that is used for bathing or swimming.
A large outdoor screen for showing motion pictures.

An area of defined limits which is set aside for human recreation and enjoyment and/or for historic preservation purposes, and is usually maintained in a natural, semi-natural, or ornamentally planted state.
objetos.descripcion: Parks may be in urban areas such as Central Park in New York City or in less developed areas such as Poplar Forest in Forest, Virginia, where Thomas Jefferson's plantation and plantation house are located.

objetos.definicion: A site that has been set aside for picnics.
objetos.descripcion: It may have picnic tables for public use.

objetos.definicion: A table used for picnics.
objetos.descripcion: Often includes attached benches for seating.

objetos.definicion: An open site that serves as a public meeting location in a built-up area.
A ground or tract marked out for racing.
objetos.descripcion: The track may be banked to facilitate high-speed racing, either by grading of the terrain or the use of structures. The bank angle may exceed 30 arc degrees and such structures can reach significant heights.

objetos.definicion: A structure extending into the water used as a platform for recreational purposes, not intended as a berthing place for vessels.
objetos.descripcion: For example, a fishing pier or a promenade pier.

objetos.definicion: The deteriorated remains of an unspecified structure.
A large outdoor board for publicly displaying the score in an athletic event.
objetos.descripcion: Usually associated with a sports stadium or major playing field.

objetos.definicion: A commercial facility tenanted by multiple retail stores (for example: household goods, clothing, or books), restaurants (for example: a food court), entertainment venues (for example: a movie theatre or electronic games arcade), and/or other businesses (for example: professional services), that is completely enclosed, climate controlled, has a common public arcade (for example: furnished with decorative plantings, benches, and/or fountains) and a common vehicle parking area (for example: a parking lot or parking garage).
objetos.descripcion: When the commercial entrances open onto the interior of the complex (public access being by means of central entries and broad corridors) it may consist of multiple levels connected by escalators and is often termed a 'shopping mall'. When the commercial entrances open towards the exterior of the complex and access to individual commercial entrances is directly from an adjacent vehicle parking area it consists of a single level and is often termed a 'shopping centre' or 'shopping plaza'.
objetos.aliases: Shopping Centre, Shopping Plaza, Shopping Mall

objetos.definicion: A man-made structure consisting of a steep ramp levelling off at the end and built on a natural slope, used in ski-jumping.
A slope or trail prepared for skiing.
A resort town or area centered around mineral and/or hot springs that are believed to have restorative powers.
objetos.descripcion: Originally named after a watering-place in the province of Liege, Belgium, celebrated for the curative properties of its mineral springs. A modern spa can be a luxurious resort or resort hotel, that may be located near a special water source or offers hot tub or similar warm-water hydromassage facilities.

objetos.definicion: An open area where sporting events, exercises, and/or games occur.
objetos.descripcion: For example, an athletic field, a playing field, and/or a sports field.

objetos.definicion: An athletic field partially or completely surrounded by a structure designed to allow spectators to stand or sit and view the event.
objetos.descripcion: Often designed in size and shape to accommodate specific sports (for example: baseball or football). The smaller ones may be open at one or both ends.

objetos.definicion: A field and/or stage partly or completely surrounded by a structure designed to allow spectators to stand or sit while viewing an event.
objetos.descripcion: The field and/or stage may be enclosed in a building or be outdoors. Stadiums are surrounded on most or all sides by tiered seating for spectators. Often designed in size and shape to accommodate specific sports (for example: baseball, football, basketball or ice hockey), theater or musical performances.

objetos.definicion: A man-made pool used for swimming outdoors.
A site and associated facilities used for the sport of tennis.
One or more firm-surfaced courts that are used for tennis.
objetos.descripcion: Includes a net across the centre when in use.

objetos.definicion: A site where wild animals are kept for exhibition to the public, that may also support breeding and/or study.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which relate to politics and/or which describe administrative issues.

objetos.definicion: A boundary between administratively controlled regions.
An administratively subordinate division of a geopolitical entity.
objetos.descripcion: A geopolitical entity (country) is typically divided into first-, second-, and lower-order administrative divisions. First-order administrative divisions are immediately subordinate to the government of the geopolitical entity, with second- and lower-order divisions subordinate to those above them. Examples: (first-order) a United States state, a German Land, a French region; a Canadian province; (second-order) a U.S. county, a French department; (third-order) a U.S. township, a French arrondissement; (lower-levels) a French commune.

objetos.definicion: A region controlled by an administrative authority.
A line established by opposing political groups as a result of cessation of hostilities.
A location that serves as a point on, and which partially defines a segment of, a national boundary baseline.
objetos.descripcion: May be monumented or unmonumented. A national boundary baseline is used for defining the landward edge or margin of a nation's various contiguous zones such as the 3 and 12 nautical mile limits and the Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ).

objetos.definicion: A line along which active hostilities are suspended.
A limit of an area which is unilaterally claimed by one political group without consent or negotiation with another.
A line established to regulate matters between nations or groups over a specific area or territory.
A modeling entity collecting information regarding the availability and specifics of customs and immigration, including the facilities used for this service.
An existing line of separation not officially recognized by various governments.
A region where military activity is prohibited.
