A territorial region for which agreed procedures are developed and maintained to prevent, reduce, control, mitigate and take other protective and/or ameliorative measures in the event of an emergency (for example: in the event of an accident at a nuclear facility).

A region controlled by a political community having an organized government and possessing internal and external sovereignty, most often as a State but sometimes having a dependent relationship on another political authority or a special sovereignty status.
objetos.descripcion: The degree of sovereignty may be limited in specific areas (for example: matters of economic, administrative, legislative, judicial, military and/or foreign policy). The region controlled by a sovereign geopolitical entity is commonly referred to as a 'country'.

objetos.definicion: A geospatially described boundary representing the limits of authority for administration, control, military and/or other kinds of activities, as asserted by one or more political organizations (whether unilaterally or in agreement), including recognized governments, provisional authorities, and international bodies.
objetos.descripcion: A geopolitical line is typically indicated at ground level, but in effect represents a two-dimensional plane roughly perpendicular to the Earth's surface along that line, passing through the air above and the ground below.

objetos.definicion: A territorial region where humanitarian relief is provided under the administrative control of a relief organization.
objetos.descripcion: Humanitarian relief agencies, in particular those with ongoing international operations, may have established regions with administrative infrastructure for managing their operations in the area.

objetos.definicion: An area which is the responsibility of territorial commands.
A route established for the safe passage of vessels through offshore oil and gas fields and minefields.
A region where a community (people) has the full sovereignty about a national territory.
objetos.descripcion: As defined by the meaning of the law of nations.

objetos.definicion: A geographic area characterized by statistically derived and/or aggregated properties (for example: population age profile, distribution of land uses, probability of types of events).
objetos.descripcion: These areas may be characterized by statistics in one or both of the following ways: (1) delineation of the area, wholly or partially, on a statistical basis (for example: a population threshold is applied, as for a Census Tract); (2) a statistical description of the area is developed (for example: age and gender statistics; economic statistics; or natural hazard occurrences within the area). Special constraints may be applied, such as: (a) the value of one or more statistical parameters is the same throughout the area, and different from adjacent areas; (b) the value of some statistical parameter(s) falls within a range that applies throughout the area.

objetos.definicion: A territory, which is not an independent sovereign State nor a regular part of a sovereign State.
objetos.descripcion: It is a region which is separated from its homeland because of its geographic position (for example: an island, overseas territory, exclave) or its legal status (for example: trust territory, occupation or long-run lease) or which is not fully integrated in their homeland or which has special relations respectively which have special administration structures in comparison to the rest of the homeland (for example: Hong Kong to China).

objetos.definicion: A route that links two locations and is served by regularly scheduled transport.
objetos.descripcion: For example, air routes between aerodromes or sea routes between ports. The route is used for the transport of people and/or goods.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which describe scientific issues and/or Concepts which relate to education.

objetos.definicion: The geographic location at which a set of acoustic observations were taken.
A building designed and equipped (for example: with a telescope) for making observations of celestial objects (including the earth in relation to them), of space, and of the universe as a whole.
objetos.descripcion: Typically incorporates a dome-shaped covering that may be opened in order to expose instruments to the sky or closed to protect them from the weather.

objetos.definicion: The geographic location at which a set of magnetic observations were taken.
A device used for the collection of hydrographic and oceanographic data.
A recognizable feature in the terrain that is subject to defined protective rules (for example: world cultural heritage).
objetos.descripcion: It may be of either artificial or natural origin, and may not be in its original pristine state (for example: overgrown, damaged or fragmentary).

objetos.definicion: An apparatus for imparting high velocities to charged particles.
A facility that is intended to be used for research and/or scientific purposes.
objetos.descripcion: For example, an astronomic observatory with facilities like dish aerials, buildings and infrastructure.

objetos.definicion: A facility that is used to support space related activities (for example: services such as assembly, launching or recovery of spacecraft or managing flight operations).
An apparatus used for observing distant objects and/or phenomena.
A balloon that is tethered to the ground at an anchoring device (for example: a ring and pad) or substantial structure (for example: a mooring tower).
objetos.descripcion: It is usually deployed for extended periods of time and may be used, for example, for weather sensing and/or observation of the surrounding terrain.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which relate to cultures, population and its characteristics.
subcategorias.descripcion: Concepts such as tribal affiliation and language, itself.

objetos.definicion: A fortified complex of buildings and related structures that consists principally of a central keep with surrounding thick walls, battlements, and often the presence of a moat, and is commonly of some historical significance.
objetos.descripcion: A castle complex may be quite extensive, including multiple distinct buildings of diverse function. Historically castle complexes were designed and constructed as defensive structures situated so as to dominate the surrounding countryside. With advancing technology, especially artillery, they have become obsolete for military defensive purposes and are now valued primarily for their historical significance. Examples of castle complexes include Prague and Windsor Castles.

objetos.definicion: An area that is protected (for example: designated as World Heritage Site) because of its cultural (for example: historical) importance.
objetos.descripcion: For example, the Dresden Elbe Valley.

objetos.definicion: A location that normally does not appear as a specific, characterized object but that represents an area where a specific cultural factor (for example: religion, ethnicity, language, or tribal/clan affiliation) predominates.
A modeling entity collecting information about the religious significance and/or characteristics of features.
A geographic area characterized by statistically derived and/or aggregated properties (for example: population age profile, distribution of land uses, probability of types of events).
objetos.descripcion: These areas may be characterized by statistics in one or both of the following ways: (1) delineation of the area, wholly or partially, on a statistical basis (for example: a population threshold is applied, as for a Census Tract); (2) a statistical description of the area is developed (for example: age and gender statistics; economic statistics; or natural hazard occurrences within the area). Special constraints may be applied, such as: (a) the value of one or more statistical parameters is the same throughout the area, and different from adjacent areas; (b) the value of some statistical parameter(s) falls within a range that applies throughout the area.

contenido: This Group consists of Concepts which relate to transportation to include railways, roads and tracks, water bodies, guided devices, pipelines, restrictions, crossings and all associated transportation Concepts.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which relate to land transportation based on rails.

objetos.definicion: A length or single point along a route that due to its width, surface quality, alignment, fixed human activity or fixed human feature is likely to impede movement at a constant speed resulting in slowing, and either by vehicular bunching or by type may cause temporary halts.
A location along a transportation route where construction or maintenance is occurring.
objetos.descripcion: A construction zone may contain safety markers, construction equipment and/or temporary traffic controls.

objetos.definicion: A structure that houses personnel and equipment used to control the flow of traffic within a specified range of an installation.
objetos.descripcion: Examples of installations that use control towers are aerodromes, railways, and maritime routes.

objetos.definicion: A location that is the furthest point reached by a railway where equipment and/or materials are loaded onto or unloaded from rail wagons.
One or more railway tracks comprising a network that is operated for the conveyance of passengers and/or goods.
A raised walk, floor, or other elevated structure along the side of the track at a railway station, for convenience in getting goods and/or passengers on and off a train.
A stretch of railway track connected to a main railway and used for temporary storage, passing, loading, and/or unloading.
objetos.aliases: Railway Siding, Railway Spur, Railroad Spur, Railroad Siding

objetos.definicion: A signal used to control traffic on a railway.
A facility at which passengers may board and alight from trains and/or rail-transported freight may be loaded or unloaded.
A device integrated with a railway track with which the rails may be switched to permit access to another railway track.
A rail or set of parallel rails on which a train, tram, or rail wagon runs.
A sideways-moving platform for shifting a railway carriage or engine from one set of rails to another parallel set.
A rotating platform with railway tracks used for turning locomotives and/or railway carriages.
objetos.descripcion: May be enclosed within a structure.

objetos.definicion: A system of railway tracks and associated structures that are located within defined limits and that provide for loading, unloading, and/or assembling trains.

A sign placed by an authority charged with the regulation of traffic along a transportation route for the purpose of regulating the flow of traffic (for example: vessels, vehicles and/or pedestrians) and/or providing information pertinent to the control of that traffic.
A circular or semicircular building, with a railway turntable in the centre, used for storing and/or repairing railway locomotives.
objetos.descripcion: The railway turntable may be either completely covered, partially covered or not covered, and partially or completely surrounded by the building.

objetos.definicion: A stretch along a land transportation route where the slope is high enough to slow, hinder, or even stop traffic.
objetos.descripcion: The percent (%) slope is the ratio of change in elevation (vertical distance) to horizontal ground distance multiplied by 100.

objetos.definicion: A location where one or more devices have been temporarily or permanently stationed for the purpose of collecting information regarding vehicular and/or pedestrian traffic.
objetos.descripcion: Such information may include analysis of traffic flow, turning movements, speeds, congestion and delays, parking and loading, and pedestrian movement.

objetos.definicion: A route that links two locations and is served by regularly scheduled transport.
objetos.descripcion: For example, air routes between aerodromes or sea routes between ports. The route is used for the transport of people and/or goods.

objetos.definicion: A section of a transportation route where its size (for example: narrowing or expansion in width) and/or operating speed is significantly different than in the adjacent sections of the route.
objetos.descripcion: For example, an increase or decrease in the number of lanes in a road. Constrictions along or beside a transportation route may impede the flow of vehicles or people thus resulting in 'choke points'.

objetos.definicion: A structure built over and/or along a transportation route designed to prevent damage to, or blockage of, the route from rock slides, snow slides and/or weather phenomena.
objetos.descripcion: For example, a snow shed, a rock shed or a gallery. These structures are usually located in rugged mountainous regions.

objetos.definicion: An intermediate stop, usually having minimal or no associated structures, along a transportation route, which serves as a place for disembarking or taking on passengers or freight.
objetos.descripcion: Transportation routes may include railway, pipeline, road, water or air. Associated structures could include a sign or small shelter. Some stops have no specific infrastructure and are known only by their location.

objetos.definicion: A complex of buildings, associated facilities, roads, and adapted areas used for transshipment of freight between the same or different kinds of transport.
A railway running underground, especially beneath the streets and buildings of a city.
objetos.descripcion: Usually includes those portions of an underground railway system that may not be underground.

objetos.definicion: A location on a land transportation route which restricts vehicles of a specific weight to pass.
objetos.descripcion: These restrictions may be caused because of surface damage, construction limits or surrounding obstacles (for example: tunnels or culverts below the road).

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which are related to road-like Concepts, mainly which can be used by wheeled vehicles.

objetos.definicion: A transport link (route, way, path, trail) that in some manner has been dedicated to bicycles.
A large outdoor board for advertisements.
objetos.descripcion: May be attached to another structure or self-supporting. Usually elevated so as to be seen for a significant distance.

objetos.definicion: An unimproved road.
objetos.descripcion: The surface is usually rough (for example: rutted) and minimally prepared (for example: packed earth or thinly covered with gravel).

objetos.definicion: A length or single point along a route that due to its width, surface quality, alignment, fixed human activity or fixed human feature is likely to impede movement at a constant speed resulting in slowing, and either by vehicular bunching or by type may cause temporary halts.
A location along a transportation route where construction or maintenance is occurring.
objetos.descripcion: A construction zone may contain safety markers, construction equipment and/or temporary traffic controls.

objetos.definicion: A structure that houses personnel and equipment used to control the flow of traffic within a specified range of an installation.
objetos.descripcion: Examples of installations that use control towers are aerodromes, railways, and maritime routes.

objetos.definicion: A border of concrete, asphalt or stone forming part of a gutter along the edge of a street or road.
An unenclosed road or trail, due to the regular movement of animal herds.
objetos.descripcion: Chiefly for cattle and/or sheep.

objetos.definicion: A shaped area at the terminus of a local street that provides sufficient turning space allowing incoming traffic to turn around and exit without performing a stop-and-change-direction manoeuvre.
objetos.descripcion: The site is intended to slow down and control the flow of vehicular traffic leaving the main avenue. Construction is typically in the form of a defined shape (for example: circle, loop, or crescent). Access to the shaped turnaround site is provided through a single inlet passageway and along a short, connecting street. Traffic flow proceeds continuously around the turnaround site (in whatever shape and degree of utility). Egress is provided back along the same short, connecting street through a single outlet. The single inlet and single outlet are the same passageways. A median-like structure may exist in the center of the turnaround site, thus ensuring a well-defined pattern of vehicle movement. In residential areas the turnaround site often has multiple adjoining properties, each of which may have a separate driveway and/or defined parking area along the perimeter of the shaped area.

objetos.definicion: A shallow place in a body of water used as a crossing.
A route over a frozen watercourse.
objetos.descripcion: Usually marked and intended to support substantial vehicle traffic. Often designed as an alternate to a seasonally-closed ferry crossing (see Feature: 'Ferry Crossing').

objetos.definicion: The route or routes designated within an area of operations upon which the bulk of traffic flows in support of military operations.
objetos.descripcion: See AAP-6(2007), page 2-M-1.

objetos.definicion: A building at, or in which, motor vehicles are refuelled, serviced, and sometimes repaired.
objetos.descripcion: Usually accompanied by several prominently placed petrol pumps.

objetos.definicion: A sign placed by an authority charged with the regulation of traffic along a transportation route for the purpose of regulating the flow of traffic (for example: vessels, vehicles and/or pedestrians) and/or providing information pertinent to the control of that traffic.
A route with a specially prepared surface that is intended for use by wheeled vehicles.
A system of interconnecting roads (sometimes called ramps) located at a road junction that provides for the free movement of traffic between two or more routes on different levels.
objetos.descripcion: A road interchange utilizes grade separation and bridges to permit traffic on at least one road to pass through the junction without directly crossing any other traffic stream.

objetos.definicion: A section of a road interchange connecting two or more roads at different levels by means of an inclined roadway.
A roadside place usually having facilities for people and/or vehicles.
objetos.aliases: Vehicle Stopping Area, Rest Area, Lay By

objetos.definicion: A sign used to designate the name and/or identifying number of a road.
objetos.descripcion: The sign may also display an emblem used to designate the road type (for example: national, interstate, or local).

objetos.definicion: A curve along a land transportation route that may restrict vehicle traffic.
A paved or improved pedestrian path, typically located adjacent and parallel to a street or road.
A stretch along a land transportation route where the slope is high enough to slow, hinder, or even stop traffic.
objetos.descripcion: The percent (%) slope is the ratio of change in elevation (vertical distance) to horizontal ground distance multiplied by 100.

objetos.definicion: A crossing or turn pad where tracked military vehicles cross over other transportation elements.
objetos.descripcion: Typically a hardened area minimizing the impact of tracked vehicles on the underlying transportation feature (for example: road or railway). May be used as a crossing over other transportation, or a turn pad within a system of tank trails.

objetos.definicion: A designated route where tracked military vehicles have jurisdiction to travel, usually within a military training area.
A location where one or more devices have been temporarily or permanently stationed for the purpose of collecting information regarding vehicular and/or pedestrian traffic.
objetos.descripcion: Such information may include analysis of traffic flow, turning movements, speeds, congestion and delays, parking and loading, and pedestrian movement.

objetos.definicion: A path worn by the passage of people or animals.
A route that links two locations and is served by regularly scheduled transport.
objetos.descripcion: For example, air routes between aerodromes or sea routes between ports. The route is used for the transport of people and/or goods.

objetos.definicion: A section of a transportation route where its size (for example: narrowing or expansion in width) and/or operating speed is significantly different than in the adjacent sections of the route.
objetos.descripcion: For example, an increase or decrease in the number of lanes in a road. Constrictions along or beside a transportation route may impede the flow of vehicles or people thus resulting in 'choke points'.

objetos.definicion: A structure built over and/or along a transportation route designed to prevent damage to, or blockage of, the route from rock slides, snow slides and/or weather phenomena.
objetos.descripcion: For example, a snow shed, a rock shed or a gallery. These structures are usually located in rugged mountainous regions.

objetos.definicion: An intermediate stop, usually having minimal or no associated structures, along a transportation route, which serves as a place for disembarking or taking on passengers or freight.
objetos.descripcion: Transportation routes may include railway, pipeline, road, water or air. Associated structures could include a sign or small shelter. Some stops have no specific infrastructure and are known only by their location.

objetos.definicion: A complex of buildings, associated facilities, roads, and adapted areas used for transshipment of freight between the same or different kinds of transport.
A site, including building(s) and associated equipment, that is used to inspect and weigh vehicles.
objetos.descripcion: Located adjacent to a road and used to enforce a variety of vehicle safety regulations. Vehicles may be weighed by moving them (for example: by driving) onto a platform.
objetos.aliases: Motor Carrier Service Centre, Commercial Vehicle Enforcement Facility

objetos.definicion: A location on a land transportation route which restricts vehicles of a specific weight to pass.
objetos.descripcion: These restrictions may be caused because of surface damage, construction limits or surrounding obstacles (for example: tunnels or culverts below the road).

objetos.definicion: A raised way, path, or road across a low or wet place or stretch of water that is constructed from wooden planks.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which relate to a guided transportation like a cableway or a teleferic.

objetos.definicion: A suspended transportation system consisting of one or more load cables, supporting pylons, carrier units (for example: cars or buckets intended to transport people, material, and/or equipment) and usually stations.
objetos.descripcion: A cableway consists of carrier units attached to load cables which are strung between pylons and/or stations. For example, a ski-lift.

objetos.definicion: A device for conveying articles or materials from one location to another during manufacture or processing using a continuously moving mechanism.
objetos.descripcion: Usually long, thin, and rectangular, and located above ground surface. It can be situated horizontally, vertically, at a slope between flat and upright, or in a combination of these postures. In general, conveyor systems consist of the bucket, screw (auger), apron, or flight conveyors to load silos or bunkers. Other systems use a series of rollers to move a range of products from relatively lightweight luggage and cargo packages at transportation terminals, up to heavyweight plate steel and ingots in industrial mills. The most common system is the belt conveyor. Some systems use a combination of these designs such as shallow buckets (or flat plates) attached to a belt conveyor. Conveyors can be used for long distance transportation (ifor example, kilometres) of materials. Long distance conveyor systems are usually constructed in segments to accommodate changes in direction where needed.

objetos.definicion: A sign placed by an authority charged with the regulation of traffic along a transportation route for the purpose of regulating the flow of traffic (for example: vessels, vehicles and/or pedestrians) and/or providing information pertinent to the control of that traffic.
A location where one or more devices have been temporarily or permanently stationed for the purpose of collecting information regarding vehicular and/or pedestrian traffic.
objetos.descripcion: Such information may include analysis of traffic flow, turning movements, speeds, congestion and delays, parking and loading, and pedestrian movement.

objetos.descripcion: For example, an increase or decrease in the number of lanes in a road. Constrictions along or beside a transportation route may impede the flow of vehicles or people thus resulting in 'choke points'.

objetos.descripcion: For example, a snow shed, a rock shed or a gallery. These structures are usually located in rugged mountainous regions.

objetos.definicion: An intermediate stop, usually having minimal or no associated structures, along a transportation route, which serves as a place for disembarking or taking on passengers or freight.
objetos.descripcion: Transportation routes may include railway, pipeline, road, water or air. Associated structures could include a sign or small shelter. Some stops have no specific infrastructure and are known only by their location.

objetos.definicion: A complex of buildings, associated facilities, roads, and adapted areas used for transshipment of freight between the same or different kinds of transport.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which relate to any transportation on water.

objetos.definicion: The geographic location at which a set of acoustic observations were taken.

A heavy object, kept in place on the seafloor by its weight and possibly with flukes, to which is attached a cable, rope, or chain that keeps a floating structure (for example, a buoy) on the waterbody surface positioned within a narrow region.
A designated area of water where a single vessel (for example: a ship or a sea plane) may anchor.
objetos.descripcion: Usually defined by a centre point and a swinging circle.

objetos.definicion: An area of relatively uniform water depth with no cables, pipelines, or hazardous obstructions present on the seafloor, in which vessels anchor or may anchor.
objetos.descripcion: Anchorage areas are additionally determined by: the depth of water in comparison to the tidal range; the material of the seafloor bottom; local environmental effects of wind and currents; and proximity to hazards to navigation, adjacent ships, and harbor traffic lanes. Although the anchorage refers to an identified area along the water surface, its physical structure is considered to be the material and condition of the seafloor below. An anchorage can be physically damaged by natural events (for example: an earthquake or tsunami) by which the preferred seafloor bottom type can change, or hazardous obstructions can be created or moved into the anchorage area.

objetos.definicion: A facility involved in the culturing or farming (including harvesting) of aquatic organisms (for example: fish, mollusks, crustaceans, plants, crocodiles, alligators or amphibians) using techniques designed to increase the production of the organisms in question beyond the natural capacity of the environment (for example: regular stocking, feeding and protection from predators).
objetos.descripcion: Culturing or farming refers to the rearing of individuals up to their juvenile and/or adult phase under captive conditions. In addition, it also encompasses individual, corporate or state ownership of the individual organisms throughout the rearing or culture stage, up to and including harvesting.

objetos.definicion: A region of waterborne cellular or vascular plants (for example: algae, grasses, reeds, and water hyacinths).
objetos.descripcion: The vegetation may moored (for example: sea grass and reeds) or floating (for example: sargasso and water hyacinths).

objetos.definicion: A named or numbered place where a vessel is moored at a wharf.
A structure primarily used as a berthing place for vessels.
objetos.descripcion: For example, a pier, a wharf, and a quay. Consideration should be given to using the more general Feature: 'Shoreline Construction' and a type-discriminating attribute.

objetos.definicion: A place where boats receive or discharge passengers and freight, but lacking most port facilities.
A small shaped post, mounted on the ground or pavement surface.
objetos.descripcion: Bollards may be mounted on a wharf or dolphin and used to secure ship's lines, or they may be mounted at intervals on the ground or pavement surface in order to protect critical infrastructure, delimit an area such as a roadway sidewalk or path, or to exclude vehicles. Bollards may be fixed above the surface or may be installed in housings below the surface so as to be very quickly raised into a blocking position to prevent the progress of threatening vehicles.

objetos.definicion: A structure that protects a waterbody region (for example: a shore, a harbour, and/or an anchorage) from water waves by preventing them from reaching the protected region or reducing their magnitude.
A floating object moored to the bottom in a particular place, as an aid to navigation or for other specific purposes.
The location at which vessels are required to report to a traffic control center.
objetos.descripcion: Note that this is not the same as Feature: 'Aeronautical Waypoint' which is for aircraft only.

objetos.definicion: That part of a body of water, either ocean or inland, (sometimes dredged) deep enough for navigation through an area otherwise not navigable.
objetos.descripcion: It is usually marked by a single or double line of buoys and sometimes by leading lines. It is often the deepest part of a stream, bay or strait through which the main current flows.

objetos.definicion: A length or single point along a route that due to its width, surface quality, alignment, fixed human activity or fixed human feature is likely to impede movement at a constant speed resulting in slowing, and either by vehicular bunching or by type may cause temporary halts.
A geographic region characterized by a historical accounting of shipping lane location, width, distribution, and use by vessel size.
objetos.descripcion: Used, for example, for mission planning to identify areas of high and low commercial traffic for the submarine navigator and sonarman.

objetos.definicion: A location along a transportation route where construction or maintenance is occurring.
objetos.descripcion: A construction zone may contain safety markers, construction equipment and/or temporary traffic controls.

objetos.definicion: A structure that houses personnel and equipment used to control the flow of traffic within a specified range of an installation.
objetos.descripcion: Examples of installations that use control towers are aerodromes, railways, and maritime routes.

objetos.definicion: An artificially enclosed body of water within which vessels may moor and which may have gates used to regulate the interior water level.
An area of the bottom of a body of water (for example: a channel) which has been deepened by dredging.
An artificial basin fitted with a gate or caisson into which vessels can be floated and the water pumped out to expose the bottom of the vessel.
The reservoir in a dry dock bounded by the dry dock wall and dry dock gate.
The gate at the end of a dry dock that excludes the water after pumping out the dock.
objetos.descripcion: The pumping engines are often located in the caisson.

objetos.definicion: The wall of a dry dock.
objetos.descripcion: Along with the dry dock gate it encloses the dry dock basin.

objetos.definicion: A man-made embankment to contain or hold back water.
An area on a water body bottom established to simulate a natural reef and intended to enhance fishery resources and commercial and/or recreational fishing opportunities.
objetos.descripcion: The haven (reef) is constructed by dumping (or emplacing) assorted scrap materials (or artificial structures) in areas which may be of very small extent or may stretch a considerable distance along a depth contour.

objetos.definicion: An area containing structures (usually portable) for catching fish.
A harbour that is primarily used by fishing vessels.
A geographic region characterized by a historical level of large-scale (generally greater than 100 gross ton) commercial fishing activity.
objetos.descripcion: Typically only fishing vessels traveling at trawling speeds (typically not exceeding 6 knots) are included, and regions near the coastline (for example: less than 10 nautical miles) are excluded.

objetos.definicion: A form of dry dock consisting of a floating structure of one or more sections which can be partly submerged by controlled flooding to receive a vessel, then raised by pumping out the water so that the vessel's bottom can be exposed.
A device (for example: located on a vessel or an aid to navigation) that transmits a warning signal during periods of low visibility, especially due to fog.
A timber structure in the intertidal zone serving as a support for vessels at low stages of the tide to permit work on the exposed portion of the vessel's hull.
A low artificial wall-like structure of durable material extending from the land to seaward for a particular purpose, such as to prevent coast erosion.
A natural or artificial improved body of water providing protection for vessels and generally anchorage and docking facilities.
objetos.descripcion: A harbour consists of both its port (see Feature: 'Port') and its waters (see Feature: 'Harbour Waters').

objetos.definicion: A natural or artificial improved body of water providing protection for vessels and usually associated with a port.
objetos.descripcion: Harbour waters and its related port (see Feature: 'Port') together comprise a harbour (see Feature: 'Harbour').

objetos.definicion: A routeing measure comprising a designated area between the landward boundary of a traffic separation scheme and the adjacent coast, to be used in accordance with the provisions of the International Regulations for Preventing Collisions at Sea.
A small, insubstantial navigational mark.
objetos.descripcion: For example, a staff placed on top of a rock or shoal to mark a hazard or serve as a navigational aid.

objetos.definicion: Steps at the shoreline as the connection between land and water on different levels.
A buoy used to indicate a lateral limit of navigable water.
Two or more lights associated so as to form a leading line to be followed.
A line which passes through at least two clearly defined objects, along which a vessel can safely travel.
A sector defined by bearings from seaward within which a light shows a specified character or color, or is obscured.
A distinctively marked vessel anchored or moored at a charted point, to serve as an aid to navigation.
objetos.descripcion: By night, it displays a characteristic light(s) and is usually equipped with other devices (for example: a fog signal, a submarine sound signal, and/or a radio-beacon) to assist navigation.

objetos.definicion: A distinctive structure on or off a coast exhibiting a major light designed to serve as an aid to navigation.
Lights marking area limits, the alignment of an electrical cable, alignments for anchoring, or serving a similar purpose but not marking direction or course.
An enclosure with a pair or series of gates used for raising or lowering vessels as they pass from one water level to another.
The reservoir in a lock, bounded by lock walls and lock gates.
The pair of massive hinged doors at each end of a lock.
One of the pair of walls, usually masonary, that contain a lock basin and support the lock gates.
An inclined plane used to dump logs into the water for transport, or to haul logs out of the water for processing.
The geographic location at which a set of magnetic observations were taken.

A site where marine organisms are cultivated for food and other products in either the open ocean, in an enclosed section of the ocean, or in tanks, ponds or raceways that are filled with seawater (for example: the farming of marine fish, prawns, or oysters in saltwater ponds).
A device used for the collection of hydrographic and oceanographic data.

A sloping structure that can either be used, as a landing place, at variable water levels, for small vessels (for example: landing ships and ferry boats), or for hauling a cradle carrying a small vessel.
objetos.descripcion: The cradle may travel on rails.

objetos.definicion: A surveyed reference track marking the centre-line of a marine test range.
objetos.descripcion: Vessels undergoing testing must maintain position along this track.

objetos.definicion: A facing of stone or other material, either permanent or temporary, placed along the edge of a stream, river or canal to stabilize the bank and to protect it from the erosive action of the water.
An area in which certain activities or factors of significance to navigation and/or operation apply.
Generally, an area where the mariner has to be made aware of circumstances influencing the safety of navigation.
objetos.descripcion: The caution may represent a specific danger, a general risk, or a rule and/or navigation advice that is not directly related to a specific object. Appropriate consideration should be given, for example, to the use of Features: 'Wreck', 'Hazardous Rock' and 'Well'.

objetos.definicion: A line where on either side certain activities or factors of significance to navigation and/or operation apply.
A prominent, specially constructed object forming a conspicuous mark as a fixed aid to navigation or for use in hydrographic survey.
A luminous or lighted device intended for the purpose of aiding maritime navigation.
objetos.descripcion: A Maritime Navigation Light refers to the light itself including its housing but does not include any support structure or ancillary aids to maritime navigation.

objetos.definicion: An otherwise unspecified fixed structure which supports a Maritime Navigation Light.
objetos.descripcion: May also be used to support other aids to maritime navigation (for example: maritime radiobeacons or fog signals).

objetos.definicion: A coloured (usually white) mark on a vertical surface (for example: a cliff, a rocky outcrop, and/or a wall) that is a conspicuous landmark for maritime navigation.
A light-reflecting device that is secured to an unlit maritime navigation aid in order to distinguish its location and purpose at night.
objetos.descripcion: The retro-reflector may be either a self-contained unit affixed to another structure or consist of a material or coating applied directly to the surface of that structure. The colour and colour patten of the retro-reflector is based on either the Standard Code or the Comprehensive Code referenced within International Association of Lighthouse Authorities (IALA) E-106.

objetos.definicion: A signboard used to indicate speed restrictions, cable landings, and other items of interest to maritime navigation.
A track along which ships may be guided by coastal radar stations, especially in the event of reduced visibility.
An electronic aid to maritime navigation consisting of a radio transmitter that broadcasts distinctive signals.
A track or lane established for the safe passage of vessels.
A place on shore from which signals are made to vessels at sea.
A maritime course, the length of which has been accurately measured, whose endpoints are often established by leading lines.
objetos.descripcion: It is used by vessels to calibrate logs, engine revolution counters, and other onboard equipment, and to determine speed.

objetos.definicion: An area where Mine Counter Measure operations have taken place.
objetos.descripcion: Operation could comprise detection but not neccessarily removal or neutralisation.

objetos.definicion: A form of breakwater alongside which vessels may lie on the sheltered side only.
objetos.descripcion: It is usually a substantial masonry structure, and often serves as a breakwater on its outer side while offering facilities for ships in its inner side. In some cases it may lie entirely within an artificial harbour, permitting vessels to lie along both sides.

objetos.definicion: A chain or similar physical connection (for example: a cable) used to moor a vessel.
objetos.descripcion: For example, used between an anchor and a mooring buoy or between a bollard on a dock and a hulk.

objetos.definicion: The equipment or structure used to secure a vessel.
A metal ring attached to a structure and used to secure a vessel.
Complex feature with possible components: BB019, BC098.
An area where Naval forces (for example: vessels or aircraft) conduct firing and/or munition exercises.
objetos.descripcion: Distinguished from areas where Naval forces conduct general operations and manoeuvers.

objetos.definicion: An area where Naval forces conduct operations.
objetos.descripcion: Distinguished from areas where Naval forces conduct firing and/or munition exercises.

objetos.definicion: A straight line extending towards an area of navigational interest and generally generated by two navigational aids or one navigational aid and a bearing.
A location offshore where a pilot may board a vessel in preparation to piloting it through local waters.
objetos.descripcion: The pilot may either be stationed in a small craft cruising in the near vicinity of the designated location, or may be brought out from shore (for example: by a helicopter) upon request.

objetos.definicion: An airtight air-filled hollow structure, usually rectangular in shape, which is buoyant in water.
objetos.descripcion: Pontoons have enough buoyancy to float both themselves and a significant load. Pontoons may serve as supports for bridges or piers.

objetos.definicion: A place provided with terminal and transfer facilities for loading and/or discharging cargo or passengers, usually located in a harbour.
objetos.descripcion: A port and its related waters (see Feature: 'Harbour Waters') together comprise a harbour (see Feature: 'Harbour').

objetos.definicion: A location on a watercourse that has ramps, structural piles, and/or piers constructed on one or both shores to allow for suitable future crossing operations using floating bridges or rafting equipment.
objetos.descripcion: For example, a prepared float bridge site or a prepared raft site.

objetos.definicion: Indicates the coverage of a sea area by a radar surveillance station.
objetos.descripcion: Inside this area a vessel may request shore based radar assistance, particularly in poor visibility.

objetos.definicion: A facility utilizing radar to detect and analyze objects (for example: aircraft, artificial satellites, asteroids, and/or missiles) and/or environmental phenomena (for example: tornadoes).
objetos.descripcion: May include both a radar aerial as well as a structure housing radar equipment.

objetos.definicion: A sign placed by an authority charged with the regulation of traffic along a transportation route for the purpose of regulating the flow of traffic (for example: vessels, vehicles and/or pedestrians) and/or providing information pertinent to the control of that traffic.
A region in which certain aspects of maritime navigation are restricted.
A layer of broken rock, cobbles, boulders, or fragments of sufficient size to resist the erosive forces of flowing water and wave action.
An area near the shore where vessels can anchor in safety, usually a shallow indentation in the coast.
objetos.descripcion: They are often located outside of harbours that are restricted by size, depth, or operating capacity, and are typically used for lightering operations and unofficial anchoring.

objetos.definicion: A route established for the safe passage of vessels through offshore oil and gas fields and minefields.
A designated portion of water that is outlined by visual surface markings and used by seaplanes to land and take-off.
objetos.aliases: Seaplane Landing Area, Seaplane Take-off Area

objetos.definicion: An embankment or wall for protection against waves or tidal action along a shore or water front.
That part of an inland body of water where the depth is relatively slight (less than 1 metre) and thus likely to limit the passage of watercraft.
objetos.descripcion: Shallow water areas may be identified using overhead imagery, where there are visible bottom features, surface waves, and/or other water surface phenomena.

objetos.definicion: A device used to raise ships vertically between water bodies with different elevations.
objetos.descripcion: Normally ship elevators consist of water filled chambers which can be raised or lowered by means of mechanical devices. Commonly used to move ships between canals where locks would be impractical.

objetos.definicion: A ramp-like structure on a shoreline that is intended to facilitate the movement of vessels and/or materials (for example: logs) into or out of the water.
A mooring structure used by tankers to load and unload in port approaches or in offshore oil and/or gas fields.
objetos.descripcion: The size of the structure may vary between that of a large mooring buoy and that of a manned structure that may be either floating or fixed to the sea bed.

objetos.definicion: The prepared and usually reinforced inclined surface on which keel- and bilge-blocks are laid for supporting a vessel under construction.
objetos.descripcion: Rails associated with a slipway are usually represented separately, for example as a marine railway.

objetos.definicion: A place at which a service generally of interest to small craft or pleasure boats is available.
An acoustic aid to navigation consisting of a device that generates distinctive audible sounds.
objetos.descripcion: For example, a buoy with a bell. See also Feature: 'Fog Signal'.

objetos.definicion: A region that has been determined to be clear of navigational dangers to a specified depth.
A line of known direction from a fixed location that is used to determine accurate positions of a vessel on certain test ranges.
A characteristic shape secured at the top of a buoy or beacon to aid in its identification.
The actual path or route of a craft over the ground or sea bottom.
objetos.descripcion: May be used to delineate the graphic representation of the route rather than the actual route.

objetos.definicion: An area of horizontal coverage recorded by SONAR array systems.
A location where one or more devices have been temporarily or permanently stationed for the purpose of collecting information regarding vehicular and/or pedestrian traffic.
objetos.descripcion: Such information may include analysis of traffic flow, turning movements, speeds, congestion and delays, parking and loading, and pedestrian movement.

objetos.definicion: A maritime routeing measure that separates opposing streams of traffic by appropriate means.
objetos.descripcion: For example, traffic lanes and traffic circles. Often referred to by its acronym, TSS.

objetos.definicion: A wall, bank or jetty often submerged, built to direct or confine the flow of a river or tidal current or to promote scour actions.
A route that links two locations and is served by regularly scheduled transport.
objetos.descripcion: For example, air routes between aerodromes or sea routes between ports. The route is used for the transport of people and/or goods.

objetos.definicion: A section of a transportation route where its size (for example: narrowing or expansion in width) and/or operating speed is significantly different than in the adjacent sections of the route.
objetos.descripcion: For example, an increase or decrease in the number of lanes in a road. Constrictions along or beside a transportation route may impede the flow of vehicles or people thus resulting in 'choke points'.

objetos.definicion: A structure built over and/or along a transportation route designed to prevent damage to, or blockage of, the route from rock slides, snow slides and/or weather phenomena.
objetos.descripcion: For example, a snow shed, a rock shed or a gallery. These structures are usually located in rugged mountainous regions.

objetos.definicion: An intermediate stop, usually having minimal or no associated structures, along a transportation route, which serves as a place for disembarking or taking on passengers or freight.
objetos.descripcion: Transportation routes may include railway, pipeline, road, water or air. Associated structures could include a sign or small shelter. Some stops have no specific infrastructure and are known only by their location.

objetos.definicion: A complex of buildings, associated facilities, roads, and adapted areas used for transshipment of freight between the same or different kinds of transport.
A mechanical device for lifting vessels from the water.
objetos.descripcion: The device may be, for example, a stationary crane or a wheeled vehicle. After removal from the water the vessel may be maintained (for example: cleaning the hull of encrustations) or stored (for example: moved to a building, shed, or lot for winter storage).

objetos.definicion: An enlargement of a channel to permit the turning of vessels.
A location at which currents, tides, and/or other types of water movement are specified.
An artificial structure subdividing a waterbody.
objetos.descripcion: May consist of an artificial earthen embankment subdividing a pond or rice paddy, or an artificial partition (constructed, for example, from concrete or steel) subdividing a fish hatchery tank or water treatment plant aeration tank.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which relate to transportation in the air.

objetos.definicion: A modeling entity collecting information regarding the electrical power available at an aerodrome.
The specific location of the highest point of the aerodrome landing area.
objetos.descripcion: Typically this elevation is the highest point on any of the landing runway surfaces, and is considered the specific point at which the official aerodrome elevation is determined.

objetos.definicion: A prescribed location in which the fuelling of aircraft and service vehicles from a fixed fuel pumping station is performed.
A location denoting the center of the minimum bounding rectangle that defines the functional area of an aerodrome.
objetos.descripcion: The functional area of an aerodrome includes all runways and other aircraft movement areas, hangars, and related facilities required to support aircraft operations.

objetos.definicion: A modeling entity collecting information for areas designed for either the movement or the parking of aircraft and that are not reported elsewhere as aprons, hardstands, or helipads.

The site and equipment of a radar station designed to detect all principal features on the surface of an aerodrome, including aircraft and vehicular traffic, and to present the entire image on a radar indicator console in the aerodrome control tower.
objetos.descripcion: The aerodrome surface detection system is used to augment visual observation by tower personnel of aircraft and/or vehicular movements on aerodrome movement surfaces (for example: runways and taxiways).

objetos.definicion: A ground based piece of electronic equipment that provides aeronautical navigation guidance information or position data.
The navigational center point of a radio navigation installation, determined by either a specified geographic position or by a geographic fix that is referenced to a geographic location.
objetos.descripcion: A radio navigation installation point can be used by itself as a navigational fix or be used in combination with a specific bearing and distance to identify another designated point, which is used for navigational purposes.

objetos.definicion: A prescribed path, established by air refuelling points, along which air-to-air refuelling of aircraft is performed.
objetos.descripcion: An air refuelling route shares the same characteristics as an air refuelling track and air refuelling anchor pattern, combining the routing structures of both into one specific path for the aircraft to fly.

objetos.nombre: Air Traffic Service (ATS) Route Crossing Information
objetos.definicion: A modeling entity collecting information regarding the relationship between an Air Traffic Service (ATS) route segment direction and the ATS route significant point, and how the two are used in an aircraft navigation environment.
objetos.descripcion: For example, minimum altitudes for crossing an aviation designated point onto the same air traffic service route or crossing onto a different air traffic service route segment.

objetos.nombre: Air Traffic Service (ATS) Route Segment Direction
objetos.definicion: One of the two possible directions in which an aircraft may travel along an Air Traffic Service (ATS) route segment.

objetos.nombre: Air Traffic Service (ATS) Route Significant Point
objetos.definicion: A designated point within the airspace structure which serves as a beginning, intermediate, or ending point for an Air Traffic Service (ATS) route.
A defined volume in the air, described as horizontal projection with vertical limits, used to sectionalize the sky for facilitating air traffic services.

The site and equipment of an automated sensor suite that measures, collects, and disseminates weather data to serve aviation and meteorological needs for safe and efficient aviation operations and weather forecasting.
A modeling entity collecting information regarding the aircraft hydraulic fluid types, stock levels, and associated service(s) that are available at an aerodrome.
A modeling entity collecting information regarding the aircraft nitrogen supply types, stock levels, and associated service(s) that are available at an aerodrome.
A modeling entity collecting information regarding the aircraft oil types, stock levels, and associated service(s) that are available at an aerodrome.
A modeling entity collecting information regarding the aircraft oxygen supply types, stock levels, equipment, and associated service(s) that are available at an aerodrome.
A structure that houses personnel and equipment used to control the flow of traffic within a specified range of an installation.
objetos.descripcion: Examples of installations that use control towers are aerodromes, railways, and maritime routes.

objetos.definicion: A set of parameters used to define two specific geometric locations used as navigational points for aircraft utilizing precision Area Navigation (RNAV) approach procedures to land an aircraft in adverse approach conditions.
The portion of an Instrument Approach Procedure (IAP) between the initial approach fix and the runway.
objetos.descripcion: IAP segments include: initial, intermediate, transition, final, and missed approach legs.

objetos.nombre: Instrument Flight Rules (IFR) Takeoff Minimum Information
objetos.definicion: A modeling entity defining the minimum climb gradient and speed that an aircraft must maintain until reaching a specified altitude.
objetos.descripcion: Takeoff minimums are usually defined based on prominent obstacles along the designated flight path, requiring that an aircraft be at a minimum altitude above those obstacles when passing over them.

objetos.definicion: A modeling entity collecting information regarding the service available at an aerodrome that is comprised of equipment available with which to start the engine(s) of a jet aircraft.
A designated site or structure from which a rocket or missile is launched.
A Very High Frequency (VHF) transmitter, radiating signals in a particular direction in order to provide a straight line azimuth path in the horizontal plane to the centre line of a runway.
objetos.descripcion: The Localizer-type Directional Aid (LDA) is of comparable use and accuracy to a localizer but is not part of a complete Instrument Landing System (ILS). The LDA course usually provides a more precise approach course than the similar Simplified Directional Facility (SDF) installation, utilizing a course width of 3 to 6 arc degrees instead of the 6 to 12 arc degrees that a typical SDF may provide.

objetos.definicion: A vertical structure that is used to mark turns and/or provide obstacles around which aircraft may perform low level aerobatic manoeuvres (for example: during racing or training).
objetos.descripcion: It may be either a temporary (for example: being deflated when not in use) or permanent structure that has been placed on dry land or mounted on a barge (for example: on a lake, in a harbour, or along a river).

objetos.definicion: A modeling entity collecting information about alternative characteristics and textual descriptions of an aviation missed approach procedure.
A mast used to secure an airship.

An area surrounding commercial airports with scheduled air services and/or military airfields earmarked for the operation of aircraft with jet engines, where building restrictions may be enforced in order to protect the public from dangers, major disadvantages and major irritation due to aircraft noise.

A sign placed by an authority charged with the regulation of traffic along a transportation route for the purpose of regulating the flow of traffic (for example: vessels, vehicles and/or pedestrians) and/or providing information pertinent to the control of that traffic.
An operationally significant position on the centre-line of a runway surface.
objetos.descripcion: Though the runway centre-line point is a fixed location on the runway surface, the operational significance, or how the centre-line point is used, is based upon the runway direction. For example, the touchdown zone centre-line point, while a fixed location on the runway surface, is only applicable to one of the two associated runway directions for that runway surface.

objetos.definicion: A modeling entity collecting available distance information for aerodrome runway directions.
The intersecting area shared by two or more runways.
A subdivision of a Safe Altitude Area (SAA) within which there is a single set of minimum altitudes.
objetos.descripcion: A safe altitude area defines an obstruction-free minimum altitude for safe aircraft operations within 25 nautical miles of an aerodrome. An SAA is usually divided into sectors, allowing lower altitudes at certain areas around the aerodrome, based on where common aircraft operations may take place.

objetos.definicion: A designated portion of water that is outlined by visual surface markings and used by seaplanes to land and take-off.
objetos.aliases: Seaplane Landing Area, Seaplane Take-off Area

objetos.definicion: A predefined geographic area in which a specific search and rescue organization(s) is responsible for operating.
An organization that is responsible for planning, coordinating, and executing search and rescue services within a specified search and rescue region.
A unit that is designated as the appropriate responder for a specified search and rescue region.
A directional aid facility providing only lateral guidance (front or back course) for a terminal instrument approach from a final approach fix.
objetos.descripcion: The Simplified Directional Facility (SDF) provides a final approach course similar to that of the Instrument Landing System (ILS) localizer, however an SDF is intended only for use by non-precision approach procedures. It is generally less accurate than a localizer, and may not be aligned to the runway. The SDF signal is fixed at either 6 or 12 arc degrees course width as necessary to provide maximum flyability and optimum course quality.

objetos.definicion: A series of predetermined maneuvers used to transition an aircraft either from the enroute phase of flight to the aerodrome, or from the aerodrome to the enroute phase of flight.
Minimum weather condition requirements established for either take-off or landing operations.
objetos.descripcion: Procedure minima may include weather conditions such as prevailing visibility, overcast cloud cover or precipitation.

objetos.definicion: A geographic position or radio navigation fix along a procedure segment leg.
objetos.descripcion: It is a type of aviation designated point that is primarily used in the terminal phase of flight.

objetos.definicion: A published procedure used to connect either the basic terminal instrument procedure to one of several enroute Air Traffic Service (ATS) routes, or to connect one of several enroute ATS routes to the basic terminal instrument procedure.
A location where one or more devices have been temporarily or permanently stationed for the purpose of collecting information regarding vehicular and/or pedestrian traffic.
objetos.descripcion: Such information may include analysis of traffic flow, turning movements, speeds, congestion and delays, parking and loading, and pedestrian movement.

objetos.definicion: The elevation and transponder emission sensor of a transponder landing system.
objetos.descripcion: A transponder landing system is a precision landing system that uses the transponder emissions of an airborne aircraft coupled with ground elevation sensors to determine the position of the aircraft, and then sending the aircraft guidance signals via existing onboard Instrument Landing System (ILS) equipment. The transponder landing system is often used to create a precision approach at a location where an ILS would normally not be available due to cost or terrain issues.

objetos.definicion: A route that links two locations and is served by regularly scheduled transport.
objetos.descripcion: For example, air routes between aerodromes or sea routes between ports. The route is used for the transport of people and/or goods.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which relate to a restriction.
subcategorias.descripcion: Concepts like a narrow or a place with an overpass, on a land transportation route.

objetos.definicion: A structure that connects two locations and provides for the passage of a transportation route (for example: a road or a railway) over a terrain obstacle (for example: a waterbody, a gully, and/or a road).
objetos.descripcion: A bridge consists of a set of two abutments and/or zero or more bridge piers joined by bridge spans. A bridge may serve, for example, as an overpass or a viaduct. In the context of a bridge, the scope of the term 'transportation route' includes the transportation of liquids or gases by means of either pipelines or aqueducts.

objetos.definicion: A location to control passage and/or to register, declare and/or inspect goods, vehicles and/or people.

A length or single point along a route that due to its width, surface quality, alignment, fixed human activity or fixed human feature is likely to impede movement at a constant speed resulting in slowing, and either by vehicular bunching or by type may cause temporary halts.

An area of land and/or sea especially dedicated to the protection and maintenance of biological diversity, and of natural and associated cultural resources, and managed through legal or other effective means.
objetos.descripcion: As determined, for example, by the International Union for Conservation of Nature and Natural Resources (IUCN).

objetos.definicion: A location along a transportation route where construction or maintenance is occurring.
objetos.descripcion: A construction zone may contain safety markers, construction equipment and/or temporary traffic controls.

objetos.definicion: Upward-pointing obstacles laid in the ground to slow or stop the movement of vehicles.
objetos.descripcion: Typically constructed of regularly spaced concrete or metal shapes laid in single or multiple rows.

objetos.definicion: A shaped area at the terminus of a local street that provides sufficient turning space allowing incoming traffic to turn around and exit without performing a stop-and-change-direction manoeuvre.
objetos.descripcion: The site is intended to slow down and control the flow of vehicular traffic leaving the main avenue. Construction is typically in the form of a defined shape (for example: circle, loop, or crescent). Access to the shaped turnaround site is provided through a single inlet passageway and along a short, connecting street. Traffic flow proceeds continuously around the turnaround site (in whatever shape and degree of utility). Egress is provided back along the same short, connecting street through a single outlet. The single inlet and single outlet are the same passageways. A median-like structure may exist in the center of the turnaround site, thus ensuring a well-defined pattern of vehicle movement. In residential areas the turnaround site often has multiple adjoining properties, each of which may have a separate driveway and/or defined parking area along the perimeter of the shaped area.

objetos.definicion: A shallow place in a body of water used as a crossing.
A barrier on a transportation route (for example: a road, a railway, a tunnel, or a bridge) that controls passage (may be opened and closed).
A narrow route through a mountainous region or over a mountain range.
An overhead obstruction (for example: an underpass, an overhead pipeline, and/or the overhang of a building) on a transportation route.

A sign placed by an authority charged with the regulation of traffic along a transportation route for the purpose of regulating the flow of traffic (for example: vessels, vehicles and/or pedestrians) and/or providing information pertinent to the control of that traffic.
A location where a route narrows or expands in width.
objetos.descripcion: For example, an increase or decrease in the number of lanes in a road.

objetos.definicion: That part of an inland body of water where the depth is relatively slight (less than 1 metre) and thus likely to limit the passage of watercraft.
objetos.descripcion: Shallow water areas may be identified using overhead imagery, where there are visible bottom features, surface waves, and/or other water surface phenomena.

objetos.definicion: A curve along a land transportation route that may restrict vehicle traffic.
A device used to raise ships vertically between water bodies with different elevations.
objetos.descripcion: Normally ship elevators consist of water filled chambers which can be raised or lowered by means of mechanical devices. Commonly used to move ships between canals where locks would be impractical.

objetos.definicion: A stretch along a land transportation route where the slope is high enough to slow, hinder, or even stop traffic.
objetos.descripcion: The percent (%) slope is the ratio of change in elevation (vertical distance) to horizontal ground distance multiplied by 100.

objetos.definicion: A substantial semi-permanent assemblage of material, usually in the form of concrete blocks and/or cylinders, positioned alongside or above a land transportation route, ready to be activated as a potential barrier.
objetos.descripcion: For example, a rolling block is positioned alongside the route and a drop gate is positioned above the route.

objetos.definicion: An underground passage that is open at both ends and usually contains a land transportation route (for example: a road and/or a railway).
objetos.descripcion: Commonly used to pass through a hill or mountain, or under a river or road. May also provide underground passage in a mine.

objetos.definicion: The opening of a tunnel into a larger space (for example: onto the terrain surface).
objetos.descripcion: A tunnel is usually open to the terrain surface at both ends, but may sometimes lead to an enclosed space, for example: leading to an underground bunker, into an underground mine (termed an 'adit') or into an underground railway station.

objetos.definicion: An obstruction associated with a transportation route (for example: a road, a railway, a tunnel, or a bridge) to constrain, restrict, and/or prevent passage of vehicles.
objetos.descripcion: A permanent obstruction is fixed in place at a given location to continuously constrain traffic, and it is constructed such that it cannot be removed without major roadway excavation. A semi-permanent obstruction is placed at a given location so that traffic can be continuously constrained, but it is constructed such that it can be removed without major roadway excavation. A temporary, or non-permanent obstruction is placed at a given location to constrain traffic for a limited time only, and it is constructed such that it can be removed without major roadway excavation.

objetos.definicion: A location on a land transportation route which restricts vehicles of a specific weight to pass.
objetos.descripcion: These restrictions may be caused because of surface damage, construction limits or surrounding obstacles (for example: tunnels or culverts below the road).

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which relate to any kind of land transportation route crossing.
subcategorias.descripcion: For example an intersection or a bridge.

objetos.definicion: A structure that connects two locations and provides for the passage of a transportation route (for example: a road or a railway) over a terrain obstacle (for example: a waterbody, a gully, and/or a road).
objetos.descripcion: A bridge consists of a set of two abutments and/or zero or more bridge piers joined by bridge spans. A bridge may serve, for example, as an overpass or a viaduct. In the context of a bridge, the scope of the term 'transportation route' includes the transportation of liquids or gases by means of either pipelines or aqueducts.

objetos.definicion: A pillar or abutment that supports a bridge span.
A component of the deck of a bridge spanning successive bridge piers.
A superstructure of a bridge, above the lowest deck, not including pylons or towers.
A tower and/or pylon from which the deck of a bridge is suspended.

A length or single point along a route that due to its width, surface quality, alignment, fixed human activity or fixed human feature is likely to impede movement at a constant speed resulting in slowing, and either by vehicular bunching or by type may cause temporary halts.
A location where land transportation routes intersect or cross at the same vertical level.
objetos.descripcion: For example, a railway crossing, a road intersection, and a ford.

objetos.definicion: A location of entrance and/or exit.
objetos.descripcion: For example, a cave mouth or a doorway.

objetos.definicion: A route where a ferry crosses from one shore to another.
A location where a ferry takes on or discharges its load.
A shallow place in a body of water used as a crossing.
A route over a frozen watercourse.
objetos.descripcion: Usually marked and intended to support substantial vehicle traffic. Often designed as an alternate to a seasonally-closed ferry crossing (see Feature: 'Ferry Crossing').

objetos.definicion: An elevated or suspended bridge-like structure providing pedestrian passage.
objetos.descripcion: For example, may be used to cross a strreet, a waterbody, or an interior floor space.

objetos.definicion: A traversable site extending across a pipeline that acts as a passageway for cross-country movement of vehicles or troops.
An airtight air-filled hollow structure, usually rectangular in shape, which is buoyant in water.
objetos.descripcion: Pontoons have enough buoyancy to float both themselves and a significant load. Pontoons may serve as supports for bridges or piers.

objetos.definicion: A location on a watercourse that has ramps, structural piles, and/or piers constructed on one or both shores to allow for suitable future crossing operations using floating bridges or rafting equipment.
objetos.descripcion: For example, a prepared float bridge site or a prepared raft site.

objetos.definicion: A device integrated with a railway track with which the rails may be switched to permit access to another railway track.
A system of interconnecting roads (sometimes called ramps) located at a road junction that provides for the free movement of traffic between two or more routes on different levels.
objetos.descripcion: A road interchange utilizes grade separation and bridges to permit traffic on at least one road to pass through the junction without directly crossing any other traffic stream.

objetos.definicion: A crossing or turn pad where tracked military vehicles cross over other transportation elements.
objetos.descripcion: Typically a hardened area minimizing the impact of tracked vehicles on the underlying transportation feature (for example: road or railway). May be used as a crossing over other transportation, or a turn pad within a system of tank trails.

objetos.definicion: An underground passage that is open at both ends and usually contains a land transportation route (for example: a road and/or a railway).
objetos.descripcion: Commonly used to pass through a hill or mountain, or under a river or road. May also provide underground passage in a mine.

objetos.definicion: The opening of a tunnel into a larger space (for example: onto the terrain surface).
objetos.descripcion: A tunnel is usually open to the terrain surface at both ends, but may sometimes lead to an enclosed space, for example: leading to an underground bunker, into an underground mine (termed an 'adit') or into an underground railway station.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which support Concepts stored in the other land transportation Group (03).

objetos.definicion: A pylon supporting an aerial cable.
objetos.descripcion: For example, a ski lift pylon.

objetos.definicion: A location that is marked or designated as a meeting or an assembly point for a specific purpose (for example: evacuation) for specific individuals.
A transport link (route, way, path, trail) that in some manner has been dedicated to bicycles.
A solid raised way across a terrain obstacle (for example: a wetland or a body of shallow water) that is intended to support a transportation route (for example: a road or a railway).
objetos.descripcion: The causeway structure is often constructed from local fill supplemented by other materials (for example: rocks, boulders or gravel) and consists of a solid linear structure in the configuration of an embankment. Causeway structures are built just high enough to insure that the transportation route will remain passable during periods of flooding, tides and seasonal rainfall. Culverts may occur along the length of the causeway structure and individual sections of the causeway structure may be interrupted by bridges.

objetos.definicion: A structure that houses personnel and equipment used to control the flow of traffic within a specified range of an installation.
objetos.descripcion: Examples of installations that use control towers are aerodromes, railways, and maritime routes.

objetos.definicion: A location where land transportation routes intersect or cross at the same vertical level.
objetos.descripcion: For example, a railway crossing, a road intersection, and a ford.

objetos.definicion: An enclosed channel for carrying a watercourse (for example: a stream, a sewer, or a drain) under a route (for example: a road, a railway, or an embankment).
objetos.descripcion: Usually the construction of the route is unaffected.

objetos.definicion: A border of concrete, asphalt or stone forming part of a gutter along the edge of a street or road.
An excavation in the terrain to provide passage for a land or water transportation route (for example: a road, a railway, and/or a canal).
An upright panel or similar structure used to convey visual information.
A marker that designates the distance from a given location.
Upward-pointing obstacles laid in the ground to slow or stop the movement of vehicles.
objetos.descripcion: Typically constructed of regularly spaced concrete or metal shapes laid in single or multiple rows.

objetos.definicion: A man-made raised long mound of earth or other material.
A location where a ferry takes on or discharges its load.
A facility for the storage of fuel (for example: jet fuel, gasoline, or diesel oil).
objetos.descripcion: The fuel is typically stored in large tanks that may be partially or wholly buried and is accompanied by metering and dispensing equipment. Facilities may range in size from a small stockpile of drums (sometimes termed a 'fuel dump') to a large perimeter-controlled site with multiple permanent surface tanks, in-ground pipelines and associated equipment (sometimes termed a 'fuel depot').

objetos.definicion: A sunken or cut passageway along a transportation route in mountainous regions constructed to protect vehicles from the elements.
objetos.descripcion: A series of openings on one side may be present for light or ventilation.

objetos.definicion: A barrier on a transportation route (for example: a road, a railway, a tunnel, or a bridge) that controls passage (may be opened and closed).

An area surrounding commercial airports with scheduled air services and/or military airfields earmarked for the operation of aircraft with jet engines, where building restrictions may be enforced in order to protect the public from dangers, major disadvantages and major irritation due to aircraft noise.
An elevated or suspended bridge-like structure providing pedestrian passage.
objetos.descripcion: For example, may be used to cross a strreet, a waterbody, or an interior floor space.

objetos.definicion: A designated, multi-level, structure used for parking and/or storing vehicles.
objetos.descripcion: May be present as part of a building or as a separate structure.

objetos.definicion: A traversable site extending across a pipeline that acts as a passageway for cross-country movement of vehicles or troops.
A shelter built to protect a section of road or railway from slides of snow and/or rock.
objetos.descripcion: For example, a snow shed or a rock shed.

objetos.definicion: A raised walk, floor, or other elevated structure along the side of the track at a railway station, for convenience in getting goods and/or passengers on and off a train.
An inclined plane, usually man-made, for moving between two levels.
A roadside place usually having facilities for people and/or vehicles.
objetos.aliases: Vehicle Stopping Area, Rest Area, Lay By

objetos.definicion: A sign used to designate the name and/or identifying number of a road.
objetos.descripcion: The sign may also display an emblem used to designate the road type (for example: national, interstate, or local).

objetos.definicion: A paved or improved pedestrian path, typically located adjacent and parallel to a street or road.
A lamp intended to illuminate a road.
objetos.descripcion: May also illuminate the ground adjacent to the road. Usually attached to a tall pole.

objetos.definicion: A sign placed along a road for the purpose of regulating the flow of traffic (for example: vehicles and/or pedestrians) and/or providing information.
A set of automatic lights (usually red, amber, and green) for controlling road traffic, especially at a road intersection.
objetos.descripcion: Usually attached to tall poles or suspended from overhead cables.

objetos.definicion: A location where one or more devices have been temporarily or permanently stationed for the purpose of collecting information regarding vehicular and/or pedestrian traffic.
