objetos.descripcion: Such information may include analysis of traffic flow, turning movements, speeds, congestion and delays, parking and loading, and pedestrian movement.

objetos.definicion: A section of a transportation route where its size (for example: narrowing or expansion in width) and/or operating speed is significantly different than in the adjacent sections of the route.
objetos.descripcion: For example, an increase or decrease in the number of lanes in a road. Constrictions along or beside a transportation route may impede the flow of vehicles or people thus resulting in 'choke points'.

objetos.definicion: A structure built over and/or along a transportation route designed to prevent damage to, or blockage of, the route from rock slides, snow slides and/or weather phenomena.
objetos.descripcion: For example, a snow shed, a rock shed or a gallery. These structures are usually located in rugged mountainous regions.

objetos.definicion: A station, usually having associated structures, which serves as a place for disembarking or taking on passengers or freight along a transportation route.
objetos.descripcion: Transportation routes may include railway, pipeline, road, water or air. Transportation stations may have associated structures for vehicle parking or ticket sales.

objetos.definicion: A complex of buildings, associated facilities, roads, and adapted areas used for transshipment of freight between the same or different kinds of transport.
An underground passage that is open at both ends and usually contains a land transportation route (for example: a road and/or a railway).
objetos.descripcion: Commonly used to pass through a hill or mountain, or under a river or road. May also provide underground passage in a mine.

objetos.definicion: The opening of a tunnel into a larger space (for example: onto the terrain surface).
objetos.descripcion: A tunnel is usually open to the terrain surface at both ends, but may sometimes lead to an enclosed space, for example: leading to an underground bunker, into an underground mine (termed an 'adit') or into an underground railway station.

objetos.definicion: A tract used for storing and/or parking vehicles (for example: recreational vehicles) and/or vessels.
objetos.aliases: Vehicle Storage Area, Parking Area, Car Park, Boat Park

objetos.definicion: A solid man-made barrier of generally heavy material used as an enclosure, boundary, or for protection.
A raised way, path, or road across a low or wet place or stretch of water that is constructed from wooden planks.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which relate to and are essential to servicing spacecraft, enabling spacecraft to launch or re-enter, or transferring passengers or space cargo to or from spacecraft, including launch control centres and rocket assembly facilities.
This Subgroup consists of Concepts which relate to the transport in networks, such as pipelines or channels, above or below surface.

objetos.definicion: Utilities or pipeline network that is located underground or below a waterbody.
objetos.descripcion: For example, cables transmitting electrical power and/or communication signals and pipes carrying liquids, slurries, or gases.

objetos.definicion: A tube or passageway associated with a culvert which carries a watercourse (for example: a stream, a sewer, or a drain) under a route (for example: a road, a railway, or an embankment).
objetos.descripcion: Usually the construction of the route is unaffected.

objetos.definicion: A shaft sunk into the ground to reach and tap a supply of liquids and/or gases other than water intended for use in agriculture or domestic consumption.
objetos.descripcion: Typically drilled to tap underground reservoirs of hydrocarbons (for example: petroleum or natural gas). May also, for example, yield geothermally heated liquids for use in power generation or heating, or brine for use in the extraction of salt.

objetos.definicion: The location where there occurs a regulated discharge of pollutants (for example: from a pipe or a man-made ditch) into ground or surface waters.
objetos.descripcion: Pollutants include dredged spoil, solid waste, incinerator residue, sewage, garbage, sewage sludge, munitions, chemical wastes, biological materials, radioactive materials, heat, wrecked or discarded equipment, rock, sand, cellar dirt and industrial, municipal, and agricultural waste discharged into water. In the United States, permits for pollutant discharge are issued by the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), and such discharges are monitored and legal limits enforced.

objetos.definicion: A full set of equipment, capable of independent operation, used to generate power at a power station.
objetos.descripcion: In the case of electric power generation it includes all equipment up to the high-voltage terminal of the generator step-up transformer (IEEE 762). In the case of a steam electric power generating unit, it consists of individual boilers, any installed emission control equipment, and any steam turbine/generators dedicated to generating electricity. All combustion units/boilers/combined cycle turbines that produce steam for use in a single steam turbine/generator unit are part of the same electric power generating unit.

objetos.definicion: A vertical shaft that provides access to an underground aqueduct and which is part of a qanat system.
objetos.descripcion: A qanat system consists a system of deep underground tunnels especially constructed to channel water from an uphill region to a dryer lower region for use (for example: a village, a garden, a crop land), and qanat shafts to provide access from the surface to the underground tunnels.

objetos.definicion: A section of a transportation route where its size (for example: narrowing or expansion in width) and/or operating speed is significantly different than in the adjacent sections of the route.
objetos.descripcion: For example, an increase or decrease in the number of lanes in a road. Constrictions along or beside a transportation route may impede the flow of vehicles or people thus resulting in 'choke points'.

objetos.definicion: An intermediate stop, usually having minimal or no associated structures, along a transportation route, which serves as a place for disembarking or taking on passengers or freight.
objetos.descripcion: Transportation routes may include railway, pipeline, road, water or air. Associated structures could include a sign or small shelter. Some stops have no specific infrastructure and are known only by their location.

contenido: This Group consists of Concepts which relate to the sea navigation, to waterbodies in any form and/or other relevant Concepts.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which describe the coast and/or the littoral zones like beaches.

objetos.definicion: That part of a shore or beach which is usually dry, being reached only by the highest tides.
On a shore, the area on which the waves break and over which shore debris (for example: sand, shingle, and/or pebbles) accumulate.
objetos.descripcion: A beach includes backshore and foreshore.

objetos.definicion: A point from which exit can be made from a beach.
A location on a beach suitable for the landing of troops and vehicles.
A representation of the three dimensional relief of the beach along a line or series of connected lines.
A line generally following the contact between a land mass and a body of water that is based on the low water line.
objetos.descripcion: It is used as a reference for measuring international boundaries such as Territorial Limits or Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ). Consideration should be given to using the more specific Feature: 'Low Water Line' based on the nature of the source data collection.

objetos.definicion: A geographic region characterized by a historical accounting of shipping lane location, width, distribution, and use by vessel size.
objetos.descripcion: Used, for example, for mission planning to identify areas of high and low commercial traffic for the submarine navigator and sonarman.

objetos.definicion: A location where civilian diving activities take place.
objetos.descripcion: For example, training areas for diving schools.

objetos.definicion: An area on a water body bottom established to simulate a natural reef and intended to enhance fishery resources and commercial and/or recreational fishing opportunities.
objetos.descripcion: The haven (reef) is constructed by dumping (or emplacing) assorted scrap materials (or artificial structures) in areas which may be of very small extent or may stretch a considerable distance along a depth contour.

objetos.definicion: A geographic region describing the distribution of a marine species that may sustain a fishery.
objetos.descripcion: Fisheries may be characterized as commercial and/or artisanal.

objetos.definicion: A geographic region characterized by a historical level of large-scale (generally greater than 100 gross ton) commercial fishing activity.
objetos.descripcion: Typically only fishing vessels traveling at trawling speeds (typically not exceeding 6 knots) are included, and regions near the coastline (for example: less than 10 nautical miles) are excluded.

objetos.definicion: The part of the shore or beach which lies between the low water mark and the upper limit of normal wave action.
The line dividing the backshore and foreshore along a coast or beach as defined by the National Authority.

A routeing measure comprising a designated area between the landward boundary of a traffic separation scheme and the adjacent coast, to be used in accordance with the provisions of the International Regulations for Preventing Collisions at Sea.
A land mass, other than a continent, surrounded by water.
An enclosed area of salt or brackish water separated from the open sea by some more or less effective, but not complete, obstacle (for example: a sand bank).
objetos.descripcion: The name most commonly used for the area of water enclosed by a barrier reef or atoll.

objetos.definicion: An area of new land that has been reclaimed from an area previously covered by water.
objetos.descripcion: Commonly created by building embankments and draining water from an area.

objetos.definicion: The line where a land mass is in contact with a body of water and the tide state or river stage are unspecified.
objetos.descripcion: It may be in either the littoral or inland waters. In the littoral, consideration should be given to using the more specific high water or low water lines based on the nature of the source data collection.

objetos.definicion: The line dividing foreshore and nearshore along a coast at the seaward edge of the beach to which the sea recedes at low water.
An otherwise unspecified fixed structure which supports a Maritime Navigation Light.
objetos.descripcion: May also be used to support other aids to maritime navigation (for example: maritime radiobeacons or fog signals).

objetos.definicion: A signboard used to indicate speed restrictions, cable landings, and other items of interest to maritime navigation.
A place on shore from which signals are made to vessels at sea.
The part of the shore or beach which lies between the low water mark and the landward limit of the offshore region.
The comparatively flat zone of variable width that extends from the outer margin of the rather steeply sloping shoreface to the edge of the continental shelf.
An artificial structure that is located offshore.
objetos.descripcion: It usually has a surface that is raised above the sea and may be used as a working stage for conducting offshore operations (for example: drilling for petroleum and/or natural gas, loading and/or unloading vessels, or navigation support).

objetos.definicion: A location offshore where a pilot may board a vessel in preparation to piloting it through local waters.
objetos.descripcion: The pilot may either be stationed in a small craft cruising in the near vicinity of the designated location, or may be brought out from shore (for example: by a helicopter) upon request.

objetos.definicion: A mass of rock or coral which either reaches close to the sea surface or is exposed at low tide, posing a hazard to navigation.
The connected water areas of the Earth that surround the continents and are not completly surrounded by the landmass of a single continent.
objetos.descripcion: The areas differ in morphology and/or other natural characteristics and may be covered by ice.

objetos.definicion: An area where earthquakes or other seismic events routinely occur.
A line drawn along the normal limit of wave action above the higher high water line as defined by the National Authority.
objetos.descripcion: Consideration should be given to using the more specific Feature: 'High Water Line' based on the nature of the source data collection.

objetos.definicion: An artificial structure attached to land bordering a body of water and fixed in position.
objetos.descripcion: It is usually fixed to the waterbody bottom (for example: a mole) but may occasionally be fixed in position (for example: attached to the shore at one end and held between pilings at the other), but floating. Shoreline constructions are normally used for berthing and/or protection.

objetos.definicion: The line where a land mass is in contact with a body of water and is defined in terms of a specific tidal state, sounding datum and/or water condition.
objetos.descripcion: For example, a high water or low water line.

objetos.definicion: A geographically defined part of a waterbody (for example: the sea or other navigable waters).
objetos.descripcion: It may have a proper name (for example: Philippine Sea, Bismark Sea, or Coral Sea).

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which relate to ports, harbours and/or places where vessels can be moored.

objetos.definicion: A heavy object, kept in place on the seafloor by its weight and possibly with flukes, to which is attached a cable, rope, or chain that keeps a floating structure (for example, a buoy) on the waterbody surface positioned within a narrow region.
A designated area of water where a single vessel (for example: a ship or a sea plane) may anchor.
objetos.descripcion: Usually defined by a centre point and a swinging circle.

objetos.definicion: An area of relatively uniform water depth with no cables, pipelines, or hazardous obstructions present on the seafloor, in which vessels anchor or may anchor.
objetos.descripcion: Anchorage areas are additionally determined by: the depth of water in comparison to the tidal range; the material of the seafloor bottom; local environmental effects of wind and currents; and proximity to hazards to navigation, adjacent ships, and harbor traffic lanes. Although the anchorage refers to an identified area along the water surface, its physical structure is considered to be the material and condition of the seafloor below. An anchorage can be physically damaged by natural events (for example: an earthquake or tsunami) by which the preferred seafloor bottom type can change, or hazardous obstructions can be created or moved into the anchorage area.

objetos.definicion: A gate that impounds water within a basin or chamber that is used by watercraft.
objetos.descripcion: For example, gates used at locks or dry docks.

objetos.definicion: A named or numbered place where a vessel is moored at a wharf.
A structure primarily used as a berthing place for vessels.
objetos.descripcion: For example, a pier, a wharf, and a quay. Consideration should be given to using the more general Feature: 'Shoreline Construction' and a type-discriminating attribute.

objetos.definicion: A place where boats receive or discharge passengers and freight, but lacking most port facilities.
A small shaped post, mounted on the ground or pavement surface.
objetos.descripcion: Bollards may be mounted on a wharf or dolphin and used to secure ship's lines, or they may be mounted at intervals on the ground or pavement surface in order to protect critical infrastructure, delimit an area such as a roadway sidewalk or path, or to exclude vehicles. Bollards may be fixed above the surface or may be installed in housings below the surface so as to be very quickly raised into a blocking position to prevent the progress of threatening vehicles.

objetos.definicion: A structure that protects a waterbody region (for example: a shore, a harbour, and/or an anchorage) from water waves by preventing them from reaching the protected region or reducing their magnitude.
The location at which vessels are required to report to a traffic control center.
objetos.descripcion: Note that this is not the same as Feature: 'Aeronautical Waypoint' which is for aircraft only.

objetos.definicion: A geographic region characterized by a historical accounting of shipping lane location, width, distribution, and use by vessel size.
objetos.descripcion: Used, for example, for mission planning to identify areas of high and low commercial traffic for the submarine navigator and sonarman.

objetos.definicion: An artificially enclosed body of water within which vessels may moor and which may have gates used to regulate the interior water level.
A post or group of posts used for mooring, warping a ship or as an aid to navigation.
An area of the bottom of a body of water (for example: a channel) which has been deepened by dredging.
An artificial basin fitted with a gate or caisson into which vessels can be floated and the water pumped out to expose the bottom of the vessel.
The reservoir in a dry dock bounded by the dry dock wall and dry dock gate.
The gate at the end of a dry dock that excludes the water after pumping out the dock.
objetos.descripcion: The pumping engines are often located in the caisson.

objetos.definicion: The wall of a dry dock.
objetos.descripcion: Along with the dry dock gate it encloses the dry dock basin.

objetos.definicion: A man-made embankment to contain or hold back water.
An area on a water body bottom established to simulate a natural reef and intended to enhance fishery resources and commercial and/or recreational fishing opportunities.
objetos.descripcion: The haven (reef) is constructed by dumping (or emplacing) assorted scrap materials (or artificial structures) in areas which may be of very small extent or may stretch a considerable distance along a depth contour.

objetos.definicion: A harbour that is primarily used by fishing vessels.
A geographic region characterized by a historical level of large-scale (generally greater than 100 gross ton) commercial fishing activity.
objetos.descripcion: Typically only fishing vessels traveling at trawling speeds (typically not exceeding 6 knots) are included, and regions near the coastline (for example: less than 10 nautical miles) are excluded.

objetos.definicion: A form of dry dock consisting of a floating structure of one or more sections which can be partly submerged by controlled flooding to receive a vessel, then raised by pumping out the water so that the vessel's bottom can be exposed.
An artificial structure or gate that is utilized as a defense against flooding or storm surges.
objetos.descripcion: Consideration should be given to using the more specific Dam or Embankment features where appropriate in lieu of Flood Control Structure.

objetos.definicion: A timber structure in the intertidal zone serving as a support for vessels at low stages of the tide to permit work on the exposed portion of the vessel's hull.
A low artificial wall-like structure of durable material extending from the land to seaward for a particular purpose, such as to prevent coast erosion.
A natural or artificial improved body of water providing protection for vessels and generally anchorage and docking facilities.
objetos.descripcion: A harbour consists of both its port (see Feature: 'Port') and its waters (see Feature: 'Harbour Waters').

objetos.definicion: A natural or artificial improved body of water providing protection for vessels and usually associated with a port.
objetos.descripcion: Harbour waters and its related port (see Feature: 'Port') together comprise a harbour (see Feature: 'Harbour').

objetos.definicion: Steps at the shoreline as the connection between land and water on different levels.
An enclosure with a pair or series of gates used for raising or lowering vessels as they pass from one water level to another.
The reservoir in a lock, bounded by lock walls and lock gates.
The pair of massive hinged doors at each end of a lock.
One of the pair of walls, usually masonary, that contain a lock basin and support the lock gates.
An inclined plane used to dump logs into the water for transport, or to haul logs out of the water for processing.

A sloping structure that can either be used, as a landing place, at variable water levels, for small vessels (for example: landing ships and ferry boats), or for hauling a cradle carrying a small vessel.
objetos.descripcion: The cradle may travel on rails.

objetos.definicion: A facing of stone or other material, either permanent or temporary, placed along the edge of a stream, river or canal to stabilize the bank and to protect it from the erosive action of the water.
An otherwise unspecified fixed structure which supports a Maritime Navigation Light.
objetos.descripcion: May also be used to support other aids to maritime navigation (for example: maritime radiobeacons or fog signals).

objetos.definicion: A signboard used to indicate speed restrictions, cable landings, and other items of interest to maritime navigation.
An electronic aid to maritime navigation consisting of a radio transmitter that broadcasts distinctive signals.
A form of breakwater alongside which vessels may lie on the sheltered side only.
objetos.descripcion: It is usually a substantial masonry structure, and often serves as a breakwater on its outer side while offering facilities for ships in its inner side. In some cases it may lie entirely within an artificial harbour, permitting vessels to lie along both sides.

objetos.definicion: A chain or similar physical connection (for example: a cable) used to moor a vessel.
objetos.descripcion: For example, used between an anchor and a mooring buoy or between a bollard on a dock and a hulk.

objetos.definicion: The equipment or structure used to secure a vessel.
A metal ring attached to a structure and used to secure a vessel.
Complex feature with possible components: BB019, BC098.
A location offshore where a pilot may board a vessel in preparation to piloting it through local waters.
objetos.descripcion: The pilot may either be stationed in a small craft cruising in the near vicinity of the designated location, or may be brought out from shore (for example: by a helicopter) upon request.

objetos.definicion: An airtight air-filled hollow structure, usually rectangular in shape, which is buoyant in water.
objetos.descripcion: Pontoons have enough buoyancy to float both themselves and a significant load. Pontoons may serve as supports for bridges or piers.

objetos.definicion: A place provided with terminal and transfer facilities for loading and/or discharging cargo or passengers, usually located in a harbour.
objetos.descripcion: A port and its related waters (see Feature: 'Harbour Waters') together comprise a harbour (see Feature: 'Harbour').

objetos.definicion: A layer of broken rock, cobbles, boulders, or fragments of sufficient size to resist the erosive forces of flowing water and wave action.
An area near the shore where vessels can anchor in safety, usually a shallow indentation in the coast.
objetos.descripcion: They are often located outside of harbours that are restricted by size, depth, or operating capacity, and are typically used for lightering operations and unofficial anchoring.

objetos.definicion: An embankment or wall for protection against waves or tidal action along a shore or water front.
A large enclosed area adjoining the sea or a major river, including facilities in which ships are built or repaired.
An artificial structure attached to land bordering a body of water and fixed in position.
objetos.descripcion: It is usually fixed to the waterbody bottom (for example: a mole) but may occasionally be fixed in position (for example: attached to the shore at one end and held between pilings at the other), but floating. Shoreline constructions are normally used for berthing and/or protection.

objetos.definicion: A ramp-like structure on a shoreline that is intended to facilitate the movement of vessels and/or materials (for example: logs) into or out of the water.
A mooring structure used by tankers to load and unload in port approaches or in offshore oil and/or gas fields.
objetos.descripcion: The size of the structure may vary between that of a large mooring buoy and that of a manned structure that may be either floating or fixed to the sea bed.

objetos.definicion: The prepared and usually reinforced inclined surface on which keel- and bilge-blocks are laid for supporting a vessel under construction.
objetos.descripcion: Rails associated with a slipway are usually represented separately, for example as a marine railway.

objetos.definicion: A place at which a service generally of interest to small craft or pleasure boats is available.
A location where one or more devices have been temporarily or permanently stationed for the purpose of collecting information regarding vehicular and/or pedestrian traffic.
objetos.descripcion: Such information may include analysis of traffic flow, turning movements, speeds, congestion and delays, parking and loading, and pedestrian movement.

objetos.definicion: A wall, bank or jetty often submerged, built to direct or confine the flow of a river or tidal current or to promote scour actions.
A mechanical device for lifting vessels from the water.
objetos.descripcion: The device may be, for example, a stationary crane or a wheeled vehicle. After removal from the water the vessel may be maintained (for example: cleaning the hull of encrustations) or stored (for example: moved to a building, shed, or lot for winter storage).

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which are used to describe the depths of waterbodies.

objetos.definicion: A water area whose depth is within a defined range of values.
A line connecting points of equal depth at and below the hydrographic datum.
objetos.descripcion: Depth contours follow the rules for contour formation, that is, contours must close on themselves, must be continuous, and must precisely represent the shape of the bottom. Depth contours are usually based on detailed bathymetric information.

objetos.definicion: A navigational safety line indicating that no sounding of a lesser depth exists seaward of the line, but greater depths may occur on the shallow side of the line.
objetos.descripcion: Depth curves should not be confused with Feature: 'Depth Contour'. Depth curves are generalised, are biased towards safety of navigation, and do not fully follow the rules for contour formation, that is, contours must close on themselves, must be continuous, and must precisely represent the shape of the bottom.

objetos.definicion: A location where civilian diving activities take place.
objetos.descripcion: For example, training areas for diving schools.

objetos.definicion: An area of the bottom of a body of water (for example: a channel) which has been deepened by dredging.
An area of horizontal coverage recorded by side scan SONAR survey.
A spot depth or drying height that has been referenced to a vertical datum.
A region that has been determined to be clear of navigational dangers to a specified depth.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which describe the bottom of a waterbody.

objetos.definicion: A region of marine plants that grow in long narrow ribbons.
objetos.descripcion: Algae may be moored or floating. For example, sea grass, kelp, or sargasso.

objetos.definicion: A region of a waterbody bottom that is homogeneous with respect to a measurement (for example: consistency, color, and/or composition).
objetos.aliases: Seabed Area, Quality of the Bottom, Bottom Characteristics

objetos.definicion: A region of a waterbody bottom that is homogeneous with respect to form (for example: seamounts or sand waves).
A sea area where dredged material or other potentially more harmful material (for example: explosives or chemical waste) is deliberately deposited.
A region over which it is safe to navigate but which should be avoided for anchoring, intentional grounding, or ground fishing.
An object on the sea floor (for example: a wreck) that, when detected (for example: using acoustic or magnetic sensors), appears similar to and could be confused with a operating submarine.
A mass of rock or coral which either reaches close to the sea surface or is exposed at low tide, posing a hazard to navigation.
A clearing away of mud or other seabed deposits by the action of an object impacting and/or traversing along the seabed before settling.
A flow of underground water that emerges naturally from the seafloor.
objetos.descripcion: A submarine spring occurs when a water table or aquitard intersects with the ground surface offshore. A submarine spring is relatively cool in temperature and has far less salinity than the seawater it is entering, resulting in a brackish water condition.

objetos.definicion: An underwater hill or mountain situated over an opening or openings in the Earth's crust through which lava, steam, and/or gases, are or have been expelled.
objetos.descripcion: Underwater volcanoes that have grown to the point of emerging above the water surface are usually collected as Feature: Volcano, or as Feature: Volcano within the perimeter of a Feature: Island.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which relate to constructions and production installations which are placed in the offshore area.

objetos.definicion: An area in a shallow portion of a body of water, usually at the mouth of a river, where logs are collected, staged, and formed into log booms for further transportation and delivery to a logging mill.
objetos.descripcion: The booming ground foundation is commonly constructed of piles or large stones placed into cribs within the waterbody to aid in shaping the log assembly into alignment with the outer logs forming the log boom barrier itself.

objetos.definicion: A permanent structure set in the water, typically framed with wooden beams and filled with rocks or boulders that is used to anchor log booms or support other constructions (for example: submerged outfalls, diffusers, or piers).
objetos.descripcion: They may always be dry, submerged, or covered and uncovered. Cribs should not be confused with water intake towers which may sometimes also be termed a 'crib'.

objetos.definicion: A structure in shallow water for fishing purposes that may be a hazard to navigation.
objetos.descripcion: The position of these structures may vary frequently over time.

objetos.definicion: A floating barrier used to protect a region of a body of water or to create a sheltered area on a body of water for storage purposes.
objetos.descripcion: For example, a boom placed around an oil tanker to catch accidental releases of oil or placed so as to enclose and contain rafted logs.

objetos.definicion: A floating barrier, anchored to the bottom, used to deflect the path of floating ice in order to prevent obstruction (for example: of lock basins and/or water intakes) and/or to prevent damage to structures (for example: to bridge piers).
Equipment located at or below water level where liquids (for example: cooling water) are spread out.
A floating barrier used to enclose and contain rafted logs.
A self-contained floatable or floating drilling machine that appears as an offshore working platform when in position for operations.
objetos.descripcion: Constructed in many forms, for example, as a jackup, a semisubmersible, and as a fully submersible.

objetos.definicion: The comparatively flat zone of variable width that extends from the outer margin of the rather steeply sloping shoreface to the edge of the continental shelf.
An artificial structure that is located offshore.
objetos.descripcion: It usually has a surface that is raised above the sea and may be used as a working stage for conducting offshore operations (for example: drilling for petroleum and/or natural gas, loading and/or unloading vessels, or navigation support).

objetos.definicion: An offshore structure with a flat surface raised above the sea, used as a working stage for conducting offshore operations.
objetos.descripcion: May be fixed or floating.

objetos.definicion: A floating barrier to stop and contain the spread of oil on a waterbody surface.
A connected set of pipes for conveying liquids, slurries, or gases.
objetos.descripcion: Usually for long distances and often located underground.

objetos.definicion: Shallow pools, normally man-made, used for the natural evaporation of water for the collection of salt.
A place where sewerage may be pumped off a vessel.

A long pile (for example: a heavy timber or section of steel, wood, or concrete) forced into the earth that may serve as a support (for example: for a pier) or as a free standing pole within a marine environment.
An area where nets used for catching tunny (tuna) have been deployed.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which relate to tidal issues and/or to the currents of water.

objetos.definicion: A circular movement of water usually formed, where currents pass obstructions between two adjacent currents flowing counter to each other, or along the edge of a permanent current.
The line dividing foreshore and nearshore along a coast at the seaward edge of the beach to which the sea recedes at low water.
The location in a tidally influenced stream where observations are taken.
objetos.descripcion: Tidal stream observation stations are either embedded in the seafloor or attached to a buoy. They measure the speed and direction of tidally influenced water movement.

objetos.definicion: Any water the level of which changes periodically due to tidal action.
A station containing an instrument for measuring the height of the tide.
A natural watercourse in tidal areas where water flows during the ebb or flood.
objetos.descripcion: For example, a channel through which a tidal current runs.

objetos.definicion: A waterbody region in which a water current persists.
objetos.descripcion: For example, a tidal stream or an ocean current.

objetos.definicion: A location at which water-related measurements are taken.
objetos.descripcion: Water measurements include, for example: water chemistry and/or quality; water depth, volume or velocity; and water presence variability or seasonality.

objetos.definicion: A disturbance of water caused by the interaction of any combination of waves, currents, eddies, tidal streams, wind, shoals, and obstructions.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which relate to the navigation on sea.

objetos.definicion: The geographic location at which a set of acoustic observations were taken.
A region of waterborne cellular or vascular plants (for example: algae, grasses, reeds, and water hyacinths).
objetos.descripcion: The vegetation may moored (for example: sea grass and reeds) or floating (for example: sargasso and water hyacinths).

objetos.definicion: A floating object moored to the bottom in a particular place, as an aid to navigation or for other specific purposes.
The location at which vessels are required to report to a traffic control center.
objetos.descripcion: Note that this is not the same as Feature: 'Aeronautical Waypoint' which is for aircraft only.

objetos.definicion: That part of a body of water, either ocean or inland, (sometimes dredged) deep enough for navigation through an area otherwise not navigable.
objetos.descripcion: It is usually marked by a single or double line of buoys and sometimes by leading lines. It is often the deepest part of a stream, bay or strait through which the main current flows.

objetos.definicion: A length or single point along a route that due to its width, surface quality, alignment, fixed human activity or fixed human feature is likely to impede movement at a constant speed resulting in slowing, and either by vehicular bunching or by type may cause temporary halts.
A geographic region characterized by a historical accounting of shipping lane location, width, distribution, and use by vessel size.
objetos.descripcion: Used, for example, for mission planning to identify areas of high and low commercial traffic for the submarine navigator and sonarman.

objetos.definicion: An area of the bottom of a body of water (for example: a channel) which has been deepened by dredging.
An area containing structures (usually portable) for catching fish.
A geographic region characterized by a historical level of large-scale (generally greater than 100 gross ton) commercial fishing activity.
objetos.descripcion: Typically only fishing vessels traveling at trawling speeds (typically not exceeding 6 knots) are included, and regions near the coastline (for example: less than 10 nautical miles) are excluded.

objetos.definicion: A device (for example: located on a vessel or an aid to navigation) that transmits a warning signal during periods of low visibility, especially due to fog.
A natural or artificial improved body of water providing protection for vessels and generally anchorage and docking facilities.
objetos.descripcion: A harbour consists of both its port (see Feature: 'Port') and its waters (see Feature: 'Harbour Waters').

objetos.definicion: A routeing measure comprising a designated area between the landward boundary of a traffic separation scheme and the adjacent coast, to be used in accordance with the provisions of the International Regulations for Preventing Collisions at Sea.
A small, insubstantial navigational mark.
objetos.descripcion: For example, a staff placed on top of a rock or shoal to mark a hazard or serve as a navigational aid.

objetos.definicion: A buoy used to indicate a lateral limit of navigable water.
Two or more lights associated so as to form a leading line to be followed.
A line which passes through at least two clearly defined objects, along which a vessel can safely travel.
A sector defined by bearings from seaward within which a light shows a specified character or color, or is obscured.
A distinctively marked vessel anchored or moored at a charted point, to serve as an aid to navigation.
objetos.descripcion: By night, it displays a characteristic light(s) and is usually equipped with other devices (for example: a fog signal, a submarine sound signal, and/or a radio-beacon) to assist navigation.

objetos.definicion: A distinctive structure on or off a coast exhibiting a major light designed to serve as an aid to navigation.
Lights marking area limits, the alignment of an electrical cable, alignments for anchoring, or serving a similar purpose but not marking direction or course.
The geographic location at which a set of magnetic observations were taken.
A device used for the collection of hydrographic and oceanographic data.
A surveyed reference track marking the centre-line of a marine test range.
objetos.descripcion: Vessels undergoing testing must maintain position along this track.

objetos.definicion: Generally, an area where the mariner has to be made aware of circumstances influencing the safety of navigation.
objetos.descripcion: The caution may represent a specific danger, a general risk, or a rule and/or navigation advice that is not directly related to a specific object. Appropriate consideration should be given, for example, to the use of Features: 'Wreck', 'Hazardous Rock' and 'Well'.

objetos.definicion: A prominent, specially constructed object forming a conspicuous mark as a fixed aid to navigation or for use in hydrographic survey.
A luminous or lighted device intended for the purpose of aiding maritime navigation.
objetos.descripcion: A Maritime Navigation Light refers to the light itself including its housing but does not include any support structure or ancillary aids to maritime navigation.

objetos.definicion: An otherwise unspecified fixed structure which supports a Maritime Navigation Light.
objetos.descripcion: May also be used to support other aids to maritime navigation (for example: maritime radiobeacons or fog signals).

objetos.definicion: A coloured (usually white) mark on a vertical surface (for example: a cliff, a rocky outcrop, and/or a wall) that is a conspicuous landmark for maritime navigation.
A light-reflecting device that is secured to an unlit maritime navigation aid in order to distinguish its location and purpose at night.
objetos.descripcion: The retro-reflector may be either a self-contained unit affixed to another structure or consist of a material or coating applied directly to the surface of that structure. The colour and colour patten of the retro-reflector is based on either the Standard Code or the Comprehensive Code referenced within International Association of Lighthouse Authorities (IALA) E-106.

objetos.definicion: A signboard used to indicate speed restrictions, cable landings, and other items of interest to maritime navigation.
A track along which ships may be guided by coastal radar stations, especially in the event of reduced visibility.
A track or lane established for the safe passage of vessels.
A place on shore from which signals are made to vessels at sea.
A maritime course, the length of which has been accurately measured, whose endpoints are often established by leading lines.
objetos.descripcion: It is used by vessels to calibrate logs, engine revolution counters, and other onboard equipment, and to determine speed.

objetos.definicion: An area where Mine Counter Measure operations have taken place.
objetos.descripcion: Operation could comprise detection but not neccessarily removal or neutralisation.

objetos.definicion: A straight line extending towards an area of navigational interest and generally generated by two navigational aids or one navigational aid and a bearing.
A location offshore where a pilot may board a vessel in preparation to piloting it through local waters.
objetos.descripcion: The pilot may either be stationed in a small craft cruising in the near vicinity of the designated location, or may be brought out from shore (for example: by a helicopter) upon request.

objetos.definicion: A location on a watercourse that has ramps, structural piles, and/or piers constructed on one or both shores to allow for suitable future crossing operations using floating bridges or rafting equipment.
objetos.descripcion: For example, a prepared float bridge site or a prepared raft site.

objetos.definicion: Indicates the coverage of a sea area by a radar surveillance station.
objetos.descripcion: Inside this area a vessel may request shore based radar assistance, particularly in poor visibility.

objetos.definicion: A facility utilizing radar to detect and analyze objects (for example: aircraft, artificial satellites, asteroids, and/or missiles) and/or environmental phenomena (for example: tornadoes).
objetos.descripcion: May include both a radar aerial as well as a structure housing radar equipment.

objetos.definicion: A sign placed by an authority charged with the regulation of traffic along a transportation route for the purpose of regulating the flow of traffic (for example: vessels, vehicles and/or pedestrians) and/or providing information pertinent to the control of that traffic.
A route established for the safe passage of vessels through offshore oil and gas fields and minefields.
That part of an inland body of water where the depth is relatively slight (less than 1 metre) and thus likely to limit the passage of watercraft.
objetos.descripcion: Shallow water areas may be identified using overhead imagery, where there are visible bottom features, surface waves, and/or other water surface phenomena.

objetos.definicion: A device used to raise ships vertically between water bodies with different elevations.
objetos.descripcion: Normally ship elevators consist of water filled chambers which can be raised or lowered by means of mechanical devices. Commonly used to move ships between canals where locks would be impractical.

objetos.definicion: An acoustic aid to navigation consisting of a device that generates distinctive audible sounds.
objetos.descripcion: For example, a buoy with a bell. See also Feature: 'Fog Signal'.

objetos.definicion: A region that has been determined to be clear of navigational dangers to a specified depth.
A line of known direction from a fixed location that is used to determine accurate positions of a vessel on certain test ranges.
A characteristic shape secured at the top of a buoy or beacon to aid in its identification.
The actual path or route of a craft over the ground or sea bottom.
objetos.descripcion: May be used to delineate the graphic representation of the route rather than the actual route.

objetos.definicion: An area of horizontal coverage recorded by SONAR array systems.
A location where one or more devices have been temporarily or permanently stationed for the purpose of collecting information regarding vehicular and/or pedestrian traffic.
objetos.descripcion: Such information may include analysis of traffic flow, turning movements, speeds, congestion and delays, parking and loading, and pedestrian movement.

objetos.definicion: A maritime routeing measure that separates opposing streams of traffic by appropriate means.
objetos.descripcion: For example, traffic lanes and traffic circles. Often referred to by its acronym, TSS.

objetos.definicion: An enlargement of a channel to permit the turning of vessels.
A location at which currents, tides, and/or other types of water movement are specified.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which relate to a hazard and/or an obstruction for navigation on sea.

objetos.definicion: A region of marine plants that grow in long narrow ribbons.
objetos.descripcion: Algae may be moored or floating. For example, sea grass, kelp, or sargasso.

objetos.definicion: A facility involved in the culturing or farming (including harvesting) of aquatic organisms (for example: fish, mollusks, crustaceans, plants, crocodiles, alligators or amphibians) using techniques designed to increase the production of the organisms in question beyond the natural capacity of the environment (for example: regular stocking, feeding and protection from predators).
objetos.descripcion: Culturing or farming refers to the rearing of individuals up to their juvenile and/or adult phase under captive conditions. In addition, it also encompasses individual, corporate or state ownership of the individual organisms throughout the rearing or culture stage, up to and including harvesting.

objetos.definicion: A region of waterborne cellular or vascular plants (for example: algae, grasses, reeds, and water hyacinths).
objetos.descripcion: The vegetation may moored (for example: sea grass and reeds) or floating (for example: sargasso and water hyacinths).

objetos.definicion: An area in a shallow portion of a body of water, usually at the mouth of a river, where logs are collected, staged, and formed into log booms for further transportation and delivery to a logging mill.
objetos.descripcion: The booming ground foundation is commonly constructed of piles or large stones placed into cribs within the waterbody to aid in shaping the log assembly into alignment with the outer logs forming the log boom barrier itself.

objetos.definicion: A region of a waterbody bottom that is homogeneous with respect to a measurement (for example: consistency, color, and/or composition).
objetos.aliases: Seabed Area, Quality of the Bottom, Bottom Characteristics

objetos.definicion: A region of a waterbody bottom that is homogeneous with respect to form (for example: seamounts or sand waves).
Waves which break over off-lying shoals or near the shore.

A structure that connects two locations and provides for the passage of a transportation route (for example: a road or a railway) over a terrain obstacle (for example: a waterbody, a gully, and/or a road).
objetos.descripcion: A bridge consists of a set of two abutments and/or zero or more bridge piers joined by bridge spans. A bridge may serve, for example, as an overpass or a viaduct. In the context of a bridge, the scope of the term 'transportation route' includes the transportation of liquids or gases by means of either pipelines or aqueducts.

objetos.definicion: A component of the deck of a bridge spanning successive bridge piers.
A single continuous rope-like bundle consisting of multiple strands.
objetos.descripcion: The strands may be individually insulated and/or protected and the cable as a whole sheathed. Cables may be used for load bearing (for example, supporting or suspending equipment and/or structures), transmitting electrical power, and/or communicating signals (for example, by electrical or optical means).

objetos.definicion: A small insular feature, which may contain scant vegetation; usually composed of sand or coral.
objetos.descripcion: Often applied to smaller coral shoals.

objetos.definicion: A length or single point along a route that due to its width, surface quality, alignment, fixed human activity or fixed human feature is likely to impede movement at a constant speed resulting in slowing, and either by vehicular bunching or by type may cause temporary halts.

A permanent structure set in the water, typically framed with wooden beams and filled with rocks or boulders that is used to anchor log booms or support other constructions (for example: submerged outfalls, diffusers, or piers).
objetos.descripcion: They may always be dry, submerged, or covered and uncovered. Cribs should not be confused with water intake towers which may sometimes also be termed a 'crib'.

objetos.definicion: The site at which has occurred a serious disruption of the functioning of a community or a society causing widespread human, material, economic or environmental losses which exceed the ability of the affected community or society to cope using its own resources.
A region of water having a colour distinctly different from that of the surrounding region.
A post or group of posts used for mooring, warping a ship or as an aid to navigation.
A circular movement of water usually formed, where currents pass obstructions between two adjacent currents flowing counter to each other, or along the edge of a permanent current.
An explosive device used in naval warfare deployed on or below the sea surface.
An area on a water body bottom established to simulate a natural reef and intended to enhance fishery resources and commercial and/or recreational fishing opportunities.
objetos.descripcion: The haven (reef) is constructed by dumping (or emplacing) assorted scrap materials (or artificial structures) in areas which may be of very small extent or may stretch a considerable distance along a depth contour.

objetos.definicion: An area containing structures (usually portable) for catching fish.
A fence of stakes or wall of stones set in a river or along the shore to direct fish towards fish traps or nets.
objetos.descripcion: The weir is shaped so as to encourage fish to naturally congregate, usually based on river or tidal flow. Although generally consisting of linear segments on rivers, in shore areas one or more components may be curved so as to form an enclosure with a narrow entrance. When constructed of stones the thickness of the wall constitutes a permanent hazard to maritime navigation.

objetos.definicion: Poles or stakes placed in shallow water to outline fishing grounds or to catch fish.
A structure in shallow water for fishing purposes that may be a hazard to navigation.
objetos.descripcion: The position of these structures may vary frequently over time.

objetos.definicion: A floating barrier used to protect a region of a body of water or to create a sheltered area on a body of water for storage purposes.
objetos.descripcion: For example, a boom placed around an oil tanker to catch accidental releases of oil or placed so as to enclose and contain rafted logs.

objetos.definicion: A region over which it is safe to navigate but which should be avoided for anchoring, intentional grounding, or ground fishing.
An isolated rocky formation or a single large stone or coral, usually one constituting a danger to navigation.
objetos.descripcion: May be either dry, awash, or below the water surface.

objetos.definicion: A vessel, either stranded aground or permanently moored, that is no longer seaworthy due to an inoperable propulsion plant or compromised vessel integrity.

A floating barrier, anchored to the bottom, used to deflect the path of floating ice in order to prevent obstruction (for example: of lock basins and/or water intakes) and/or to prevent damage to structures (for example: to bridge piers).
An object protruding above the water body bottom of which at least one component of height, width or length is a minimum of 5 metres.
objetos.descripcion: These include: rocks (for example: pinnacles), underwater constructions (for example: wellheads and other equipment in oil and gas fields), wrecks, and other man-made debris (for example: lost ground tackle or dumped materials).

objetos.definicion: A floating barrier used to enclose and contain rafted logs.

A site where marine organisms are cultivated for food and other products in either the open ocean, in an enclosed section of the ocean, or in tanks, ponds or raceways that are filled with seawater (for example: the farming of marine fish, prawns, or oysters in saltwater ponds).
In maritime navigation, anything that hinders or prevents movement, particularly anything that endangers or prevents passage of a vessel.
objetos.descripcion: The term is usually used to refer to an isolated danger to navigation.

objetos.definicion: An otherwise unspecified fixed structure which supports a Maritime Navigation Light.
objetos.descripcion: May also be used to support other aids to maritime navigation (for example: maritime radiobeacons or fog signals).

objetos.definicion: An area where Mine Counter Measure operations have taken place.
objetos.descripcion: Operation could comprise detection but not neccessarily removal or neutralisation.

objetos.definicion: A self-contained floatable or floating drilling machine that appears as an offshore working platform when in position for operations.
objetos.descripcion: Constructed in many forms, for example, as a jackup, a semisubmersible, and as a fully submersible.

objetos.definicion: A chain or similar physical connection (for example: a cable) used to moor a vessel.
objetos.descripcion: For example, used between an anchor and a mooring buoy or between a bollard on a dock and a hulk.

objetos.definicion: An object on the sea floor (for example: a wreck) that, when detected (for example: using acoustic or magnetic sensors), appears similar to and could be confused with a operating submarine.
An offshore structure with a flat surface raised above the sea, used as a working stage for conducting offshore operations.
objetos.descripcion: May be fixed or floating.

objetos.definicion: A floating barrier to stop and contain the spread of oil on a waterbody surface.
A connected set of pipes for conveying liquids, slurries, or gases.
objetos.descripcion: Usually for long distances and often located underground.

objetos.definicion: An airtight air-filled hollow structure, usually rectangular in shape, which is buoyant in water.
objetos.descripcion: Pontoons have enough buoyancy to float both themselves and a significant load. Pontoons may serve as supports for bridges or piers.

objetos.definicion: A mass of rock or coral which either reaches close to the sea surface or is exposed at low tide, posing a hazard to navigation.
The deteriorated remains of an unspecified structure.
That part of an inland body of water where the depth is relatively slight (less than 1 metre) and thus likely to limit the passage of watercraft.
objetos.descripcion: Shallow water areas may be identified using overhead imagery, where there are visible bottom features, surface waves, and/or other water surface phenomena.

objetos.definicion: An object protruding above the water body bottom whose greatest dimension is less than five metres.
objetos.descripcion: The object may, depending on conditions, float and/or be partially exposed above the water surface. In general such objects appear as 'mine-like' contacts on sonar sensors and will be further investigated in situations where the presence of explosive mines is suspected.

objetos.definicion: A substantial item of woody vegetation (for example: tree, trunk, or bush) or a broken structural pile that is embedded in the bottom of a body of water (for example: ocean, river or inland waterbody) thereby creating a hazard to water travel.
objetos.descripcion: The visibility of the snag at the water surface will depend in its size and the existing water depth.

objetos.definicion: A long pile (for example: a heavy timber or section of steel, wood, or concrete) forced into the earth that may serve as a support (for example: for a pier) or as a free standing pole within a marine environment.
An underwater hill or mountain situated over an opening or openings in the Earth's crust through which lava, steam, and/or gases, are or have been expelled.
objetos.descripcion: Underwater volcanoes that have grown to the point of emerging above the water surface are usually collected as Feature: Volcano, or as Feature: Volcano within the perimeter of a Feature: Island.

objetos.definicion: An area where nets used for catching tunny (tuna) have been deployed.
The ruined remains of a stranded or sunken vessel that has been rendered useless.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which relate to sea ice.

objetos.definicion: A floating barrier, anchored to the bottom, used to deflect the path of floating ice in order to prevent obstruction (for example: of lock basins and/or water intakes) and/or to prevent damage to structures (for example: to bridge piers).
A floating ice sheet of considerable thickness that is normally attached to the land along its landward edge.
objetos.descripcion: Ice shelves are the seaward extension of land glaciers. Limited areas of the ice shelf may be aground where the glacier first enters the water and possibly in other places offshore. Ice shelves are usually of great horizontal extent and have a level or gently undulating surface. The seaward edge of an ice shelf is termed an 'ice cliff'.

objetos.definicion: Term used in a wide sense to include any area of sea ice other than fast ice.
objetos.descripcion: Pack ice commonly consists of connected floating plates of ice and has a mosaic look. Fast Ice is defined as sea ice which remains fast, generally in the position where originally formed, and which may attain a considerable thickness. Fast ice is found along coasts, where it is attached to the shore, or over shoals, where it may be held in position by islands, grounded icebergs, or grounded polar ice.

objetos.definicion: Sea ice that is more than one year old and more than 3 metres thick.
objetos.descripcion: Sea ice is any form of ice which has originated from sea water.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which are used to describe water zones where special actions and/or behaviours are restricted, regulated or permitted.

objetos.definicion: A facility involved in the culturing or farming (including harvesting) of aquatic organisms (for example: fish, mollusks, crustaceans, plants, crocodiles, alligators or amphibians) using techniques designed to increase the production of the organisms in question beyond the natural capacity of the environment (for example: regular stocking, feeding and protection from predators).
objetos.descripcion: Culturing or farming refers to the rearing of individuals up to their juvenile and/or adult phase under captive conditions. In addition, it also encompasses individual, corporate or state ownership of the individual organisms throughout the rearing or culture stage, up to and including harvesting.

objetos.definicion: An area of land and/or sea especially dedicated to the protection and maintenance of biological diversity, and of natural and associated cultural resources, and managed through legal or other effective means.
objetos.descripcion: As determined, for example, by the International Union for Conservation of Nature and Natural Resources (IUCN).

objetos.definicion: A location where civilian diving activities take place.
objetos.descripcion: For example, training areas for diving schools.

objetos.definicion: A sea area where dredged material or other potentially more harmful material (for example: explosives or chemical waste) is deliberately deposited.
An area on a water body bottom established to simulate a natural reef and intended to enhance fishery resources and commercial and/or recreational fishing opportunities.
objetos.descripcion: The haven (reef) is constructed by dumping (or emplacing) assorted scrap materials (or artificial structures) in areas which may be of very small extent or may stretch a considerable distance along a depth contour.

objetos.definicion: An area containing structures (usually portable) for catching fish.
A geographic region describing the distribution of a marine species that may sustain a fishery.
objetos.descripcion: Fisheries may be characterized as commercial and/or artisanal.

objetos.definicion: A site where marine organisms are cultivated for food and other products in either the open ocean, in an enclosed section of the ocean, or in tanks, ponds or raceways that are filled with seawater (for example: the farming of marine fish, prawns, or oysters in saltwater ponds).
An area in which certain activities or factors of significance to navigation and/or operation apply.
Generally, an area where the mariner has to be made aware of circumstances influencing the safety of navigation.
objetos.descripcion: The caution may represent a specific danger, a general risk, or a rule and/or navigation advice that is not directly related to a specific object. Appropriate consideration should be given, for example, to the use of Features: 'Wreck', 'Hazardous Rock' and 'Well'.

objetos.definicion: A line where on either side certain activities or factors of significance to navigation and/or operation apply.
A signboard used to indicate speed restrictions, cable landings, and other items of interest to maritime navigation.
An area where Naval forces (for example: vessels or aircraft) conduct firing and/or munition exercises.
objetos.descripcion: Distinguished from areas where Naval forces conduct general operations and manoeuvers.

objetos.definicion: An area where Naval forces conduct operations.
objetos.descripcion: Distinguished from areas where Naval forces conduct firing and/or munition exercises.

objetos.definicion: A region in which certain aspects of maritime navigation are restricted.
The connected water areas of the Earth that surround the continents and are not completly surrounded by the landmass of a single continent.
objetos.descripcion: The areas differ in morphology and/or other natural characteristics and may be covered by ice.

objetos.definicion: A designated portion of water that is outlined by visual surface markings and used by seaplanes to land and take-off.
objetos.aliases: Seaplane Landing Area, Seaplane Take-off Area

objetos.definicion: An artificial structure subdividing a waterbody.
objetos.descripcion: May consist of an artificial earthen embankment subdividing a pond or rice paddy, or an artificial partition (constructed, for example, from concrete or steel) subdividing a fish hatchery tank or water treatment plant aeration tank.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which relate to waterbodies without tides.

objetos.definicion: An area within which lakes are disappearing due to either the diversion of inflowing water or the desposition of (typically fine) sediments and plant colonization.
objetos.descripcion: Examples of water diversion include the Aral Sea and Lake Chad.

objetos.definicion: A pipe or artificial channel that is designed to transport water from a remote source, usually by gravity, for freshwater supply, agricultural, and/or industrial use.
objetos.descripcion: It may be supported by a bridge.

objetos.definicion: An underground layer of water-bearing permeable rock or unconsolidated materials (for example: gravel, sand, silt, or clay).
objetos.descripcion: It may yield economically significant quantities of groundwater to wells and springs.

objetos.definicion: A region along the edge of a body of water or watercourse generally dominated by riparian vegetation.
objetos.descripcion: May extend up to approximately 100 metres from the water edge, often including land subject to inundation and, if vegetation is present, commonly dominated by woody vegetation.

objetos.definicion: A gate that impounds water within a basin or chamber that is used by watercraft.
objetos.descripcion: For example, gates used at locks or dry docks.

objetos.definicion: A permanently wet area of land consisting of incompletely decayed organic material and mainly stagnant fresh water.
objetos.descripcion: It is generally too soft to bear the weight of any heavy body. A subtype of the more generalized Feature: 'Wetland'.

objetos.definicion: An artificial waterway with no flow, or a controlled flow, usable or built for navigation.
An elevated irrigation system revolving around a central pivot point.
A man-made container used for the collection and/or storage of water.
A watercourse that is covered, preventing its observation or further classification.
objetos.descripcion: For example, an underground river, a sewer, and an aqueduct tunnel.

objetos.definicion: An enclosed channel for carrying a watercourse (for example: a stream, a sewer, or a drain) under a route (for example: a road, a railway, or an embankment).
objetos.descripcion: Usually the construction of the route is unaffected.

objetos.definicion: A barrier constructed to hold back water and raise its level to form a reservoir or to prevent flooding.
An artificial waterway with no flow, or a controlled flow, usually unlined, used for draining or irrigating land.
A boundary defined by all or part of the outer limit of a drainage basin, which distinguishes the headstreams that are tributaries to different river systems or basins.
A man-made open container holding water for animals to drink.
An apparatus for drawing water directly from a main, especially alongside a street or road, consisting of a pipe with one or more nozzles or spouts, to which a hose of a fire-engine may be attached.
A facility involved in the breeding (hatching and associated activities) and cultivation (raising for release or harvesting) of fish in tanks or landlocked enclosures.
objetos.descripcion: Fish species raised on fish farms include, for example, salmon, catfish, tilapia, cod, carp, and trout.

objetos.definicion: A series of ascending pools constructed to enable fish to swim upstream over (or around) a dam.
An artificial obstruction placed in a watercourse to increase the depth or to divert it.
An artificial structure or gate that is utilized as a defense against flooding or storm surges.
objetos.descripcion: Consideration should be given to using the more specific Dam or Embankment features where appropriate in lieu of Flood Control Structure.

objetos.definicion: Land subject to controlled inundation (for example: flooded by the regulation of the level of water impounded by a dam or a beaver dam).
objetos.descripcion: It is often used to describe permanently flooded areas in which trees are still standing.

objetos.definicion: An inclined channel for conveying water from a distance.
objetos.descripcion: For example, carries water to be utilized for power, transportation, and/or irrigation.

objetos.definicion: A shallow place in a body of water used as a crossing.
A monumental and/or ornamental structure containing moving water, often including jets, falls, or other decorative features.
objetos.descripcion: The structure is often of a civic nature; the water is typically recirculated.

objetos.definicion: A device that monitors river flow and/or depth, and any associated support structures.
A structure over which brine trickles and is concentrated through increased evaporation.
Any type of surface water (for example: a river) which has no connection to the oceans except if it flows regularly into ocean waters.
objetos.descripcion: This concept can be used if the type of inland water (for example: a lake, pond, reservoir, or stream) is not currently known.

objetos.definicion: A body of water that is entirely surrounded by land.
objetos.descripcion: It may occur in a natural terrain depression in which water collects, or may be impounded by a dam, or formed by its bed being hollowed out of the soil, or formed by embanking and/or damming up a natural hollow (for example: by a beaver dam). Inland waterbodies have many uses such as: a source of water for irrigation, industrial processes, human consumption, and recreation. Impounded inland waterbodies may also be used for flood control.

objetos.definicion: The region along the edge of an inland water body that lies between the water and the first break in slope.
A place where water is taken into a channel or pipe from a waterbody.
objetos.descripcion: For example, to supply an aqueduct or a water treatment facility.

objetos.definicion: A tract that is exceptionally covered by water, excluding tidal waters.
objetos.descripcion: It may be caused by either uncontrolled inundation (for example: flooding due to a river overflowing its banks or low-lying regions accumulating standing water following severe rainfall) or controlled inundation (for example: flooded by the regulation of the level of a reservoir).

objetos.definicion: A land mass, other than a continent, surrounded by water.
A large body of water entirely surrounded by land.
An area of new land that has been reclaimed from an area previously covered by water.
objetos.descripcion: Commonly created by building embankments and draining water from an area.

objetos.definicion: A tract periodically covered by flood water, excluding tidal waters.
A trench surrounding a tract of land and serving as a barrier.
objetos.descripcion: It is usually filled with water.

objetos.definicion: A naturally formed pool of water.
objetos.descripcion: It is usually fed by surface drainage from the surrounding region and/or water arising from an underground source (for example: a spring or a resurgence).

objetos.definicion: A shaft sunk into the ground to reach and tap a supply of liquids and/or gases other than water intended for use in agriculture or domestic consumption.
objetos.descripcion: Typically drilled to tap underground reservoirs of hydrocarbons (for example: petroleum or natural gas). May also, for example, yield geothermally heated liquids for use in power generation or heating, or brine for use in the extraction of salt.

objetos.definicion: A pipeline that is used by hydroelectric plants to transport water by gravity from a reservoir to the turbine(s).
A small reservoir-like body of generally still water.
objetos.descripcion: Its bed is either hollowed out of the soil or formed by embanking and damming up a natural hollow (for example: by a beaver dam).

objetos.definicion: A location on a watercourse that has ramps, structural piles, and/or piers constructed on one or both shores to allow for suitable future crossing operations using floating bridges or rafting equipment.
objetos.descripcion: For example, a prepared float bridge site or a prepared raft site.

objetos.definicion: A facility to move solids, liquids or gases by means of pressure or suction.
Portions of a stream with accelerated current where it descends rapidly but without a break in the slope of the bed sufficient to form a waterfall.
objetos.descripcion: The surface is usually broken by boulders and rocks.

objetos.definicion: A substantial lake-like body of water impounded by a dam.
objetos.descripcion: May be used for flood control and/or as a source of water for irrigation, industrial processes, and/or human consumption.

objetos.definicion: The location at which a watercourse re-emerges from the terrain at the end of an underground part of its course.
A tract that is periodically covered with water and is used for growing rice.
A natural flowing watercourse.
Shallow pools, normally man-made, used for the natural evaporation of water for the collection of salt.
That part of an inland body of water where the depth is relatively slight (less than 1 metre) and thus likely to limit the passage of watercraft.
objetos.descripcion: Shallow water areas may be identified using overhead imagery, where there are visible bottom features, surface waves, and/or other water surface phenomena.

objetos.definicion: A device used to raise ships vertically between water bodies with different elevations.
objetos.descripcion: Normally ship elevators consist of water filled chambers which can be raised or lowered by means of mechanical devices. Commonly used to move ships between canals where locks would be impractical.

objetos.definicion: A pipe used for conveying liquid from one level to a lower level, using the liquid pressure differential to force a column of the liquid up to a higher level before it falls to the outlet.
An open, inclined conduit fitted with a gate for regulating water flow.
objetos.descripcion: May be employed in mine ore washing operations.

objetos.definicion: A gate used to regulate the flow or level of water in a watercourse (for example: stream, irrigation ditch, or sluice).
objetos.descripcion: Sluice gates are normally installed in a superstructure and/or frame and most commonly slide vertically to open but on occasion may instead slide horizontally. When opened they allow water to flow under or beside the gate. Commonly sluice gates will be installed perpendicular to the orientation of the flow of water within a watercourse and will be constructed as wide as the watercourse they regulate. Sluice gates may also be installed along the margins of watercourses for the purpose of controlling or permitting the flow of water to or from that watercourse into adjacent watercourses. Sluice gates may be used to regulate both tidal or non-tidal waters.

objetos.definicion: A passage for surplus water to run over or around a dam.
A flow of water rising or welling naturally from the earth.
A collector opening into a pipe or channel to allow the removal of excess runoff water or in some cases sewage.
objetos.descripcion: In civil engineering terms, a drop inlet.

objetos.definicion: An imaginary line connecting the points of lowest bed elevation in a watercourse.
objetos.descripcion: It usually marks the line of maximum flow in the watercourse.

objetos.definicion: A location where one or more devices have been temporarily or permanently stationed for the purpose of collecting information regarding vehicular and/or pedestrian traffic.
objetos.descripcion: Such information may include analysis of traffic flow, turning movements, speeds, congestion and delays, parking and loading, and pedestrian movement.

objetos.definicion: The location at which a watercourse disappears into the terrain.
objetos.aliases: River Vanishing Point, Stream Vanishing Point

objetos.definicion: A barrier that may be swung, drawn, or lowered to block an entrance or passageway on a watercourse.
A tower-like structure associated with a dam or water source and used for the intake of water.
The line where a land mass is in contact with a body of water and is defined in terms of a specific tidal state, sounding datum and/or water condition.
objetos.descripcion: For example, a high water or low water line.

objetos.definicion: A location at which water-related measurements are taken.
objetos.descripcion: Water measurements include, for example: water chemistry and/or quality; water depth, volume or velocity; and water presence variability or seasonality.

objetos.definicion: An artificial channel for a current of water, especially one built to provide water for industrial or agricultural purposes or for transporting water-borne materials.
objetos.descripcion: For example, a sluice, a flume, or a tailrace.

objetos.definicion: A tower supporting an elevated storage tank of water.
A tract for the treatment of water that consists of a bed of material where water is aerated or filtered.
A small natural terrain depression in which water collects, especially a pool where animals come to drink.

A shallow ridge or mound of unconsolidated mineral material that is located in a stream channel, at the mouth of a stream, in an estuary, at a lagoon, in the wave-break zone along a coast or at the sea bottom.
A vertically descending part of a watercourse where it falls from a height (for example: over a rock or a precipice).
objetos.descripcion: In place names, commonly shortened to 'fall' or 'falls', for example, 'Niagara Falls'.

objetos.definicion: An excavation drilled or dug into the ground (for example: the sea bed) for the extraction of liquids and/or gases.
A marsh, swamp, or other stretch of land that is usually saturated with water.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which describe the physical conditions of water, for example temperature or density.

objetos.definicion: A region of water having a colour distinctly different from that of the surrounding region.
A temporally and spatially variable boundary between two large masses of ocean water that have different physical properties.
A location at which water-related measurements are taken.
objetos.descripcion: Water measurements include, for example: water chemistry and/or quality; water depth, volume or velocity; and water presence variability or seasonality.

contenido: This Group consists of Concepts which describe the form of the earth’s surface and Concepts which describe special parts beneath the surface.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which describe the form (positions and heights) of the terrain surface.
subcategorias.descripcion: As opposed to Subgroup 05.02, you find in this Subgroup only auxiliaries for modelling the surface like contour lines. These Concepts mainly have no counterpart in the real world.

objetos.definicion: The specific location of the highest point of the aerodrome landing area.
objetos.descripcion: Typically this elevation is the highest point on any of the landing runway surfaces, and is considered the specific point at which the official aerodrome elevation is determined.

objetos.definicion: A reference mark on a permanent object indicating elevation relative to an established datum.
A line delineating a sudden and significant change in the gradient of the terrain.
A line connecting points having the same elevation value relative to a vertical datum.
An arbitrary area specified to represent elevation as polygons between contour lines.
A line along which large scale, linear tectonic manifestations have occurred.
The elevation value relative to a vertical datum, taken on an inland water surface at a designated location.
A line delineating the top of a ridge.
