A region where the terrain slope is within a set range of values.
A designated location with an elevation value relative to a vertical datum.
A set of three spot elevations defining a terrain region of constant slope and aspect.
objetos.descripcion: A set of nonoverlapping surface triangles may be used to represent the terrain surface, for example as a Triangulated Irregular Network (TIN).

objetos.definicion: A location where horizontal and/or vertical control has been determined by surveying methods.
objetos.descripcion: Surveys are used to establish positions (horizontal or vertical) of selected points. The points are then used to reference other survey observations or measurements.

objetos.definicion: An area of the surface of the Earth characterized by a common surface form or set of related surface forms.
objetos.descripcion: The physical shape, configuration, or general unevenness of a part of Earth's surface.

objetos.definicion: An imaginary line connecting the points of lowest bed elevation in a watercourse.
objetos.descripcion: It usually marks the line of maximum flow in the watercourse.

objetos.definicion: A line delineating the lowest part of a valley.
An area where heaped material (for example: waste or spoil) is deposited.
objetos.descripcion: Waste heaps may be located at disposal sites or in unsanctioned and unprepared locations where illegal dumping takes place. Illegal dumping sites are usually composed of materials produced in the immediately surrounding area; for example, in a residential neighborhood their content would principally be household trash. Illegal dumping sites have no associated structures or facilities.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which describe the earth’s surface and Concepts which relate to the shaping of land forms.
subcategorias.descripcion: As opposed to Subgroup 05.01, you find in this Subgroup Concepts which exist in the real world like hills, valleys, dips, etc.

objetos.definicion: An excavation drilled into the ground for purposes other than the extraction of potable water, oil, gas or brine.
objetos.descripcion: For example, drilled to support the underground testing of munitions, for coring or sampling of bedrock or ice for scientific purposes, or drilled for the injection of waste material.

objetos.definicion: A line delineating a sudden and significant change in the gradient of the terrain.
An interconnected series of naturally occurring subterranean chambers.
objetos.descripcion: Typically located in limestone, and often open to the Earth's surface either vertically or horizontally. Alterations may have been made to the cave chamber.

objetos.definicion: A modeling entity collecting information (for example: its method of formation, its access orientation, its cultural significance) about a cave.
The entrance to an interconnected series of naturally occurring subterranean chambers.
objetos.descripcion: Typically located in limestone, and often open to the Earth's surface either vertically or horizontally. Alterations may have been made to the cave mouth.

objetos.definicion: The bottom edge of a steep slope (for example: a cliff).
The top edge of a steep slope (for example: a cliff).
A narrow opening or fissure produced by a crack in the land, especially in rock.
objetos.descripcion: May also describe a deep vertical opening in the terrain that appears after an earthquake.

objetos.definicion: An excavation in the terrain to provide passage for a land or water transportation route (for example: a road, a railway, and/or a canal).
The face of an excavation within a cut.
The demarcation line between a cut and the surrounding land surface.
A sunken place in the terrain that is completely surrounded by higher terrain.
An arid and treeless uncultivated sparsely populated tract of land.
An area of the terrain that is subject to a persisting change of landscape towards that of desert that is typically caused by agriculture together with over-use of the ecosystem.
objetos.descripcion: Over the longer term, desertification may also be caused by natural reasons such as change of climate.

objetos.definicion: A tract neither permanently nor temporarily covered by water.
One or more ridges or hills of loose sediments.
objetos.descripcion: For example constisting of sand or loess.

objetos.definicion: A man-made embankment to contain or hold back water.
A man-made raised long mound of earth or other material.

An area of the land where removal processes have caused an areal degradation of soil particles (for example: erosion by the action of the wind) or to a linear degradation with deep erosion of different grades (for example: erosion by the action of moving water).
A long, narrow ridge of sand and gravel deposited by a glacial stream.
A sunken or cut passageway along a transportation route in mountainous regions constructed to protect vehicles from the elements.
objetos.descripcion: A series of openings on one side may be present for light or ventilation.

objetos.definicion: A fracture or zone of fractures in a rock formation, marked by the relative displacement on either side of the plane of the fracture.
objetos.descripcion: The intersection of a geologic fault with the ground surface is termed the 'fault trace' and is commonly plotted on maps to represent a fault. Since geologic faults do not usually consist of a single, clean fracture, the term 'fault zone' (or 'distributed fault') is often used when referring to the zone of complex deformation and numerous small fractures that is associated with the fault plane.

objetos.definicion: An area within which dislodgment and downslope transport of soil and/or bedrock under the influence of gravity has occurred.
objetos.descripcion: The movement may be either fast (for example: a landslide) or a slower creep.

objetos.definicion: A line along which the slope of a land surface model changes relatively abruptly.
objetos.descripcion: For example, a ridge line and a cliff. Land surface models use elevation data to approximate the shape of the terrain as a continuous mathematical surface.

objetos.definicion: A location where the slope of a land surface model changes sign when approached from any direction.
objetos.descripcion: For example, a peak and a pit. Land surface models approximate the shape of the terrain as a continuous surface based on limited data.

objetos.definicion: An area affected by vertical and/or horizontal movements of the Earth surface due to geological forces, ground instability and/or a changing stress-state, leading to volume changes within the soil.
objetos.descripcion: An example of ground movements due to geological forces are earthquakes, leading to mass desplacements and/or rupture of the Earth surface. Examples of ground instability include slope instability, geological voids (for example karst), and subsidence due to mining.

objetos.definicion: A deep ditch or channel cut into the terrain that results from erosion due to surface water runoff.
A small, isolated elevation, smaller than a mountain.
objetos.descripcion: The local relief is typically less than 300 metres.

objetos.definicion: A place of higher elevation within a wetland (for example: a swamp, a bog, or a marsh).
A permanent layer of ice covering a tract of land (especially a polar region) or the top of a mountain.
objetos.descripcion: Usually includes a surface layer of snow.

objetos.definicion: A tract that is exceptionally covered by water, excluding tidal waters.
objetos.descripcion: It may be caused by either uncontrolled inundation (for example: flooding due to a river overflowing its banks or low-lying regions accumulating standing water following severe rainfall) or controlled inundation (for example: flooded by the regulation of the level of a reservoir).

objetos.definicion: A geographically defined part of the land.
objetos.descripcion: It may have a proper name (for example: the Alps, the Rocky Mountains or the Great Plains).

objetos.definicion: A region of the land surface that is homogeneous with respect to form.
objetos.descripcion: For example: a butte or a valley.

objetos.definicion: The mass of earth or rock which has slipped down from a mountain or cliff.
A narrow route through a mountainous region or over a mountain range.
A cone or dome shaped mound or hill of peat or soil, usually with a core of ice.
objetos.descripcion: It is found in tundra regions and is produced by the pressure of water or ice accumulating underground and pushing upward.

objetos.definicion: A mass of land with a high potential of slipping down from an elevated location (for example: a cliff and/or the side of a mountain).
An open-air excavation created by removal of stone by blasting or cutting.
A line delineating the top of a ridge.
A significant outcropping of exposed bedrock.
One or more mounds or ridges of sand usually formed by the wind.
A clearing away of mud or other seabed deposits by the action of an object impacting and/or traversing along the seabed before settling.
A steep, vertical, or overhanging face of rock and/or soil.
objetos.descripcion: For example, an escarpment, a bluff, or a cliff.

objetos.definicion: A location where horizontal and/or vertical control has been determined by surveying methods.
objetos.descripcion: Surveys are used to establish positions (horizontal or vertical) of selected points. The points are then used to reference other survey observations or measurements.

objetos.definicion: An excavation where gravel, sand, and/or clay are removed for use elsewhere.
objetos.descripcion: For example, a gravel pit or a sandpit.

objetos.definicion: A region undermined through mining activities that has already partly subsided or that is in the process of subsiding.
A line delineating the lowest part of a valley.
A hill or mountain situated over an opening or openings in the Earth's crust through which lava, cinders, steam, and/or gases, are or have been expelled.
A region of a waterbody, either surface or subsurface, that is homogeneous with respect to form.
objetos.descripcion: For example: a bay, a cove, or a guyot.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which relate to rocks and rocks on and beneath the surface.

objetos.definicion: An interconnected series of naturally occurring subterranean chambers.
objetos.descripcion: Typically located in limestone, and often open to the Earth's surface either vertically or horizontally. Alterations may have been made to the cave chamber.

objetos.definicion: A modeling entity collecting information (for example: its method of formation, its access orientation, its cultural significance) about a cave.
The entrance to an interconnected series of naturally occurring subterranean chambers.
objetos.descripcion: Typically located in limestone, and often open to the Earth's surface either vertically or horizontally. Alterations may have been made to the cave mouth.

objetos.definicion: A narrow opening or fissure produced by a crack in the land, especially in rock.
objetos.descripcion: May also describe a deep vertical opening in the terrain that appears after an earthquake.

objetos.definicion: Land consisting principally of bedrock that is covered by less than 10 percent loose material (for example: soil, sand, clay, and/or gravel).
objetos.descripcion: The bedrock may include extrusive materials such as lava.

objetos.definicion: A rocky peak projecting above a surrounding ice field that may be perpetually covered with ice.
An accumulation of soil and stone debris deposited by a glacier.
A significant outcropping of exposed bedrock.
A conspicuous isolated large rock.
objetos.descripcion: May be on the land or consistently exposed above a waterbody. From offshore it would appear to a mariner as a single point on land and would be appropriate for use in navigation.

objetos.definicion: An area consisting of an aggregate of one or more minerals and/or solid organic material.
An underwater hill or mountain situated over an opening or openings in the Earth's crust through which lava, steam, and/or gases, are or have been expelled.
objetos.descripcion: Underwater volcanoes that have grown to the point of emerging above the water surface are usually collected as Feature: Volcano, or as Feature: Volcano within the perimeter of a Feature: Island.

objetos.definicion: A sheet of rock filling a fissure that sometimes shows as a terrain ridge.
objetos.descripcion: Especially a mass of igneous rock that has intruded upwards through strata.

objetos.definicion: A hill or mountain situated over an opening or openings in the Earth's crust through which lava, cinders, steam, and/or gases, are or have been expelled.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which relate to the soil, which means to the upper layer of the surface.

objetos.definicion: A sterile plain containing an excess of alkali usually occurring in the bottom of an underdrained basin in an arid or semi-arid region.
objetos.descripcion: The ground may be soft and have low shearing and bearing strength, and a high organic content.

objetos.definicion: A fan-shaped alluvial deposit formed especially where a stream begins to descend a gentler slope.
A natural accumulation of liquid asphalt.
A tract so unproductive, infertile, and/or physically disturbed by human activity, as to have no significant vegetation.
objetos.descripcion: Distinguished from Feature: 'Unvegetated Land' which is typically used to characterize the vegetation cover when the underlying soil has not been disturbed.

objetos.definicion: An area with a sufficently stable surface, that allows for storage of heavy equipment, vehicles etc.
A zone adjacent to a continent (or around an island) and extending from the low water line to a depth at which there is usually a marked increase of slope towards oceanic depths.
A boundary or limit beyond which plant cultivation is not possible.
objetos.descripcion: The limiting factors include, for example, climate, topography, and soil conditions.

objetos.definicion: Land so physically disturbed as to have no identifiable type of soil.
objetos.descripcion: For example, built-up areas, strip mines, landfills, and/or railway yards.

objetos.definicion: An area of land within which all surface waters drain to a single outlet point located on an inland waterbody or watercourse.
A boundary defined by all or part of the outer limit of a drainage basin, which distinguishes the headstreams that are tributaries to different river systems or basins.
One or more ridges or hills of loose sediments.
objetos.descripcion: For example constisting of sand or loess.

objetos.definicion: A long, narrow ridge of sand and gravel deposited by a glacial stream.
An area of the surface of the Earth that shares a common characterization of its substratum (bodies of soil, rock and unconsolidated rocks) and its groundwater related properties.
The mass of earth or rock which has slipped down from a mountain or cliff.
A morphology forming different shapes that stretch above the surrounding land in a limited area and usually in the form of a peak.
objetos.descripcion: An elevation standing high above the surrounding area with small summit area, steep slopes and local relief of 300 metres or more.

objetos.definicion: A cone or dome shaped mound or hill of peat or soil, usually with a core of ice.
objetos.descripcion: It is found in tundra regions and is produced by the pressure of water or ice accumulating underground and pushing upward.

objetos.definicion: One or more mounds or ridges of sand usually formed by the wind.
An area whose soil characteristics are deteriorated by natural, semi-natural or human influences.
An area within which the upper soil horizons have become enriched in salts to a sufficient degree to result in loss in agricultural productivity.
objetos.descripcion: The enrichment may be due to either natural processes and/or human activity.

objetos.definicion: A region of the land that is homogeneous with respect to a soil characteristic.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which relate to raw materials and their deposits.
subcategorias.descripcion: Groundwater is also a raw material in this context.

objetos.definicion: A sterile plain containing an excess of alkali usually occurring in the bottom of an underdrained basin in an arid or semi-arid region.
objetos.descripcion: The ground may be soft and have low shearing and bearing strength, and a high organic content.

objetos.definicion: An underground layer of water-bearing permeable rock or unconsolidated materials (for example: gravel, sand, silt, or clay).
objetos.descripcion: It may yield economically significant quantities of groundwater to wells and springs.

objetos.definicion: A natural accumulation of liquid asphalt.
An area of land within which all surface waters drain to a single outlet point located on an inland waterbody or watercourse.
A boundary defined by all or part of the outer limit of a drainage basin, which distinguishes the headstreams that are tributaries to different river systems or basins.
A tract of public land reserved for future use and/or restricted as to present use.
objetos.descripcion: For example, reserved for hunting or limited gathering of uncultivated forest products.

objetos.definicion: An excavation made in the terrain for the purpose of extracting and/or exploiting natural resources.
A track along which a series of geophysical data observations are distributed.
A grid established for the collection of geophysical data within an area.
objetos.descripcion: The grid is typically composed of one or more series of observation points where each series is obtained along a single track and the grid is then assembled from multiple tracks.

objetos.definicion: A terrain surface feature controlled by or derived from the heat of the Earth's interior.
objetos.descripcion: For example, a hot spring.

objetos.definicion: Any underground water (for example: held in the soil and/or in rock pores and/or crevices) especially that which is below the water-table.
An area where the presence of recoverable petroleum, oil, and/or natural gas has been identified.
objetos.descripcion: The field can exist regardless of current exploitation activities.

objetos.definicion: An area of similar hydrogeologic properties and conditions of groundwater.
objetos.descripcion: Such similarities result from common geologic origin and history, leading to common hydrogeologic parameters such as ground-water flow direction and rate, recharge, and discharge.

objetos.definicion: A structure over a vertical mine shaft containing machinery (for example: a winding head or hoist) used to transport minerals, equipment, and/or workers between the surface and various levels within the mine.
objetos.descripcion: It is usually the most prominent structure at a shaft mining facility.
objetos.aliases: Mine Shaft Headframe, Mine Shaft Headgear, Pit-head Frame

objetos.definicion: An area, place, site or deposit, of which little may be known, except that specific minerals or rocks, that are considered to be valuable or that are of scientific or technical interest, have been identified and recorded.
objetos.descripcion: The minerals may be solid, liquid or gaseous.

objetos.definicion: A man-made heap of mining or quarrying products that does not contain waste materials.
objetos.descripcion: For example, a pile of coal or quarried stones.

objetos.definicion: A shaft sunk into the ground to reach and tap a supply of liquids and/or gases other than water intended for use in agriculture or domestic consumption.
objetos.descripcion: Typically drilled to tap underground reservoirs of hydrocarbons (for example: petroleum or natural gas). May also, for example, yield geothermally heated liquids for use in power generation or heating, or brine for use in the extraction of salt.

objetos.definicion: A protected (restricted use) terrain region incorporating facilities for the collection of water, so designated in order to protect the water on and beneath the terrain from being contaminated.
An open-air excavation created by removal of stone by blasting or cutting.
A natural depression in arid or semi-arid regions whose bed is covered with salt encrusted clayey soil.
objetos.descripcion: Found especially in North Africa and Arabia.

objetos.definicion: Shallow pools, normally man-made, used for the natural evaporation of water for the collection of salt.
A flat area of natural surface salt deposits.
objetos.descripcion: May also be used to describe smaller areas; these are commonly termed salt pans.

objetos.definicion: A flow of water rising or welling naturally from the earth.
An underground geological formation that is used to store materials, especially liquids and/or gases.
objetos.descripcion: The formation may be either natural (for example: a depleted oil reservoir), man-made for other purposes (for example: an abandoned mine), or intentionally engineered for the purpose of storage (for example: a hard rock cavern). Packaged (for example: in drums or on pallets) or bulk (for example: coal or grain) materials may also be stored.

objetos.definicion: An excavation drilled or dug into the ground (for example: the sea bed) for the extraction of liquids and/or gases.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which relate to volcanoes, earthquakes and/or other seismic occurrences on and beneath the surface.

objetos.definicion: An area that is affected by a natural disaster (for example: an earthquake, a volcano eruption or flooding).
objetos.descripcion: The effect maybe a long-term event (for example: an aggradation or a desertification).

objetos.definicion: An area that is estimated as potentially threatened by natural disasters because of former events or specific circumstances (for example: geological parameters).
A bowl-shaped depression in the terrain, usually round and with steep sides.
objetos.descripcion: Craters commonly are created by the removal of material by explosions, either natural (for example: the eruption of a volcano) or artificial (for example: a bomb), originating at or below the Earth's surface, or by the impact of an object with the Earth (for example: a meteorite).

objetos.definicion: A narrow opening or fissure produced by a crack in the land, especially in rock.
objetos.descripcion: May also describe a deep vertical opening in the terrain that appears after an earthquake.

objetos.definicion: The site at which has occurred a serious disruption of the functioning of a community or a society causing widespread human, material, economic or environmental losses which exceed the ability of the affected community or society to cope using its own resources.
An area of the surface of the Earth that has been damaged by an earthquake.
objetos.descripcion: The damage is due to mechanical shock and may to either of the terrain, attached structures and/or to cultural possessions.

objetos.definicion: The point on the surface of the Earth that is directly above the focus of an earthquake.
A fracture or zone of fractures in a rock formation, marked by the relative displacement on either side of the plane of the fracture.
objetos.descripcion: The intersection of a geologic fault with the ground surface is termed the 'fault trace' and is commonly plotted on maps to represent a fault. Since geologic faults do not usually consist of a single, clean fracture, the term 'fault zone' (or 'distributed fault') is often used when referring to the zone of complex deformation and numerous small fractures that is associated with the fault plane.

objetos.definicion: A line along which large scale, linear tectonic manifestations have occurred.
A terrain surface feature controlled by or derived from the heat of the Earth's interior.
objetos.descripcion: For example, a hot spring.

objetos.definicion: A torsionally rigid thin segment of the Earth's lithosphere, which may be assumed to move horizontally and adjoins other plates along zones of seismic activity.
objetos.descripcion: The lithosphere consists of the crust and the upper part of the mantle of the Earth.

objetos.definicion: An area where earthquakes or other seismic events routinely occur.
An underwater hill or mountain situated over an opening or openings in the Earth's crust through which lava, steam, and/or gases, are or have been expelled.
objetos.descripcion: Underwater volcanoes that have grown to the point of emerging above the water surface are usually collected as Feature: Volcano, or as Feature: Volcano within the perimeter of a Feature: Island.

objetos.definicion: An area of the Earth's surface that is affected by volcanic structures and/or activity.
objetos.descripcion: Disturbances of the Earth surface due to volcanic activity include, for example, the discharge of heated gases, ash, rocks, or lava and the creation of different volcanic structures such as lava-flows, cinder cones, or lava domes.

objetos.definicion: A sheet of rock filling a fissure that sometimes shows as a terrain ridge.
objetos.descripcion: Especially a mass of igneous rock that has intruded upwards through strata.

objetos.definicion: A hill or mountain situated over an opening or openings in the Earth's crust through which lava, cinders, steam, and/or gases, are or have been expelled.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which relate to glaciers and glacial phenomena.

objetos.definicion: A deep crack or fissure in a glacier that results from differential movement of ice.
A large mass or river of ice formed by accumulation and compaction of snow on higher ground that is moving slowly down a slope or valley from above the snowline.
The vertical face of a glacier or ice shelf.
A rocky peak projecting above a surrounding ice field that may be perpetually covered with ice.
A route over a frozen watercourse.
objetos.descripcion: Usually marked and intended to support substantial vehicle traffic. Often designed as an alternate to a seasonally-closed ferry crossing (see Feature: 'Ferry Crossing').

objetos.definicion: A large land area permanently covered by snow and/or ice.
objetos.descripcion: A Land Snow Field and/or Ice-field is in-situ and does not flow, therefore it should be distinguished from Feature: 'Glacier'.

objetos.definicion: An accumulation of soil and stone debris deposited by a glacier.
A tract permanently covered by snow and/or ice.
objetos.descripcion: For example, glaciers and snowfields.

objetos.definicion: A cone or dome shaped mound or hill of peat or soil, usually with a core of ice.
objetos.descripcion: It is found in tundra regions and is produced by the pressure of water or ice accumulating underground and pushing upward.

objetos.definicion: A large area permanently covered by snow and/or ice.
objetos.descripcion: May cover land and/or water.

objetos.definicion: A vast, nearly level, treeless arctic region usually with a marshy surface and underlying permafrost.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which describe anomalies in the gravity or magnetic field of earth or the fields themselves.

objetos.definicion: An area where one or more geophysical parameters differ from the surroundings due to inhomogeneities in the underground composition.
An isopleth that connects locations of equal magnetic variation.
A localized anomaly in the Earth's magnetic field.
Either of the two locations on the Earth's surface where the magnetic dip is 90 degrees (locally vertical).

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which describe the coverage of earth’s surface in a global perspective.

objetos.definicion: A tract neither permanently nor temporarily covered by water.
An area of the surface of the Earth that shares a common characterization of its tectono-, litho-, bio-, and/or chronostratigraphic properties.
Characterization of the predominant vegetation and land use characteristics of the land.
The limit of a region that is defined by inorganic (for example: climate, relief, water balance or atmosphere) or organic (for example: flora or fauna) factors.
objetos.descripcion: For example: a timberline or a cultivation limit.

objetos.definicion: A region that is defined by inorganic (for example: climate, relief, water balance or atmosphere) or organic (for example: flora or fauna) factors.
A region of surface water, whether flowing or free standing.
objetos.descripcion: For example, lakes, rivers, oceans, and/or reservoirs. Often used as a general characterization for non-terrain regions.

objetos.definicion: The connected water areas of the Earth that surround the continents and are not completly surrounded by the landmass of a single continent.
objetos.descripcion: The areas differ in morphology and/or other natural characteristics and may be covered by ice.

objetos.definicion: An area consisting of an aggregate of one or more minerals and/or solid organic material.
A global zone based on a predominant plant community.
objetos.descripcion: Vegetation zones extend across areas of similar latitude and often reflect climatic zones.

objetos.definicion: A data collection region lacking suitable source coverage and/or where data is not required.

contenido: This Group consists of Concepts which relate to organic features.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which describe the land use for agriculture.
subcategorias.descripcion: While the Subgroup 01.03 describes buildings, devices etc, this Subgroup concentrates on the cultivation of plants.

objetos.definicion: A global land-use zone based on a predominant form and type of plant cultivation.
objetos.descripcion: Agricultural zones extend across areas of similar latitude and often reflect climatic zones.

objetos.definicion: A culturally designated tract where plants are displayed.
A tract covered mainly by large treelike grasses.
objetos.descripcion: For example, bamboo and sugarcane.

objetos.definicion: An area that has been tilled for the planting of crops.
A boundary or limit beyond which plant cultivation is not possible.
objetos.descripcion: The limiting factors include, for example, climate, topography, and soil conditions.

objetos.definicion: A piece of ground (often enclosed) where fruits, flowers, herbs, or vegetables are cultivated.
objetos.descripcion: Often adjoining a house or other residential building.

objetos.definicion: A tract covered by the systematic planting of hop vines.
An area used for the cultivation of vegetables, fruits and/or flowers as well as for the raising of cultivated plants.
A tract covered by systematic plantings of trees that yield fruits (including nuts).
A tract where plants (for example: shrubs, flowers, and/or trees) are grown for transplanting, seed, and/or grafting.
A tract that is periodically covered with water and is used for growing rice.
A tract covered by the systematic planting of grape vines.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which relate to areas that are uncultivated and that are usually covered with low growing grass-like vegetation.

objetos.definicion: A tract covered mainly by short, uncultured, woody plants that have been stunted by an environmental limitation (for example: low rainfall or nutrient-poor soil).
objetos.descripcion: Typically, coverage can range from sparse to differentiated (where the vegetation is close but not tangled together). The woody plants include bushes, scrub, shrubs and/or low stunted trees. The predominant height of the vegetation is usually less than 3 metres.

objetos.definicion: A man-made cleared strip through a vegetated region.
objetos.descripcion: May be designed to: provide access for a road, railroad, pipeline, power transmission line, or electrical signal line; demarcate a boundary; obtain survey line-of-sight; or to impede the progress of forest fires (a firebreak).

objetos.definicion: A tract covered mainly by grasses that have little or no woody tissue.
objetos.descripcion: For example, pasture, meadow, and steppe.

objetos.definicion: An area of open uncultivated ground covered by heather and/or related plants, especially on acid sandy or peaty soil.
A continuous growth of shrubs planted as a fence, a boundary, and/or a windbreak.
A tract covered by a mixture of herbaceous and low-growing, uncultivated plants that may have some woody tissue.
objetos.descripcion: For example, covered by tall grasses, shrubs, and/or bushes. The predominant height is usually less than 2-3 metres.

objetos.definicion: An open grassy plain with few or no trees in a tropical or subtropical region.
A tract covered sparsely by low trees, bushes, and/or shrubs that have been stunted by an environmental limitation (for example: low rainfall or nutrient-poor soil).
A vast level grassy usually treeless plain.
objetos.descripcion: Generally found in southeastern Europe and Siberia.

objetos.definicion: A tract covered mainly by low-growing, uncultured, woody plants that are thickly tangled together.
objetos.descripcion: For example, covered by brushwood and/or stunted trees. The predominant height may be up to 6-8 metres.

objetos.definicion: A vast, nearly level, treeless arctic region usually with a marshy surface and underlying permafrost.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which relate to a tree or wood covered area.

objetos.definicion: A man-made cleared strip through a vegetated region.
objetos.descripcion: May be designed to: provide access for a road, railroad, pipeline, power transmission line, or electrical signal line; demarcate a boundary; obtain survey line-of-sight; or to impede the progress of forest fires (a firebreak).

objetos.definicion: A tract of land primarily covered by trees and undergrowth.
objetos.descripcion: The area is sometimes mixed with pasture.

objetos.definicion: A site in a forest or wood(s) that has been cleared, often for slash and burn agriculture and/or as a result of clear-cutting logging.
objetos.descripcion: May also occur from natural causes such as a forest fire.

objetos.definicion: A small wood or similar collection of trees growing closely together.
objetos.descripcion: May occur naturally or be deliberately planted for shade, ornamentation, and/or as an orchard (for example: of olives or citrus fruit).

objetos.definicion: A tract of vegetation that is being exploited for lumber resources.
A dense forest in an area of high rainfall with little seasonal variation, and whose canopy is usually closed (allowing only filtered sunlight to reach the ground).
objetos.descripcion: Especially when located in the tropics, characterized by a rich variety of plant and animal life.

objetos.definicion: A swampy coniferous forest of high northern latitudes, especially that between the tundra and steppes of Siberia.
An open tract for the storage of wooden lumber and timbers.
An individual woody perennial plant, typically having a single stem or trunk growing to a considerable height and bearing lateral branches at some distance from the ground.
objetos.descripcion: May be distinguished by its relative isolation from other features, thus serving as a landmark.

objetos.definicion: The point in altitude and/or latitude beyond which trees can no longer grow.
objetos.descripcion: The limiting factors are a combination of altitude, climate and/or soils.

objetos.definicion: A line or row of trees.
objetos.descripcion: Could be used for protection from natural influences or for ornamental purposes. Often found lining one or both sides of a road (for example: an avenue) or a water body.

objetos.definicion: A geographic area delineated by the outer edge or boundary of a wildland fire at a moment in time.
objetos.descripcion: As a wildland fire progresses its perimeter will change shape and extent, not necessarily moving outward from some central location nor necessarily increasing in total acreage within the fire perimeter. While the fire front is assumed to be the leading edge of the fire perimeter, unburned interior areas may remain; such areas may burn (or not) at a later stage of the wildland fire.

objetos.definicion: A tract of trees whose canopy is not closed (allows sunlight to reach the ground) and often includes undergrowth.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which relate to areas that are permanently or temporarily moist or covered by water.

objetos.definicion: A region of marine plants that grow in long narrow ribbons.
objetos.descripcion: Algae may be moored or floating. For example, sea grass, kelp, or sargasso.

objetos.definicion: A permanently wet area of land consisting of incompletely decayed organic material and mainly stagnant fresh water.
objetos.descripcion: It is generally too soft to bear the weight of any heavy body. A subtype of the more generalized Feature: 'Wetland'.

objetos.definicion: Land subject to controlled inundation (for example: flooded by the regulation of the level of water impounded by a dam or a beaver dam).
objetos.descripcion: It is often used to describe permanently flooded areas in which trees are still standing.

objetos.definicion: A place of higher elevation within a wetland (for example: a swamp, a bog, or a marsh).
A tract that is exceptionally covered by water, excluding tidal waters.
objetos.descripcion: It may be caused by either uncontrolled inundation (for example: flooding due to a river overflowing its banks or low-lying regions accumulating standing water following severe rainfall) or controlled inundation (for example: flooded by the regulation of the level of a reservoir).

objetos.definicion: A tract periodically covered by flood water, excluding tidal waters.
A dense thicket of mangrove that is subject to tidal inundation and forming a muddy swamp.
A soft, poorly drained wetland that is characterized by the growth of only non-woody plants (for example: grasses) and often forms a transition region between a waterbody and land.
objetos.descripcion: It is subject to frequent or tidal inundations, but not considered to be continually under water. It lacks trees. A subtype of the more generalized Feature: 'Wetland'.

objetos.definicion: A tract that is periodically covered with water and is used for growing rice.
A seasonally flooded, poorly drained wetland with more woody plants than a marsh and better drainage than a bog.
objetos.descripcion: It is covered with water all or most of the year, and accumulating dead vegetation does not rapidly decay. It can exist on flat-lying areas created by certain geomorphic environments. The vegetation mainly consists of hydrophytic trees and/or scrubs whose roots are adapted to wet conditions, with an open to very dense canopy closure. A subtype of the more generalized Feature: 'Wetland'.

objetos.definicion: A marsh, swamp, or other stretch of land that is usually saturated with water.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which describe very dry regions.

objetos.definicion: An arid and treeless uncultivated sparsely populated tract of land.
An area of the terrain that is subject to a persisting change of landscape towards that of desert that is typically caused by agriculture together with over-use of the ecosystem.
objetos.descripcion: Over the longer term, desertification may also be caused by natural reasons such as change of climate.

objetos.definicion: An area of the terrain where the rate of evaporation is exceeds the rate of precipitation.
One or more ridges or hills of loose sediments.
objetos.descripcion: For example constisting of sand or loess.

objetos.definicion: A fertile tract of land that occurs in a desert wherever a permanent supply of fresh water is available.
objetos.descripcion: Oasis vary in size from a pond with a group of date palms around small springs to the oasis cities of the deserts with extended agricultural cultivation.

objetos.definicion: One or more mounds or ridges of sand usually formed by the wind.
A tract covered by little (less than 5 percent) or no vegetation.
objetos.descripcion: Distinguished from Feature: 'Barren Ground' which is typically used to directly characterize the underlying soil (and the resulting impact on vegetation cover).

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which relate to areas that are designated as special and/or restricted regions based on their natural characteristics.

objetos.definicion: A natural area set aside for the preservation and protection of wildlife.
An area of the surface of the Earth that shares a common characterization of its level of atmospheric humidity.
An area of the surface of the Earth that shares a common characterization of its atmospheric pressure.

An area of land and/or sea especially dedicated to the protection and maintenance of biological diversity, and of natural and associated cultural resources, and managed through legal or other effective means.
objetos.descripcion: As determined, for example, by the International Union for Conservation of Nature and Natural Resources (IUCN).

objetos.definicion: A region whose prevailing natural conditions have been degraded through contamination by harmful or objectionable substances.
objetos.descripcion: The contamination may be either naturally occurring or the result of human activity. For example, polluted by sewage or toxic chemicals, obscured by smoke or ash from volcanic eruptions, or contaminated by exposure to Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and/or Nuclear (CBRN) agents.

objetos.definicion: An area within which refuse has been dumped on land or sunk (legally or illegally) in the sea and has resulted in environmental endangerment.
An area subject to extreme incidents that stress and may irreversibly injure the environment.
A tract of public land reserved for future use and/or restricted as to present use.
objetos.descripcion: For example, reserved for hunting or limited gathering of uncultivated forest products.

objetos.definicion: An area of the surface of the Earth that shares a common characterization of its wind circulation as having more or less regular (periodic, partly episodic) occurring strong winds with speeds more than 75 kilometres per hour (9 Beaufort or greater).
objetos.descripcion: May also be used to characterize areas of persistently low wind speed (for example: the 'horse latitudes').

objetos.definicion: An area of the surface of the Earth that shares a common characterization of its annual period of fog.
objetos.descripcion: The period may consist of discontinuous eposides.

objetos.definicion: A tract of land primarily covered by trees and undergrowth.
objetos.descripcion: The area is sometimes mixed with pasture.

objetos.definicion: An area of the surface of the Earth that shares a common characterization of its annual period of frost and/or snow.
objetos.descripcion: The period may consist of discontinuous eposides.

objetos.definicion: A major area of the surface of the Earth that shares a common characterization of its permanent wind circulation.
An area of the surface of the Earth where animals and/or plants may endanger or kill human life directly (by attack) or indirectly (by poison).
An area within which an infectious disease is endemic.
The limit of a region that is defined by inorganic (for example: climate, relief, water balance or atmosphere) or organic (for example: flora or fauna) factors.
objetos.descripcion: For example: a timberline or a cultivation limit.

objetos.definicion: A region that is defined by inorganic (for example: climate, relief, water balance or atmosphere) or organic (for example: flora or fauna) factors.
One of the three large regions of the world-wide ocean, each with associated sub- and marginal areas and subject to an independent flow-regime.
objetos.descripcion: They result from the relative locations of the continents.

objetos.definicion: An area of the surface of the Earth that shares a common characterization of its level of precipitation.
A protected (restricted use) terrain region incorporating facilities for the collection of water, so designated in order to protect the water on and beneath the terrain from being contaminated.
A regional area of the surface of the Earth that shares a common characterization of its wind circulation.
objetos.descripcion: The winds may be episodic rather than steady.

objetos.definicion: An area of the surface of the Earth that shares a common characterization of its solar irradiance.
objetos.descripcion: Solar irradiance primarily falls in the spectral range of approximately 0.3-3 metres in wavelength, where the shortest wavelengths are in the ultraviolet region of the spectrum, the intermediate wavelengths in the visible region, and the longer wavelengths are in the near infrared. Total solar irradiance means that the solar flux has been integrated over all wavelengths to include the contributions from ultraviolet, visible, and infrared radiation.

objetos.definicion: Any of the 24 longitudinal regions of the Earth, each occupying 15 arc degrees and having a mean solar time one hour greater than that of the neighboring region to its west.
A global zone based on a predominant plant community.
objetos.descripcion: Vegetation zones extend across areas of similar latitude and often reflect climatic zones.

objetos.definicion: A geographic area delineated by the outer edge or boundary of a wildland fire at a moment in time.
objetos.descripcion: As a wildland fire progresses its perimeter will change shape and extent, not necessarily moving outward from some central location nor necessarily increasing in total acreage within the fire perimeter. While the fire front is assumed to be the leading edge of the fire perimeter, unburned interior areas may remain; such areas may burn (or not) at a later stage of the wildland fire.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which relate to animal organisms.

objetos.definicion: A natural area set aside for the preservation and protection of wildlife.

A facility involved in the culturing or farming (including harvesting) of aquatic organisms (for example: fish, mollusks, crustaceans, plants, crocodiles, alligators or amphibians) using techniques designed to increase the production of the organisms in question beyond the natural capacity of the environment (for example: regular stocking, feeding and protection from predators).
objetos.descripcion: Culturing or farming refers to the rearing of individuals up to their juvenile and/or adult phase under captive conditions. In addition, it also encompasses individual, corporate or state ownership of the individual organisms throughout the rearing or culture stage, up to and including harvesting.

objetos.definicion: A man-made open container holding water for animals to drink.
A facility involved in the breeding (hatching and associated activities) and cultivation (raising for release or harvesting) of fish in tanks or landlocked enclosures.
objetos.descripcion: Fish species raised on fish farms include, for example, salmon, catfish, tilapia, cod, carp, and trout.

objetos.definicion: An area on a water body bottom established to simulate a natural reef and intended to enhance fishery resources and commercial and/or recreational fishing opportunities.
objetos.descripcion: The haven (reef) is constructed by dumping (or emplacing) assorted scrap materials (or artificial structures) in areas which may be of very small extent or may stretch a considerable distance along a depth contour.

objetos.definicion: A series of ascending pools constructed to enable fish to swim upstream over (or around) a dam.
An area containing structures (usually portable) for catching fish.
A fence of stakes or wall of stones set in a river or along the shore to direct fish towards fish traps or nets.
objetos.descripcion: The weir is shaped so as to encourage fish to naturally congregate, usually based on river or tidal flow. Although generally consisting of linear segments on rivers, in shore areas one or more components may be curved so as to form an enclosure with a narrow entrance. When constructed of stones the thickness of the wall constitutes a permanent hazard to maritime navigation.

objetos.definicion: Poles or stakes placed in shallow water to outline fishing grounds or to catch fish.

A site where marine organisms are cultivated for food and other products in either the open ocean, in an enclosed section of the ocean, or in tanks, ponds or raceways that are filled with seawater (for example: the farming of marine fish, prawns, or oysters in saltwater ponds).
The limit of a region that is defined by inorganic (for example: climate, relief, water balance or atmosphere) or organic (for example: flora or fauna) factors.
objetos.descripcion: For example: a timberline or a cultivation limit.

objetos.definicion: A region that is defined by inorganic (for example: climate, relief, water balance or atmosphere) or organic (for example: flora or fauna) factors.
A mass of rock or coral which either reaches close to the sea surface or is exposed at low tide, posing a hazard to navigation.
An area where nets used for catching tunny (tuna) have been deployed.
A site where wild animals are kept for exhibition to the public, that may also support breeding and/or study.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which relate to members of the Plant Kingdom.

objetos.definicion: A region of waterborne cellular or vascular plants (for example: algae, grasses, reeds, and water hyacinths).
objetos.descripcion: The vegetation may moored (for example: sea grass and reeds) or floating (for example: sargasso and water hyacinths).

objetos.definicion: A region along the edge of a body of water or watercourse generally dominated by riparian vegetation.
objetos.descripcion: May extend up to approximately 100 metres from the water edge, often including land subject to inundation and, if vegetation is present, commonly dominated by woody vegetation.

objetos.definicion: The limit of a region that is defined by inorganic (for example: climate, relief, water balance or atmosphere) or organic (for example: flora or fauna) factors.
objetos.descripcion: For example: a timberline or a cultivation limit.

objetos.definicion: A region that is defined by inorganic (for example: climate, relief, water balance or atmosphere) or organic (for example: flora or fauna) factors.
A line or row of trees.
objetos.descripcion: Could be used for protection from natural influences or for ornamental purposes. Often found lining one or both sides of a road (for example: an avenue) or a water body.

contenido: This Group consists of Concepts describing border and areas with special restrictions or permissions and of Concepts which relate to surveying and cadastre.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which relate to the official, legal or recognised boundary and/or designation of parts of earth’s surface.

objetos.definicion: A terrain region between a contact zone and the first passable land transportation route (for example: a road).
A boundary between administratively controlled regions.
An administratively subordinate division of a geopolitical entity.
objetos.descripcion: A geopolitical entity (country) is typically divided into first-, second-, and lower-order administrative divisions. First-order administrative divisions are immediately subordinate to the government of the geopolitical entity, with second- and lower-order divisions subordinate to those above them. Examples: (first-order) a United States state, a German Land, a French region; a Canadian province; (second-order) a U.S. county, a French department; (third-order) a U.S. township, a French arrondissement; (lower-levels) a French commune.

objetos.definicion: A region controlled by an administrative authority.
A line established by opposing political groups as a result of cessation of hostilities.
A location that serves as a point on, and which partially defines a segment of, a national boundary baseline.
objetos.descripcion: May be monumented or unmonumented. A national boundary baseline is used for defining the landward edge or margin of a nation's various contiguous zones such as the 3 and 12 nautical mile limits and the Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ).

objetos.definicion: An established and formally recognized location where a government checkpoint has been established between neighboring States where the movement of people and/or goods are regulated and restrictions enforced, shipments or vehicles are cleared for entry or departure, and/or customs duties are collected.
A line separating two geographic areas from each other.
A line along which active hostilities are suspended.
A limit of an area which is unilaterally claimed by one political group without consent or negotiation with another.
A terrain strip 3 metres wide limited on the water side by the contact between land and water (under average water level conditions).
A terrain strip extending from 2 metres below to 6 metres inland of the Mean Water Line.
A region whose prevailing natural conditions have been degraded through contamination by harmful or objectionable substances.
objetos.descripcion: The contamination may be either naturally occurring or the result of human activity. For example, polluted by sewage or toxic chemicals, obscured by smoke or ash from volcanic eruptions, or contaminated by exposure to Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and/or Nuclear (CBRN) agents.

objetos.definicion: A line established to regulate matters between nations or groups over a specific area or territory.
An existing line of separation not officially recognized by various governments.
A region where military activity is prohibited.

A region controlled by a political community having an organized government and possessing internal and external sovereignty, most often as a State but sometimes having a dependent relationship on another political authority or a special sovereignty status.
objetos.descripcion: The degree of sovereignty may be limited in specific areas (for example: matters of economic, administrative, legislative, judicial, military and/or foreign policy). The region controlled by a sovereign geopolitical entity is commonly referred to as a 'country'.

objetos.definicion: A geospatially described boundary representing the limits of authority for administration, control, military and/or other kinds of activities, as asserted by one or more political organizations (whether unilaterally or in agreement), including recognized governments, provisional authorities, and international bodies.
objetos.descripcion: A geopolitical line is typically indicated at ground level, but in effect represents a two-dimensional plane roughly perpendicular to the Earth's surface along that line, passing through the air above and the ground below.

objetos.definicion: A continuous growth of shrubs planted as a fence, a boundary, and/or a windbreak.
The line of demarcation specifying the operational limits of a functional area controlled by a recognized authority.
objetos.descripcion: The geographic limits of the Installation Boundary may include both land and water currently owned or used by the recognized controlling installation or facility. Typically, the Installation Boundary will enclose a grouping of facilities, located in the same general vicinity, which support functions particular to the needs and requirements of the installation property. The controlling installation or facility may have been constructed to support military operations.

objetos.definicion: A line designated as the place on the Earth where each calendar day begins.
objetos.descripcion: This line generally coincides with the 180th meridian but is modified to avoid land.

objetos.definicion: The line where a land mass is in contact with a body of water and the tide state or river stage are unspecified.
objetos.descripcion: It may be in either the littoral or inland waters. In the littoral, consideration should be given to using the more specific high water or low water lines based on the nature of the source data collection.

objetos.definicion: A line where on either side certain activities or factors of significance to navigation and/or operation apply.
The limit of a region that is defined by inorganic (for example: climate, relief, water balance or atmosphere) or organic (for example: flora or fauna) factors.
objetos.descripcion: For example: a timberline or a cultivation limit.

objetos.definicion: A region that is defined by inorganic (for example: climate, relief, water balance or atmosphere) or organic (for example: flora or fauna) factors.
A region temporarily held and controlled by a foreign military force.
An underground geological formation that is used to store materials, especially liquids and/or gases.
objetos.descripcion: The formation may be either natural (for example: a depleted oil reservoir), man-made for other purposes (for example: an abandoned mine), or intentionally engineered for the purpose of storage (for example: a hard rock cavern). Packaged (for example: in drums or on pallets) or bulk (for example: coal or grain) materials may also be stored.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which are used to designate official or legal properties abd/or which are used for surveying purposes.

objetos.definicion: A location that serves as a point on, and which partially defines a segment of, a national boundary baseline.
objetos.descripcion: May be monumented or unmonumented. A national boundary baseline is used for defining the landward edge or margin of a nation's various contiguous zones such as the 3 and 12 nautical mile limits and the Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ).

objetos.definicion: A reference mark on a permanent object indicating elevation relative to an established datum.
A line separating two geographic areas from each other.
A marker identifying the location of a surveyed boundary line.
A reference point used for orienting a cadastral map.
A heap of stones piled up as a memorial or a landmark.
A terrain object (for example: a marker) with a known location (for example: horizontal position, elevation, or both) intended to serve as a survey control.
objetos.descripcion: Usually of a lower order of positional accuracy than a Geodetic Point but of sufficient accuracy for local surveying.

objetos.definicion: A marker that indicates the value of distance measured from a starting location.
objetos.descripcion: Consists of either a solid visible structure or a distinct location without a special installation.

objetos.definicion: A marker that designates the distance from a given location.
A physical point on the Earth's surface having a known position (for example: as determined by survey) and established as part of a geodetic network.
objetos.descripcion: For example, a triangulation (trig) point.

objetos.definicion: A track along which a series of geophysical data observations are distributed.
A grid established for the collection of geophysical data within an area.
objetos.descripcion: The grid is typically composed of one or more series of observation points where each series is obtained along a single track and the grid is then assembled from multiple tracks.

objetos.definicion: A tract of land that is defined in location and extent according to legally or customarily recognized methods (for example: social tenure).
objetos.descripcion: Improvements (for example: buildings, fences, and wells) to the tract of land are distinct from the land itself and thus may have different associated rights and/or restrictions than those of the underlying tract of land. Social tenure (also called customary tenure) is the allocation and security of rights in land based on customs and social authority, rather than on a formal legal system of land registration. In some areas of the world, social tenure is the basis for informal land administration. Some legal land administration systems recognize and/or incorporate social tenure-based rights. An example of recognition without incorporation is social tenure 'shells', in which areas are set aside where social tenure is the recognized authority for land rights. In other cases, individual social tenure-based rights may be registered within the legal system.

objetos.definicion: A location where horizontal and/or vertical control has been determined by surveying methods.
objetos.descripcion: Surveys are used to establish positions (horizontal or vertical) of selected points. The points are then used to reference other survey observations or measurements.

objetos.definicion: A region of land with definite boundaries, especially one intended for development.
A formally recognized survey or reference location that is not represented by a physical boundary monument and/or benchmark.
A region for which no bathymetric survey information is available.

contenido: This Group consists of Concepts which relate to aspects of aeronautic.
descripcion: It varies from airports, ground facilities and obstructions to airspaces and restrictions in the air.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which define areas on land or water (including buildings, installations and equipment) and which are intended to be used either wholly or in part for the arrival, departure and surface movement of aircrafts/helicopters.

objetos.definicion: A defined area on land or water (including any buildings, installations and equipment) intended to be used either wholly or in part for the arrival, departure and surface movement of aircraft.
A beacon used to indicate the location of an aerodrome from the air.
objetos.descripcion: Aerodrome beacons may consist of either a rotating light source or a strobe light.

objetos.definicion: The geographical limits of an aerodrome property as defined by the local authority.
A modeling entity collecting information regarding the electrical power available at an aerodrome.
The specific location of the highest point of the aerodrome landing area.
objetos.descripcion: Typically this elevation is the highest point on any of the landing runway surfaces, and is considered the specific point at which the official aerodrome elevation is determined.

objetos.definicion: A prescribed location in which the fuelling of aircraft and service vehicles from a fixed fuel pumping station is performed.
A location on an aerodrome movement area with a history or potential risk of either collision or runway incursion, and where heightened attention by pilots/drivers is necessary.
A location denoting the center of the minimum bounding rectangle that defines the functional area of an aerodrome.
objetos.descripcion: The functional area of an aerodrome includes all runways and other aircraft movement areas, hangars, and related facilities required to support aircraft operations.

objetos.definicion: A symbol or group of symbols displayed on the surface of the movement area in order to convey aeronautical information.
That part of an aerodrome to be used for the take-off, landing and taxiing of aircraft, consisting of the manoeuvring area and the apron(s).
objetos.descripcion: This includes any Aerodrome Service Roads when they are collocated with an apron, taxiway, or runway.

objetos.definicion: A lighting system providing guidance to an aircraft or vehicle while on a ground movement area of an aerodrome.
objetos.aliases: Aerodrome Movement Surface Lighting, Surface Lighting System

objetos.definicion: A modeling entity collecting information for areas designed for either the movement or the parking of aircraft and that are not reported elsewhere as aprons, hardstands, or helipads.
The availability of passenger amenities and facilities at or in the vicinity of an aerodrome.
objetos.descripcion: For example, medical facilities located at the aerodrome, or hotels located near the aerodrome.

objetos.definicion: The designated geographic location of an aerodrome as established by the appropriate authority.
objetos.descripcion: The aerodrome reference point shall be located near the initial or planned geometric centre of the aerodrome and shall normally remain where first established.

objetos.definicion: An established surface route on the aerodrome meant for the exclusive use of authorized vehicles and personnel.
objetos.descripcion: Aerodrome service roads do not include public access roads. Examples of authorized vehicles are: fuel, maintenance and emergency trucks.

objetos.definicion: A light specifically provided as an aid to air navigation, with the exception of obstacle lights and lights forming part of surface or approach lighting systems.
Any object, or part thereof, or terrain which rises far enough above the surrounding surface or above a specified height to create a hazard to aircraft operations.
objetos.descripcion: Obstacle objects may be fixed (whether temporary or permanent) or mobile.

objetos.definicion: A point established and marked on the surface of an aerodrome where the checking of a navigation system can be accomplished.
The availability of maintenance, support and/or supply operations to aircraft at an aerodrome.
A building for housing aircraft.
A designated area on an apron intended to be used for parking an aircraft.
A point or area designated at an aerodrome where the checking of an altimeter system can be accomplished.

An airport lighting facility which provides visual guidance to landing aircraft by radiating light beams in a directional pattern by which the pilot aligns the aircraft with the final approach path for landing.
A defined area, on a land aerodrome/heliport, intended to accommodate aircraft/helicopters for purposes of loading and unloading passengers, mail or cargo, and for fuelling, parking or maintenance.

A series of devices (for example: engaging or catching devices and energy absorption devices) that are used to stop an aircraft by absorbing its momentum in a routine landing, emergency landing or aborted take-off.
objetos.descripcion: System types may consist of barriers, cables, nets and or engineered materials.

objetos.definicion: A modeling entity collecting information regarding the aircraft hydraulic fluid types, stock levels, and associated service(s) that are available at an aerodrome.
A modeling entity collecting information regarding the aircraft nitrogen supply types, stock levels, and associated service(s) that are available at an aerodrome.
A modeling entity collecting information regarding the aircraft oil types, stock levels, and associated service(s) that are available at an aerodrome.
A modeling entity collecting information regarding the aircraft oxygen supply types, stock levels, equipment, and associated service(s) that are available at an aerodrome.
A barrier used to divert and/or dissipate jet and/or propeller blast.

A defined rectangular area on the ground or water under the control of the appropriate authority, selected or prepared as a suitable area over which an aircraft may make a portion of its initial climb to a specified height.
objetos.descripcion: A helicopter clearway is a defined area on the ground or water under the control of the appropriate authority, selected and/or prepared as a suitable area over which a performance Class 1 helicopter may accelerate and achieve a specific height.

objetos.definicion: A structure that houses personnel and equipment used to control the flow of traffic within a specified range of an installation.
objetos.descripcion: Examples of installations that use control towers are aerodromes, railways, and maritime routes.

objetos.definicion: An area comprising an inner area for the parking of an aircraft to receive de-icing treatment and an outer area for the manoeuvring of two or more mobile de-icing equipment.

A raised construction that protects a military asset (for example: aircraft or fighting vehicle), equipment (for example: radar station), and/or facility (for example: surface-to-air missile site) from hostile action.
objetos.descripcion: Defensive revetments may be constructed of sandbags, concrete, compacted earth, or other material such as logs or metal. They offer protection against low flying splinters, shrapnel, and/or projectiles from bombs, rockets, grenades, small arms fire and other line-of-sight weapons. High-angle, low-velocity fragments will still impact the exposed site.

objetos.definicion: A defined area over which the final phase of the aircraft/helicopter approach manoeuvre to hover or land is completed and from which the take-off manoeuvre is commenced.
objetos.descripcion: Where the FATO is to be used by performance Class 1 helicopters, the defined area includes the rejected take-off area available.

objetos.nombre: Final Approach and Take-off Area (FATO) Safety Area
objetos.definicion: A defined area on a heliport surrounding the FATO which is free of obstacles, other than those required for air navigation purposes, and intended to reduce the risk of damage to aircraft/helicopters accidentally diverging from the FATO.
A modeling entity collecting information about aircraft ground power equipment at an aerodrome.
objetos.descripcion: This equipment is either located on a trailer and towed or is self-propelled and driven to the aircraft. Ground power equipment does not include aircraft electrical and air start (a power source is used to provide the initial rotation to start an engine).

objetos.definicion: A hardened structure built above or partially above ground that encloses aircraft to provide protection from enemy attack.
objetos.descripcion: The shelter is closed by blast resistant doors and is generally limited in size, only accommodating one or two relatively smaller (for example: fighter) aircraft. Those built to NATO specifications are designed to withstand a direct hit by a 226 kilogram bomb.

objetos.definicion: A designated area, usually with a prepared surface, used for the take-off, landing, or parking of helicopters.
objetos.descripcion: This prepared surface could either be located on land or on a platform over water. It may or may not be associated with an aerodrome. For example: a hospital helipad, and an offshore rig helipad.

objetos.definicion: An aerodrome intended to be used for the arrival, landing, takeoff or departure of vertical takeoff and landing aircraft/helicopters.
An area of defined dimensions about the localizer and glide path antennas where vehicles, including aircraft, are excluded during all Instrument Landing System (ILS) operations.
objetos.descripcion: The critical area is protected because the presence of vehicles and/or aircraft inside its boundaries will cause unacceptable disturbance to the ILS signal-in-space.

objetos.definicion: An area extending beyond the Instrument Landing System (ILS) critical area where the parking and/or movement of vehicles, including aircraft, is controlled in order to prevent the possibility of unacceptable interference to the ILS signal during ILS operations.
objetos.descripcion: The sensitive area is protected against interference caused by large moving objects outside the critical area but still normally within the aerodrome boundary.

objetos.definicion: A designated position intended for traffic control at which taxiing aircraft and vehicles shall stop and hold until further cleared to proceed, when so instructed by the aerodrome control tower.

A position designated on an aerodrome which is suitable for the parking of an aircraft which is known or believed to be the subject of unlawful interference, or which for other reasons needs to be isolated from normal aerodrome activities.
An aerodrome on land intended to be used either wholly or in part for the arrival, departure and surface movement of aircraft.

objetos.nombre: Land and Hold Short Operations (LAHSO) Hold Short Point
objetos.definicion: A point on the runway beyond which a landing aircraft is not authorized to proceed when instructed to conduct a Land and Hold Short Operation (LAHSO).
objetos.descripcion: LAHSO are operations where an aircraft is required to land and hold short of an intersecting runway, taxiway, predetermined point on the runway, or an approach/departure path to enhance aerodrome capacity.

objetos.definicion: A device that indicates visually the direction currently designated for landing and for take-off.
A designated site or structure from which a rocket or missile is launched.
A vertical structure that is used to mark turns and/or provide obstacles around which aircraft may perform low level aerobatic manoeuvres (for example: during racing or training).
objetos.descripcion: It may be either a temporary (for example: being deflated when not in use) or permanent structure that has been placed on dry land or mounted on a barge (for example: on a lake, in a harbour, or along a river).

objetos.definicion: A mast used to secure an airship.
A strip adjacent to the edge of a pavement so prepared as to provide a transition between the pavement and the adjacent surface.
objetos.descripcion: The movement area shoulder is not normally used by vehicles or aircraft, but is provided as an allowable margin in case of emergency situations.

objetos.definicion: An area surrounding commercial airports with scheduled air services and/or military airfields earmarked for the operation of aircraft with jet engines, where building restrictions may be enforced in order to protect the public from dangers, major disadvantages and major irritation due to aircraft noise.
The point on a line that is nearest to a point that is off-line.
objetos.descripcion: For example, a point on the runway centre-line is 'abeam' the Glide Slope Antenna when the distance from the centre-line point to the antenna is a minimum.

objetos.definicion: A defined rectangular area on a land aerodrome prepared for the landing and take-off of aircraft.
An operationally significant position on the centre-line of a runway surface.
objetos.descripcion: Though the runway centre-line point is a fixed location on the runway surface, the operational significance, or how the centre-line point is used, is based upon the runway direction. For example, the touchdown zone centre-line point, while a fixed location on the runway surface, is only applicable to one of the two associated runway directions for that runway surface.

objetos.definicion: A modeling entity collecting available distance information for aerodrome runway directions.
One of the two possible landing and/or take-off directions of a runway or Final Approach and Take-off Area (FATO).
objetos.descripcion: One runway direction is associated with only one runway endpoint.

objetos.definicion: A portion of a runway.
objetos.descripcion: A runway element may also include areas not defined as other portions of the runway (for example: a stopway).

objetos.definicion: An area symmetrical about the extended runway centre line and adjacent to the end of the runway strip that is primarily intended to reduce the risk of damage to an aircraft undershooting or overrunning the runway.
objetos.descripcion: The runway strip is the combination of the runway and, if provided, stopway.

objetos.definicion: The point located on a runway centre-line at either end.

A designated position intended to protect a runway, an obstacle limitation surface, or an ILS/MLS critical/sensitive area at which taxiing aircraft and vehicles shall stop and hold, unless otherwise authorized by the aerodrome control tower.
The intersecting area shared by two or more runways.
A device, normally placed near the threshold of a runway, used for reflecting radar signals.

A defined area including the runway and stopway, if provided, that is intended: a) to reduce the risk of damage to aircraft running off a runway; and b) to protect aircraft flying over it during take-off or landing operations.
The beginning of that portion of the runway that is available for landing.
objetos.descripcion: When the threshold is located at a point on the runway end other than the designated beginning of the runway end it is termed a 'displaced threshold'.

objetos.definicion: A defined area on a land aerodrome adjacent to a runway for the purpose of completing a 180-degree turn on that runway.
A designated portion of water that is outlined by visual surface markings and used by seaplanes to land and take-off.
objetos.aliases: Seaplane Landing Area, Seaplane Take-off Area

objetos.definicion: A defined rectangular area on the ground at the end of the take-off run available that has been prepared as a suitable area in which an aircraft can be stopped in the case of an abandoned take-off.
The point located on a stopway centre-line at the end of the pavement surface.
A defined path at an aerodrome established for the taxiing of aircraft and intended to provide a ground movement link between one part of the aerodrome and another.
A portion of a taxiway.
A load bearing area on which an aircraft/helicopter may touch down or lift-off.
A location where one or more devices have been temporarily or permanently stationed for the purpose of collecting information regarding vehicular and/or pedestrian traffic.
objetos.descripcion: Such information may include analysis of traffic flow, turning movements, speeds, congestion and delays, parking and loading, and pedestrian movement.

objetos.definicion: An airport lighting facility providing vertical approach slope guidance to aircraft during approach to landing.
objetos.descripcion: A directional pattern of high intensity red and white focused light beams which indicate to the pilot that they are either: 'on path' if they see red/white; 'above path' if white/white; and 'below path' if red/red.

objetos.definicion: An aerodrome intended to be used either wholly or in part for the arrival, departure and surface movement of aircraft on water.
A wind-actuated device indicating visually to aircraft the direction of the surface wind.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which contain information about defined regions in the air used for navigation under a specific authority.

objetos.definicion: The navigational center point of a radio navigation installation, determined by either a specified geographic position or by a geographic fix that is referenced to a geographic location.
objetos.descripcion: A radio navigation installation point can be used by itself as a navigational fix or be used in combination with a specific bearing and distance to identify another designated point, which is used for navigational purposes.

objetos.definicion: A prescribed pattern, established by air refuelling points, along which air-to-air refuelling of aircraft is performed.
objetos.descripcion: Air refuelling anchor patterns are usually shaped like an oval racetrack.

objetos.definicion: A geographic position or radio navigation fix along an air refuelling anchor pattern or air refuelling track.
objetos.descripcion: Usages include, for example, entry/exit, rendezvous and navigation checkpoint.

objetos.definicion: A procedure used by the military to transfer fuel from one aircraft to another during flight.
A prescribed path, established by air refuelling points, along which air-to-air refuelling of aircraft is performed.
objetos.descripcion: An air refuelling route shares the same characteristics as an air refuelling track and air refuelling anchor pattern, combining the routing structures of both into one specific path for the aircraft to fly.

objetos.definicion: A prescribed route, established by air refuelling points, geographic points and/or radio navigation fixes, along which air-to-air refuelling of aircraft is performed.
