The availability of one or more flight information services, alerting services, air traffic advisory services, and/or air traffic control services (for example: area control services, approach control services, and aerodrome control services).

objetos.nombre: Air Traffic Service (ATS) Route Crossing Information
objetos.definicion: A modeling entity collecting information regarding the relationship between an Air Traffic Service (ATS) route segment direction and the ATS route significant point, and how the two are used in an aircraft navigation environment.
objetos.descripcion: For example, minimum altitudes for crossing an aviation designated point onto the same air traffic service route or crossing onto a different air traffic service route segment.

objetos.definicion: A portion of an Air Traffic Service (ATS) route to be flown between two consecutive significant points.

objetos.nombre: Air Traffic Service (ATS) Route Segment Direction
objetos.definicion: One of the two possible directions in which an aircraft may travel along an Air Traffic Service (ATS) route segment.

objetos.nombre: Air Traffic Service (ATS) Route Significant Point
objetos.definicion: A designated point within the airspace structure which serves as a beginning, intermediate, or ending point for an Air Traffic Service (ATS) route.
A defined three dimensional region of space relevant to air traffic.
A modeling entity describing specific activities that may occur within the airspace or portions of the airspace.
objetos.descripcion: For example, parachute jump or aerobatics areas may occur within an airspace.

objetos.definicion: A defined volume in the air, described as horizontal projection with vertical limits, used to sectionalize the sky for facilitating air traffic services.

A specified route designed for channeling the flow of traffic as necessary for the provision of air traffic service (ATS) from the end of the take-off and initial climb phase to the commencement of the approach and landing phase.

A set of parameters used to define two specific geometric locations used as navigational points for aircraft utilizing precision Area Navigation (RNAV) approach procedures to land an aircraft in adverse approach conditions.
The portion of an Instrument Approach Procedure (IAP) between the initial approach fix and the runway.
objetos.descripcion: IAP segments include: initial, intermediate, transition, final, and missed approach legs.

objetos.nombre: Instrument Flight Rules (IFR) Takeoff Minimum Information
objetos.definicion: A modeling entity defining the minimum climb gradient and speed that an aircraft must maintain until reaching a specified altitude.
objetos.descripcion: Takeoff minimums are usually defined based on prominent obstacles along the designated flight path, requiring that an aircraft be at a minimum altitude above those obstacles when passing over them.

objetos.definicion: A modeling entity collecting information about alternative characteristics and textual descriptions of an aviation missed approach procedure.
A subdivision of a Safe Altitude Area (SAA) within which there is a single set of minimum altitudes.
objetos.descripcion: A safe altitude area defines an obstruction-free minimum altitude for safe aircraft operations within 25 nautical miles of an aerodrome. An SAA is usually divided into sectors, allowing lower altitudes at certain areas around the aerodrome, based on where common aircraft operations may take place.

objetos.definicion: A unit that is designated as the appropriate responder for a specified search and rescue region.
The use and location relative to an airspace of a significant point.
objetos.descripcion: A significant point is a specified geographical location used to define an Air Traffic Service (ATS) route, the flight path of an aircraft and/or for other navigation/ATS purposes.

objetos.definicion: A series of predetermined maneuvers used to transition an aircraft either from the enroute phase of flight to the aerodrome, or from the aerodrome to the enroute phase of flight.
Minimum weather condition requirements established for either take-off or landing operations.
objetos.descripcion: Procedure minima may include weather conditions such as prevailing visibility, overcast cloud cover or precipitation.

objetos.definicion: A geographic position or radio navigation fix along a procedure segment leg.
objetos.descripcion: It is a type of aviation designated point that is primarily used in the terminal phase of flight.

objetos.definicion: A published procedure used to connect either the basic terminal instrument procedure to one of several enroute Air Traffic Service (ATS) routes, or to connect one of several enroute ATS routes to the basic terminal instrument procedure.
A specified geographical location used to define an area navigation route or the flight path of an aircraft employing area navigation.

subcategorias.nombre: NAVAIDS, Landing Aids, Points and/or Obstacles
subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which describe a collection of technical or other types of aids for the navigation and/or landing of aircrafts and specify geographical locations, that are either used for navigation or pose a danger to it.

objetos.definicion: The site and equipment of a radar station designed to detect all principal features on the surface of an aerodrome, including aircraft and vehicular traffic, and to present the entire image on a radar indicator console in the aerodrome control tower.
objetos.descripcion: The aerodrome surface detection system is used to augment visual observation by tower personnel of aircraft and/or vehicular movements on aerodrome movement surfaces (for example: runways and taxiways).

objetos.definicion: A ground based piece of electronic equipment that provides aeronautical navigation guidance information or position data.
The navigational center point of a radio navigation installation, determined by either a specified geographic position or by a geographic fix that is referenced to a geographic location.
objetos.descripcion: A radio navigation installation point can be used by itself as a navigational fix or be used in combination with a specific bearing and distance to identify another designated point, which is used for navigational purposes.

objetos.definicion: A service providing aeronautical navigation guidance information or position data, intended for the benefit and safe operation of aircraft.
A point established and marked on the surface of an aerodrome where the checking of a navigation system can be accomplished.

An airport lighting facility which provides visual guidance to landing aircraft by radiating light beams in a directional pattern by which the pilot aligns the aircraft with the final approach path for landing.

The site and equipment of an automated sensor suite that measures, collects, and disseminates weather data to serve aviation and meteorological needs for safe and efficient aviation operations and weather forecasting.

A named geographical location not marked by the site of a radio navigation aid, used in defining an Air Traffic Service (ATS) route, the flight path of an aircraft and/or for other navigation or ATS purposes.
A low or medium powered Non-Directional Beacon (NDB) used as an aid for final approach.
objetos.descripcion: A locator usually has an average radius of rated coverage of between 18.5 and 46.3 kilometres (10 and 25 nautical miles).

objetos.definicion: Ultra High Frequency (UHF) ground equipment that is used in conjunction with airborne equipment to determine distance between the airborne and ground equipment.
objetos.descripcion: DME Distance is defined as the line of sight distance (slant range) from the source of a DME signal to the receiving antenna. DME operates on the interrogation-answer principle where the time required for the round trip of the signal exchange is measured in the airborne DME unit and translated into DME Distance.

objetos.definicion: A wide area service based on a satellite constellation providing radio frequency signals which can be used by airborne equipment to determine the aircraft's two-dimensional position, or depending upon the capabilities of the system, a three-dimensional position.
objetos.descripcion: For example: GLObal NAvigation Satellite System (GLONASS), Global Positioning System (GPS), Wide Area Augmentation System (WAAS), or European Geostationary Navigation Overlay Service (EGNOS).

objetos.definicion: A combination of radio navigation services intended to facilitate aircraft in landing by providing lateral and vertical guidance including indications of distance from the optimum point of landing.
objetos.descripcion: A precision instrument approach system which normally consists of the following electronic components and visual aids: localizer, glide slope, outer marker, middle marker, and approach lights.

objetos.definicion: A component of an Instrument Landing System (ILS) consisting of an Ultra High Frequency (UHF) transmitter radiating signals and providing a straight-line descent path in the vertical plane containing the centre line of the runway served by the ILS, and thereby furnishing descent information down to the surface of the runway.
objetos.descripcion: The descent information is that locus of points in the vertical plane containing the runway centre line at which the receiver indicator deflection is zero.

objetos.definicion: A component of an Instrument Landing System (ILS) consisting of a VHF transmitter, radiating signals in the direction served by the ILS, and providing a straight line azimuth path in the horizontal plane containing the centre line of the runway.
A Very High Frequency (VHF) transmitter, radiating signals in a particular direction in order to provide a straight line azimuth path in the horizontal plane to the centre line of a runway.
objetos.descripcion: The Localizer-type Directional Aid (LDA) is of comparable use and accuracy to a localizer but is not part of a complete Instrument Landing System (ILS). The LDA course usually provides a more precise approach course than the similar Simplified Directional Facility (SDF) installation, utilizing a course width of 3 to 6 arc degrees instead of the 6 to 12 arc degrees that a typical SDF may provide.

objetos.definicion: A vertical structure that is used to mark turns and/or provide obstacles around which aircraft may perform low level aerobatic manoeuvres (for example: during racing or training).
objetos.descripcion: It may be either a temporary (for example: being deflated when not in use) or permanent structure that has been placed on dry land or mounted on a barge (for example: on a lake, in a harbour, or along a river).

objetos.definicion: A radio navigation service identifying a particular location in space by means of a 75 megahertz (MHz) transmitter which transmits a directional signal to be received by aircraft flying overhead.
objetos.descripcion: For example: fan, 'Z', or compass locator.

objetos.definicion: A precision approach and landing guidance system operating in the microwave spectrum, which provides position information and various ground-to-air data.
objetos.descripcion: The position information is provided in a wide coverage sector and is determined by an azimuth angle, elevation, and distance.

objetos.definicion: A component of a Microwave Landing System (MLS) consisting of a Super High Frequency (SHF) transmitter radiating signals to provide lateral indications to aircraft approaching the runway.
objetos.descripcion: The lateral information is the locus of points in any horizontal plane where the decoded guidance angle is constant. SHF is the frequency band between 3 and 30 gigahertz (GHz). The elevation and azimuth stations of the Microwave Landing System operate from 5031 to 5091 megahertz (MHz) in this spectrum.

objetos.definicion: A component of a Microwave Landing System (MLS) consisting of an Super High Frequency (SHF) transmitter radiating signals to provide vertical indications as an angular value to aircraft approaching the runway.
objetos.descripcion: The vertical information is the locus of points in any vertical plane where the decoded guidance angle is constant. SHF is the frequency band between 3 and 30 gigahertz (GHz). The elevation and azimuth stations of the Microwave Landing System operate from 5031 to 5091 megahertz (MHz) in this spectrum.

objetos.definicion: A low or medium radio navigation service transmitting signals whereby the pilot of a suitably equipped aircraft can determine bearings, 'home in' on, and/or track to or from the station.
objetos.descripcion: The radio frequencies assigned to an NDB shall be selected from those available in that portion of the spectrum between 190 and 1750 kilohertz (kHz).

objetos.definicion: The airspace above the inner approach surface, inner transitional surfaces, and balked landing surface and that portion of the strip bounded by these surfaces, which is not penetrated by any fixed obstacle other than a low-mass and frangibly mounted one required for air navigation purposes.

Primary radar equipment used to determine the position of an aircraft during final approach, in terms of lateral and vertical deviations relative to a nominal approach path, and in range relative to touchdown.
objetos.descripcion: Precision approach radars are designated to enable pilots of aircraft to be given guidance by radio communication during the final stages of the approach to land.

objetos.definicion: The allowable circular sector coverage of a navigational aid signal.
A factor which would detract expected performance of a navigational aid signal circular sector.
A network of ground stations and satellites designed to receive navigation signals, improving the accuracy and ensuring the integrity of information for navigation and landing.
A specified geographical location used to define an air traffic service (ATS) route, the flight path of an aircraft or for other navigation/ATS purposes.
The use and location relative to an airspace of a significant point.
objetos.descripcion: A significant point is a specified geographical location used to define an Air Traffic Service (ATS) route, the flight path of an aircraft and/or for other navigation/ATS purposes.

objetos.definicion: A directional aid facility providing only lateral guidance (front or back course) for a terminal instrument approach from a final approach fix.
objetos.descripcion: The Simplified Directional Facility (SDF) provides a final approach course similar to that of the Instrument Landing System (ILS) localizer, however an SDF is intended only for use by non-precision approach procedures. It is generally less accurate than a localizer, and may not be aligned to the runway. The SDF signal is fixed at either 6 or 12 arc degrees course width as necessary to provide maximum flyability and optimum course quality.

objetos.definicion: A wide area (worldwide) service based on a chain of land stations providing radio frequency signals which can be used by airborne equipment to determine the aircraft's two-dimensional position.
objetos.descripcion: For example: Decca Navigator System or LOng Range Aid to Navigation (LORAN).

objetos.definicion: A land based facility emitting a radio signal for a special navigation system.
A military Ultra High Frequency (UHF) radio navigation service able to provide continuous bearing and Distance Measuring Equipment (DME) distance to a selected station.
objetos.descripcion: A navigation system developed by military and naval forces providing, as far as the navigating pilot is concerned and for suitably equipped aircraft, the same indication as a VOR/DME system. DME Distance is defined as the line of sight distance (slant range) from the source of a DME signal to the receiving antenna.

objetos.definicion: The elevation and transponder emission sensor of a transponder landing system.
objetos.descripcion: A transponder landing system is a precision landing system that uses the transponder emissions of an airborne aircraft coupled with ground elevation sensors to determine the position of the aircraft, and then sending the aircraft guidance signals via existing onboard Instrument Landing System (ILS) equipment. The transponder landing system is often used to create a precision approach at a location where an ILS would normally not be available due to cost or terrain issues.

objetos.definicion: A Very High Frequency (VHF) radio navigation service which uses phase comparisons of a ground transmitted signal to determine bearing.
objetos.descripcion: This term is derived from the expression 'very high frequency omnidirectional radio range'.

objetos.definicion: A specified geographical location used to define an area navigation route or the flight path of an aircraft employing area navigation.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which are used for services furnished to personnel and/or institutions concerned with flight operations, various Organisations and Authorities.

objetos.definicion: A modeling entity collecting information regarding the electrical power available at an aerodrome.
A prescribed location in which the fuelling of aircraft and service vehicles from a fixed fuel pumping station is performed.
The availability of passenger amenities and facilities at or in the vicinity of an aerodrome.
objetos.descripcion: For example, medical facilities located at the aerodrome, or hotels located near the aerodrome.

objetos.definicion: The site and equipment of a radar station designed to detect all principal features on the surface of an aerodrome, including aircraft and vehicular traffic, and to present the entire image on a radar indicator console in the aerodrome control tower.
objetos.descripcion: The aerodrome surface detection system is used to augment visual observation by tower personnel of aircraft and/or vehicular movements on aerodrome movement surfaces (for example: runways and taxiways).

objetos.definicion: The availability of one or more flight information services, alerting services, air traffic advisory services, and/or air traffic control services (for example: area control services, approach control services, and aerodrome control services).
The availability of maintenance, support and/or supply operations to aircraft at an aerodrome.

The site and equipment of an automated sensor suite that measures, collects, and disseminates weather data to serve aviation and meteorological needs for safe and efficient aviation operations and weather forecasting.
A modeling entity collecting information regarding the aircraft hydraulic fluid types, stock levels, and associated service(s) that are available at an aerodrome.
A modeling entity collecting information regarding the aircraft nitrogen supply types, stock levels, and associated service(s) that are available at an aerodrome.
A modeling entity collecting information regarding the aircraft oil types, stock levels, and associated service(s) that are available at an aerodrome.
A modeling entity collecting information regarding the aircraft oxygen supply types, stock levels, equipment, and associated service(s) that are available at an aerodrome.
A structure that houses personnel and equipment used to control the flow of traffic within a specified range of an installation.
objetos.descripcion: Examples of installations that use control towers are aerodromes, railways, and maritime routes.

objetos.definicion: A modeling entity collecting information regarding the availability and specifics of customs and immigration, including the facilities used for this service.
A modeling entity collecting information regarding the service available at an aerodrome that is comprised of equipment available with which to start the engine(s) of a jet aircraft.
A predefined geographic area in which a specific search and rescue organization(s) is responsible for operating.
An organization that is responsible for planning, coordinating, and executing search and rescue services within a specified search and rescue region.

The performance of distress monitoring, communication, coordination and search and rescue functions, initial medical assistance or medical evacuation, through the use of public and private resources, including cooperating aircraft, vessels and other craft and installations.
A unit that is designated as the appropriate responder for a specified search and rescue region.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which describe series of predetermined manoeuvres for an aircraft, in order to perform a save landing or take-off.
subcategorias.descripcion: This includes Concepts required for terminal procedures design.

objetos.definicion: The portion of an arrival route which aircraft may proceed from the en-route phase of flight to an initial approach fix.
objetos.descripcion: May be defined by one or more procedure segment legs.

objetos.definicion: The portion of a departure route between the runway and the first en-route segment.
objetos.descripcion: May be defined by one or more procedure segment legs.

objetos.definicion: That segment of an Instrument Approach Procedure (IAP) in which alignment and descent for landing are accomplished.
objetos.descripcion: May be defined by one or more procedure segment legs.

objetos.definicion: A predetermined manoeuvre which keeps an aircraft within a specified airspace while awaiting further clearance.
That segment of an instrument approach procedure between the initial approach fix and the intermediate fix or, where applicable, the final approach fix or point.
objetos.descripcion: May be defined by one or more procedure segment legs.

objetos.definicion: A series of predetermined manoeuvres by reference to flight instruments with specified protection from obstacles from the initial approach fix, or where applicable, from the beginning of a defined arrival route to a point from which a landing can be completed and thereafter, if a landing is not completed, to a position at which holding or en-route obstacle clearance criteria apply.
objetos.descripcion: Instrument approach procedures are classified as follows: 1. Non-precision approach (NPA) procedure: An instrument approach procedure which utilizes lateral guidance but does not utilize vertical guidance; 2. Approach procedure with vertical guidance (APV): An instrument procedure which utilizes lateral and vertical guidance but does not meet the requirements established for precision approach and landing operations; 3. Precision approach (PA) procedure: An instrument approach procedure using precision lateral and vertical guidance with minima as determined by the category of operation. Note that lateral and vertical guidance refers to the guidance provided either by: a) a ground-based navigation aid; or b) computer-generated navigation data.

objetos.definicion: That segment of an Instrument Approach Procedure (IAP) between either the intermediate fix and the final approach fix or point, or between the end of a reversal, racetrack or dead reckoning track procedure and the final approach fix or point, as appropriate.
objetos.descripcion: May be defined by one or more procedure segment legs.

objetos.definicion: The missed approach segment begins at the missed approach point, missed approach waypoint, or the point upon arrival at decision height, and ends at the specified missed approach NAVAID, intersection, fix or waypoint, as appropriate at the minimum Instrument Flight Rules (IFR) altitude.
objetos.descripcion: May be defined by one or more procedure segment legs.

objetos.definicion: A part of an instrument or visual flight procedure defined by two consecutive significant points.
A segment on which aircraft proceed directly from the en-route phase of flight to an initial approach fix.
objetos.descripcion: May be defined by one or more procedure segment legs.

objetos.definicion: A defined area with applicable minimum altitude providing a minimum required clearance above all objects located in the area for a defined terminal procedure(s).

A designated Instrument Flight Rule (IFR) arrival route linking a significant point, normally on an Air Traffic Service (ATS) route, with a point from which a published instrument approach procedure can be commenced.
A procedure by which a departure route is designated following the Instrument Flight Rules (IFR).
objetos.descripcion: This route links the aerodrome or a specific runway of the aerodrome with a specified significant point, normally on a designated Air Traffic Service (ATS) route, at which the en-route phase of a flight commences.

objetos.definicion: The lowest altitude that will provide a minimum clearance of 300 metres (1000 feet) above all objects located in an arc of a circle defined by a 46 kilometre (25 nautical mile) radius centred on the initial approach fix (IAF), or where there is no IAF then centered on the intermediate approach fix (IF), delimited by straight lines joining the extremity of the arc to the IAF/IF.
objetos.descripcion: The combined TAAs associated with an approach procedure shall account for an area of 360 arc degrees around the IF. Terminal Arrival Areas may be provided for RNAV approaches to facilitate descent and entry to the procedure. TAAs are associated with an RNAV procedure based upon the 'T' or 'Y' Arrangement. The Basic 'T' approach segment configuration is the standard configuration for transition from the en route to the terminal environment. The standard arrangement consists of three TAAs: straight-in, right base, and left base.

objetos.definicion: A subdivision of the Terminal Arrival Altitude (TAA) to allow for one or more minimum altitudes.
objetos.descripcion: The lowest altitude will provide a minimum clearance of 300 metres (1000 feet) above all objects located in the sector.

contenido: This Group consists of Concepts which relate to military installations or operational military structures.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which relate to military installations and facilities and/or to operational structures.

objetos.definicion: A site and related facilities (for example: buildings and/or radar equipment) for storing and launching anti-aircraft artillery.
objetos.descripcion: Walls, if any, that surround the site are typically used as the basis for delineation.

objetos.definicion: A location on a beach suitable for the landing of troops and vehicles.
An encampment where tents and/or other easily moveable structures (for example: yurts) serve as full-time, temporary, or seasonal residences.
An area containing military quarters.
objetos.descripcion: Typically consisting of the residential sections of a military installation, where tactical training may be limited due to other activities that would endanger and disrupt personnel and their dependents.

objetos.definicion: A single large fortified building that has thick walls, battlements, and often the presence of a moat, and is commonly of some historical significance.
objetos.descripcion: Historically castles were designed and constructed as defensive structures situated so as to dominate the surrounding countryside. With advancing technology, especially artillery, they have become obsolete for military defensive purposes and are now valued primarily for their historical significance. In more recent times elaborate country houses were built incorporating many design elements of a castle but which were not fully capable of being used as defensive structures. Examples of castles of both types include Doue-la-Fontaine and Neuschwanstein.

objetos.definicion: A fortified complex of buildings and related structures that consists principally of a central keep with surrounding thick walls, battlements, and often the presence of a moat, and is commonly of some historical significance.
objetos.descripcion: A castle complex may be quite extensive, including multiple distinct buildings of diverse function. Historically castle complexes were designed and constructed as defensive structures situated so as to dominate the surrounding countryside. With advancing technology, especially artillery, they have become obsolete for military defensive purposes and are now valued primarily for their historical significance. Examples of castle complexes include Prague and Windsor Castles.

objetos.definicion: A location to control passage and/or to register, declare and/or inspect goods, vehicles and/or people.
Upward-pointing obstacles laid in the ground to slow or stop the movement of vehicles.
objetos.descripcion: Typically constructed of regularly spaced concrete or metal shapes laid in single or multiple rows.

objetos.definicion: A facility utilizing long-range radar to detect approaching aircraft and/or missiles.
An excavation and/or embankment created by remolding the natural configuration of the terrain for the purpose of enhancing the defense of a site from armed attack.
objetos.descripcion: The earthwork may include ancillary elements (for example: a palisade) or reinforcements (for example: a concrete facing).

objetos.definicion: A structure constructed for the military defence of a site.
objetos.descripcion: For example, a bastion and a rampart.

objetos.definicion: A building that is specifically designed or reinforced to provide for defense from armed attack.
A facility for the storage of fuel (for example: jet fuel, gasoline, or diesel oil).
objetos.descripcion: The fuel is typically stored in large tanks that may be partially or wholly buried and is accompanied by metering and dispensing equipment. Facilities may range in size from a small stockpile of drums (sometimes termed a 'fuel dump') to a large perimeter-controlled site with multiple permanent surface tanks, in-ground pipelines and associated equipment (sometimes termed a 'fuel depot').

objetos.definicion: A structure intended for short term occupancy to protect personnel from injury.
objetos.descripcion: For example, a slit trench or other excavation either open or covered by sandbags, fill, or other material and supported by logs or other framing. May be more elaborate with many of the characteristics of an underground bunker.

objetos.definicion: A cluster of structures that combine to form a homogeneous area when grouped according to a common radar reflectance and a common height value.
Steps at the shoreline as the connection between land and water on different levels.
The route or routes designated within an area of operations upon which the bulk of traffic flows in support of military operations.
objetos.descripcion: See AAP-6(2007), page 2-M-1.

objetos.definicion: An installation designed for military use.
objetos.descripcion: For example, used to perform military operations, initiate forward movements, and/or furnish supplies. Often protected by fortifications or natural advantages.

objetos.definicion: A sub-division or portion of a military installation.
A trench dug for military purposes.
Equipment for the assembly, preparation, test and/or firing of missiles.
A site and related facilities for storing and launching missiles.
An area for the preparation and/or testing of missiles.
A facility for the storage of munitions (for example: bombs, missiles, warheads, mines or ammunition).
objetos.descripcion: Specifically, storage of weapons charged with: explosives; propellant; pyrotechnics; initiating composition; or nuclear, chemical, or biological material for use in military operations. Facilities may range in size from a small stockpile of munitions (sometimes termed an 'ammo dump') that may be revetted to a large perimeter-controlled site with multiple dispersed bunkers laid out to minimize the effect of accidental detonation (sometimes termed a 'munitions depot').

objetos.definicion: A facility utilizing radar to detect and analyze objects (for example: aircraft, artificial satellites, asteroids, and/or missiles) and/or environmental phenomena (for example: tornadoes).
objetos.descripcion: May include both a radar aerial as well as a structure housing radar equipment.

objetos.definicion: A surface structure that may be covered and/or surrounded with earth and is resistant to ordnance.
objetos.descripcion: Used, for example, for storage and/or aircraft protection.

objetos.definicion: A reinforced underground shelter.
objetos.descripcion: May be located within a mountain or buried below the terrain. Often used as an underground facility for military command, control, and/or troop billeting.

objetos.definicion: A site that is intended to launch or fire weapons (for example, missiles or artillery).

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which define borders or zones of military used areas in which special restrictions are applied and/or which are of special interest for military purposes.

objetos.definicion: A terrain region between a contact zone and the first passable land transportation route (for example: a road).
A line established by opposing political groups as a result of cessation of hostilities.
A line along which active hostilities are suspended.
A limit of an area which is unilaterally claimed by one political group without consent or negotiation with another.
A terrain strip 3 metres wide limited on the water side by the contact between land and water (under average water level conditions).
A terrain strip extending from 2 metres below to 6 metres inland of the Mean Water Line.
A region whose prevailing natural conditions have been degraded through contamination by harmful or objectionable substances.
objetos.descripcion: The contamination may be either naturally occurring or the result of human activity. For example, polluted by sewage or toxic chemicals, obscured by smoke or ash from volcanic eruptions, or contaminated by exposure to Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and/or Nuclear (CBRN) agents.

objetos.definicion: A line established to regulate matters between nations or groups over a specific area or territory.
An existing line of separation not officially recognized by various governments.
A region where military activity is prohibited.
A site designated for the purpose of discharging firearms or detonating munitions.
An area in which certain activities or factors of significance to navigation and/or operation apply.
A line where on either side certain activities or factors of significance to navigation and/or operation apply.
An area which is the responsibility of territorial commands.
A sub-division or portion of a military installation.
An area where Mine Counter Measure operations have taken place.
objetos.descripcion: Operation could comprise detection but not neccessarily removal or neutralisation.

objetos.definicion: A site laid with explosive mines.
Equipment for the assembly, preparation, test and/or firing of missiles.
An area for the preparation and/or testing of missiles.
An area where Naval forces (for example: vessels or aircraft) conduct firing and/or munition exercises.
objetos.descripcion: Distinguished from areas where Naval forces conduct general operations and manoeuvers.

objetos.definicion: An area where Naval forces conduct operations.
objetos.descripcion: Distinguished from areas where Naval forces conduct firing and/or munition exercises.

objetos.definicion: A region temporarily held and controlled by a foreign military force.
A region that has been determined to be clear of navigational dangers to a specified depth.
A site reserved for training.
An underground geological formation that is used to store materials, especially liquids and/or gases.
objetos.descripcion: The formation may be either natural (for example: a depleted oil reservoir), man-made for other purposes (for example: an abandoned mine), or intentionally engineered for the purpose of storage (for example: a hard rock cavern). Packaged (for example: in drums or on pallets) or bulk (for example: coal or grain) materials may also be stored.

objetos.definicion: A site that is intended to launch or fire weapons (for example, missiles or artillery).

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which relate to certain operations or special eventsfor military or security purposes.

objetos.definicion: An occurrence of criminal action against a ship.
objetos.descripcion: For example, the use of force to accomplish unauthorized boarding or specific acts of piracy such as hijacking, robbery, and the shooting and/or murder of the ships' crew and/or passengers.

objetos.definicion: A location that is marked or designated as a meeting or an assembly point for a specific purpose (for example: evacuation) for specific individuals.

A length or single point along a route that due to its width, surface quality, alignment, fixed human activity or fixed human feature is likely to impede movement at a constant speed resulting in slowing, and either by vehicular bunching or by type may cause temporary halts.
An excavation and/or embankment created by remolding the natural configuration of the terrain for the purpose of enhancing the defense of a site from armed attack.
objetos.descripcion: The earthwork may include ancillary elements (for example: a palisade) or reinforcements (for example: a concrete facing).

objetos.definicion: A location where an undesirable event is a potential risk or has occurred.
objetos.descripcion: The incident can be a natural event (for example: a landslide) or an event provoked by human act.

objetos.definicion: An area where Naval forces (for example: vessels or aircraft) conduct firing and/or munition exercises.
objetos.descripcion: Distinguished from areas where Naval forces conduct general operations and manoeuvers.

objetos.definicion: An area where Naval forces conduct operations.
objetos.descripcion: Distinguished from areas where Naval forces conduct firing and/or munition exercises.

objetos.definicion: A crossing or turn pad where tracked military vehicles cross over other transportation elements.
objetos.descripcion: Typically a hardened area minimizing the impact of tracked vehicles on the underlying transportation feature (for example: road or railway). May be used as a crossing over other transportation, or a turn pad within a system of tank trails.

objetos.definicion: A designated route where tracked military vehicles have jurisdiction to travel, usually within a military training area.

contenido: This Group consists of Concepts which relate to relatively static weather phenomena and/or climatic conditions.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts describing relatively stable weather phenomenas like wind conditions.

objetos.definicion: Minimum weather condition requirements established for either take-off or landing operations.
objetos.descripcion: Procedure minima may include weather conditions such as prevailing visibility, overcast cloud cover or precipitation.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts describing climate conditions like temperature or precipitation.

objetos.definicion: The limit of a region that is defined by inorganic (for example: climate, relief, water balance or atmosphere) or organic (for example: flora or fauna) factors.
objetos.descripcion: For example: a timberline or a cultivation limit.

objetos.definicion: A region that is defined by inorganic (for example: climate, relief, water balance or atmosphere) or organic (for example: flora or fauna) factors.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts describing climate zones and/or regions with special climate conditions.

objetos.definicion: A region with relatively homogenous climatic conditions.
The limit of a region that is defined by inorganic (for example: climate, relief, water balance or atmosphere) or organic (for example: flora or fauna) factors.
objetos.descripcion: For example: a timberline or a cultivation limit.

objetos.definicion: A region that is defined by inorganic (for example: climate, relief, water balance or atmosphere) or organic (for example: flora or fauna) factors.

contenido: This Group consists of Concepts which describe the appearance of other Concepts.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which describe a position of a Concept.
subcategorias.descripcion: This could be an (absolute) coordinate but also a position relative to another Concept or to a locality.

objetos.definicion: The specific location of the highest point of the aerodrome landing area.
objetos.descripcion: Typically this elevation is the highest point on any of the landing runway surfaces, and is considered the specific point at which the official aerodrome elevation is determined.

objetos.definicion: A location denoting the center of the minimum bounding rectangle that defines the functional area of an aerodrome.
objetos.descripcion: The functional area of an aerodrome includes all runways and other aircraft movement areas, hangars, and related facilities required to support aircraft operations.

objetos.definicion: An operationally significant position on the centre-line of a runway surface.
objetos.descripcion: Though the runway centre-line point is a fixed location on the runway surface, the operational significance, or how the centre-line point is used, is based upon the runway direction. For example, the touchdown zone centre-line point, while a fixed location on the runway surface, is only applicable to one of the two associated runway directions for that runway surface.

objetos.definicion: A predefined geographic area in which a specific search and rescue organization(s) is responsible for operating.
A location where horizontal and/or vertical control has been determined by surveying methods.
objetos.descripcion: Surveys are used to establish positions (horizontal or vertical) of selected points. The points are then used to reference other survey observations or measurements.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which describe a Concept in its dimensions, for example its length, width, heights, area etc, its capacity or other measurable quantities like frequency or speed.

objetos.definicion: An area of the surface of the Earth that shares a common characterization of its level of atmospheric humidity.
An area of the surface of the Earth that shares a common characterization of its level of precipitation.
A known point that is used to verify the measurements of a sensor or sensor array.
objetos.descripcion: Measurements taken from a calibration point are used to verify the accuracy and correctness of the sensor(s) and are also used as the basis for sensor adjustment.

objetos.definicion: An area of the surface of the Earth that shares a common characterization of its solar irradiance.
objetos.descripcion: Solar irradiance primarily falls in the spectral range of approximately 0.3-3 metres in wavelength, where the shortest wavelengths are in the ultraviolet region of the spectrum, the intermediate wavelengths in the visible region, and the longer wavelengths are in the near infrared. Total solar irradiance means that the solar flux has been integrated over all wavelengths to include the contributions from ultraviolet, visible, and infrared radiation.

objetos.definicion: A geographic area characterized by statistically derived and/or aggregated properties (for example: population age profile, distribution of land uses, probability of types of events).
objetos.descripcion: These areas may be characterized by statistics in one or both of the following ways: (1) delineation of the area, wholly or partially, on a statistical basis (for example: a population threshold is applied, as for a Census Tract); (2) a statistical description of the area is developed (for example: age and gender statistics; economic statistics; or natural hazard occurrences within the area). Special constraints may be applied, such as: (a) the value of one or more statistical parameters is the same throughout the area, and different from adjacent areas; (b) the value of some statistical parameter(s) falls within a range that applies throughout the area.

objetos.definicion: A location where horizontal and/or vertical control has been determined by surveying methods.
objetos.descripcion: Surveys are used to establish positions (horizontal or vertical) of selected points. The points are then used to reference other survey observations or measurements.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which describe a relative or absolute date and/or a duration of time relating to a Concept.

objetos.definicion: A line designated as the place on the Earth where each calendar day begins.
objetos.descripcion: This line generally coincides with the 180th meridian but is modified to avoid land.

objetos.definicion: A geographic area characterized by statistically derived and/or aggregated properties (for example: population age profile, distribution of land uses, probability of types of events).
objetos.descripcion: These areas may be characterized by statistics in one or both of the following ways: (1) delineation of the area, wholly or partially, on a statistical basis (for example: a population threshold is applied, as for a Census Tract); (2) a statistical description of the area is developed (for example: age and gender statistics; economic statistics; or natural hazard occurrences within the area). Special constraints may be applied, such as: (a) the value of one or more statistical parameters is the same throughout the area, and different from adjacent areas; (b) the value of some statistical parameter(s) falls within a range that applies throughout the area.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which describe the appearance of a Concept like the colour, the shape or other visible occurrence but also internal forms like the structure of a Concept.

objetos.definicion: A location at which text pertaining to that location is annotated.
objetos.descripcion: For example, a characteristic or activity pertaining to the location may be described.

objetos.definicion: An area that is affected by a natural disaster (for example: an earthquake, a volcano eruption or flooding).
objetos.descripcion: The effect maybe a long-term event (for example: an aggradation or a desertification).

objetos.definicion: An area that is estimated as potentially threatened by natural disasters because of former events or specific circumstances (for example: geological parameters).
A point from which exit can be made from a beach.
A modeling entity collecting information (for example: its method of formation, its access orientation, its cultural significance) about a cave.
An area which is related to specific homogeneous metadata.
A location associated with a feature where a significant characteristic of that feature changes.
objetos.descripcion: For example, the number of lanes of a road or the number of tracks of a railway.

objetos.definicion: Minimum weather condition requirements established for either take-off or landing operations.
objetos.descripcion: Procedure minima may include weather conditions such as prevailing visibility, overcast cloud cover or precipitation.

objetos.definicion: A section of a transportation route where its size (for example: narrowing or expansion in width) and/or operating speed is significantly different than in the adjacent sections of the route.
objetos.descripcion: For example, an increase or decrease in the number of lanes in a road. Constrictions along or beside a transportation route may impede the flow of vehicles or people thus resulting in 'choke points'.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which relate to the function and/or the status of a Concept like schedules of operation or the condition of a Concept.

objetos.definicion: A modeling entity collecting information for areas designed for either the movement or the parking of aircraft and that are not reported elsewhere as aprons, hardstands, or helipads.
A modeling entity collecting information (for example: its method of formation, its access orientation, its cultural significance) about a cave.
An area which is related to specific homogeneous metadata.
The line of demarcation specifying the operational limits of a functional area controlled by a recognized authority.
objetos.descripcion: The geographic limits of the Installation Boundary may include both land and water currently owned or used by the recognized controlling installation or facility. Typically, the Installation Boundary will enclose a grouping of facilities, located in the same general vicinity, which support functions particular to the needs and requirements of the installation property. The controlling installation or facility may have been constructed to support military operations.

objetos.definicion: A modeling entity collecting available distance information for aerodrome runway directions.

contenido: This Group consists of Concepts which name and/or designate a Concept.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which describe a name of a Concept.

objetos.definicion: A modeling entity collecting the set of geographic name(s) used to denote a feature along with a geographic location suitable for use in a gazetteer.
A modeling entity specifying both a name used to denote a feature and related information establishing the context for, and use of, that name.
A geographically defined part of the land.
objetos.descripcion: It may have a proper name (for example: the Alps, the Rocky Mountains or the Great Plains).

objetos.definicion: A tract of natural territory, defined by its geographical characteristics and known by its proper name.
objetos.descripcion: For example, the Alps or the Sahara.

objetos.definicion: A location that normally does not appear as a specific, characterized object but that has a name that is required to be displayed in association with that location.
objetos.descripcion: For example, the name of the Alps or the Sahara.

objetos.definicion: An organization that is responsible for planning, coordinating, and executing search and rescue services within a specified search and rescue region.
A geographically defined part of a waterbody (for example: the sea or other navigable waters).
objetos.descripcion: It may have a proper name (for example: Philippine Sea, Bismark Sea, or Coral Sea).

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which describe a designation of a Concept, for example a type or a technical designation.

objetos.definicion: A set of related resources (for example: datasets) that share common metadata (for example: theme, source date, resolution, and methodology).
objetos.descripcion: For example, a series of vector datasets, each of which depict surface hydrography with associated attribution, where a single dataset corresponds to one of the administrative areas within a country and the series corresponds to all administrative areas within that country.

contenido: This Group consists of Concepts which are metadata in the broadest sense and/or which are used as a reference to other external sources.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which are used for the annotation of a Concept.

objetos.definicion: A location at which text pertaining to that location is annotated.
objetos.descripcion: For example, a characteristic or activity pertaining to the location may be described.

objetos.definicion: A region in which multiple features having the same function are represented as one contiguous aggregate feature.
objetos.descripcion: May be used instead of identifying individual features within the region. Individual features included within the aggregate may or may not meet inclusion conditions to be delineated individually.

objetos.definicion: A location that does not appear as a specific, characterized object but with which specific information is associated.
Any feature type that falls within the scope of a feature type domain (for example: a feature coverage or a product specification) but is not explicitly specified in that domain.
objetos.descripcion: May be used to allow for the flexible capture of feature instances that are unanticipated at the time of specifying the feature type domain. This ensures that feature instances deemed important for a particular mission and/or user can be captured, even though the most appropriate feature type is not used.

objetos.definicion: A location associated with a feature where a significant characteristic of that feature changes.
objetos.descripcion: For example, the number of lanes of a road or the number of tracks of a railway.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which are used for the portrayal of a Concept.
This Subgroup consists of Concepts which are used to indicate the age and/or the up-to-dateness of Concepts like the date of extraction.

objetos.definicion: An area which is related to specific homogeneous metadata.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which are used to describe the quality of Concepts, like the quality of a position.

objetos.definicion: An area which is related to specific homogeneous metadata.
A data collection region lacking suitable source coverage and/or where data is not required.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which are used to describe a relation to an external source like other databases or special publications.

objetos.definicion: An area which is related to specific homogeneous metadata.
A set of related resources (for example: datasets) that share common metadata (for example: theme, source date, resolution, and methodology).
objetos.descripcion: For example, a series of vector datasets, each of which depict surface hydrography with associated attribution, where a single dataset corresponds to one of the administrative areas within a country and the series corresponds to all administrative areas within that country.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which are used to indicate a special classification of a Concept.
subcategorias.descripcion: This varies from military classifications such as 'Top Secret' to commercial restrictions such as copyrights.

objetos.definicion: An area which is related to specific homogeneous metadata.

contenido: This Group consists of Concepts which are used to model information regarding features, either as types or sets, but would not themselves represent features.
descripcion: For example, collecting geometric representation information about a feature type or collecting feature characteristics that may be shared by many different feature types.

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which are used to model information regarding feature types but would not themselves represent features.
subcategorias.descripcion: For example, pavement characteristics shared by many types of land transportation routes, or data quality characteristics shared by all inland water bodies.

objetos.definicion: An abstract modeling entity that is a superclass for actor types, which are representations of intentional (that is, purposeful) entities that act or have the capability of acting as a participant in an event.
objetos.descripcion: An actor may control resources or direct activity, and may do so by holding an organizational role. Actor entities include persons, social groups, organisations, and, in some contexts, automata. Collective actors (for example: organizations) may have a distributed rather than a point location.

objetos.definicion: A modeling entity collecting information about designations (for example: standardized names or codes) for a subordinate administrative division (for example: a (US) state, a (UK) county, a (US) township, a (CA) province, a (FR) arrondissement, a (CH) canton, a (GE) laender and a (FR) commune) of a geopolitical entity (for example: a State).
A modeling entity collecting information for areas designed for either the movement or the parking of aircraft and that are not reported elsewhere as aprons, hardstands, or helipads.
A modeling entity collecting information about aircraft pavements at aerodromes and heliports.
objetos.descripcion: For example, for runways, taxiways, aprons, and helipads.

objetos.definicion: A modeling entity collecting information (for example: its method of formation, its access orientation, its cultural significance) about a cave.

A modeling entity collecting information about the exploitation of vegetal and animal natural resources, including the activities of growing crops, raising animals, harvesting timber, and harvesting other plants, animals or animal products from a farm or their natural habitats.
objetos.descripcion: For example, the type of crop, the method of planting and the method of irrigation (if any).

objetos.definicion: A modeling entity collecting geometric representation information about a feature that is modeled as a spatial curve.
objetos.descripcion: A spatial curve is a 1-dimensional geometric primitive, representing the continuous image of a line.

objetos.definicion: An abstract modeling entity that is a superclass for modeling entities having identity and that represents common properties (attributes and association roles) of its subclasses.
objetos.descripcion: Identity enables the ability to reference entity instances from other modeling entities. Common properties may include entity-related metadata, notes, and/or data-dissemination restriction(s) and security control(s) regarding the entity.

objetos.definicion: A resource that collects instances of one or more modeling entities according to a common rationale (for example: based on a theme or spatial region).
objetos.descripcion: A transportation or drainage network are examples of thematically organized collections; a tessellation of the surface of a continent is an example of a spatially organized collection.

objetos.definicion: An abstract modeling entity that is a superclass for event types, which are representations of instantaneous or short-duration real-world phenomena, including their geometric position and extent.
objetos.descripcion: An event may be considered as a temporally transient feature, where the degree of transience distinguishing an 'event' from a 'feature' may be context-dependent.

objetos.definicion: A modeling entity collecting assurance information about the quality of the digital representation of a Geospatial Intelligence (GEOINT) feature attribute.
objetos.descripcion: For example, the currency of the information known about a feature attribute or the degree to which the attribute value is accurately and/or completely determined.

objetos.definicion: An abstract modeling entity that is a superclass for feature types, which are representations of temporally persistent real-world phenomena, including their geometric position and extent.
objetos.descripcion: The concept of a 'feature' is that of the ISO 19100-series standards and as such is not constrained to any specific representation; for example, surface representation such as grids and images are allowed in addition to vector representations.

objetos.definicion: A modeling entity collecting assurance information about the quality of the digital representation of a Geospatial Intelligence (GEOINT) feature and its properties (attributes and associations).
objetos.descripcion: For example, the currency of the information known about a feature or the degree to which the properties of a feature are accurately and/or completely determined.

objetos.definicion: An abstract modeling entity serving as a superclass that collects shared properties (attributes and associations) of modeling entities that specify geometric representation information about a feature.
objetos.descripcion: For example, the horizontal and/or vertical metadata, notes, and/or restriction(s) and/or security control(s) applicable to dissemination of data regarding the geometric representation of the feature.

objetos.definicion: A modeling entity collecting information about designations (for example: standardized names or codes) for a geopolitical entity (for example: a State).

A modeling entity collecting information about the basis for, and quality of, the horizontal coordinates and/or horizontal dimensional measures of the digital representation of a feature and/or attribute.
objetos.descripcion: For example, the spatial reference frame for a horizontal position or the accuracy of that position value.

objetos.definicion: A modeling entity collecting information about the vertical position (for example: the depth from a sounding datum) of a hydrographic object (for example: a pinnacle or a wreck).
A modeling entity collecting information about an identifier that is used to uniquely specify an instance of the entity type in a specified scope.
objetos.descripcion: The scope may be determined by the intended use and/or the data production system that assigns the identifier value.

objetos.definicion: An abstract modeling entity that is a superclass for information types, which are collections of non-geometric properties of other entity types (for example: features, actors, or events) that may be shared by multiple entity types within the model, and their values reused within datasets.
objetos.descripcion: Shared information may include entity-related metadata, notes, and/or data-dissemination restriction(s) and security control(s) regarding the associated entity.

objetos.definicion: A modeling entity collecting information about the physical or chemical transformation of materials, substances, or components into new products.
objetos.descripcion: The materials, substances, or components transformed are raw materials that are products of agriculture, forestry, fishing, mining or quarrying as well as products of other manufacturing activities. Substantial alteration, renovation or reconstruction of goods is generally considered to be manufacturing.

objetos.definicion: A modeling entity collecting unstructured information about the feature, attribute, or related information modeling entity.
A modeling entity collecting geometric representation information about a feature that is modeled as a spatial point.
objetos.descripcion: A spatial point is a 0-dimensional geometric primitive, representing a position.

objetos.definicion: A modeling entity collecting information about the processing activity(ies) that were used to define, review and/or update the digital representation of a feature and/or attribute.
A modeling entity collecting information (for example: its shape and material) about a pylon.
A modeling entity collecting information about the religious significance and/or characteristics of features.
A modeling entity collecting information about restriction(s) and/or security control(s) applicable to dissemination of data regarding the digital representation of the feature or attribute.
A modeling entity collecting information about a route pavement, a durable surface for an area intended to sustain traffic (for example: vehicular traffic or foot traffic).
objetos.descripcion: Paved surfaces may be used in a variety of traffic situations (for example: on a floor, in a courtyard, or on a road) and is generally composed of pieces of a hard material fitted closely together or of an undivided hard coating so as to give a compact, uniform, and smooth surface. In the past, brick was extensively used, as was metalling. Today, permeable paving methods are beginning to be used more for low-impact roadways and walkways. Metalling originally referred to the process of creating a carefully-engineered gravel roadway. The route of the roadway first would be dug down several feet. Depending on local conditions, French drains may or may not have been added. Next, large stone was placed and compacted, followed by successive layers of smaller stone, until the road surface was a small stone compacted into a hard, durable surface. 'Road metal' later became the name of stone chippings mixed with tar to form the road surfacing material termed 'tarmac'. A road of such material is called a 'metalled road' in British usage, and is still a common modern usage. (The word metal is derived from the Latin metallum, which means both 'mine' and 'quarry', hence the road building terminology.)

objetos.definicion: A modeling entity collecting information about the basis for, and quality of, coordinates and/or dimensional measures of the digital representation of a feature and/or attribute related to a hydrographic sounding datum.
objetos.descripcion: For example, the sounding datum with respect to which a vertical position or dimension has been determined, or the accuracy of that position or dimension value.

objetos.definicion: A modeling entity collecting information about the source data that was used to define, review and/or update the digital representation of a feature and/or attribute.
A modeling entity collecting geometric representation information about a feature that is modeled as a spatial surface.
objetos.descripcion: A spatial surface is a 2-dimensional geometric primitive, locally representing a continuous image of a region of a plane.

objetos.definicion: A modeling entity collecting information about a railway track.
objetos.descripcion: A railway track consists of (usually) two parallel rails, usually of steel, generally mounted upon cross beams (termed 'railroad ties' (US) or 'sleepers' (UK) ) of timber, concrete or steel. The underlying support maintains the rails at a fixed distance (gauge) apart. Usually vehicles running on the rails are arranged in a train (a series of individual powered or unpowered vehicles linked together). In the case of a monorail, only a single rail is employed and the vehicles may be either suspended underneath or straddle an especially wide rail.

objetos.definicion: A modeling entity collecting information about the basis for, and quality of, the vertical coordinates and/or vertical dimensional measures of the digital representation of a feature and/or attribute.
objetos.descripcion: For example, the spatial reference frame for a vertical position or the accuracy of that position value.

objetos.definicion: A modeling entity collecting information (for example: its permanence, mineral content and potability) about a water resource.
A modeling entity collecting information about a wireless telecommunication service (for example: radio broadcast or digital mobile phone service).

subcategorias.contenido: This Subgroup consists of Concepts which are used to model information regarding sets of feature instances.
subcategorias.descripcion: For example, a route network, a chart, or a map series.

objetos.definicion: A resource that is a set of instances of one or more modeling entities selected according to a single rationale (for example: a common production or publication process).
objetos.descripcion: For example, a set of modeling entities whose instances together constitute a 'water resources map'.
